suggestion.title: Public-only token attempting private repository access via public API route
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the attack: 'public-only,write:repository token to update a private pull request head branch through a public base repository route.' This is the authorization bypass signature — token scope restriction is checked against wrong repository context. Pipeline missed token-scope validation entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for API tokens authenticated with 'public-only' or limited-scope claims successfully accessing private repositories or private PR branches. In Gitea audit logs, look for authorization checks performed against public repository context but resulting modifications to private repository branches. Cross-reference token issuer scope vs. actual resource accessed.

suggestion.title: Authorization context mismatch — /api/v1/repos/{public-repo}/pulls/{index}/update modifying private PR
suggestion.rationale: Article core mechanic: 'checks the token's public-only restriction against the route repository, which is the public base repository. UpdatePullRequest() then authorizes the pull re[quest against the private PR destination].' Detection must capture requests to public repo endpoints that cascade authorization failures down to private resources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal repository boundaries: which accounts/tokens update which repositories. Flag requests where the route repository (public) differs from the target repository (private) after PR traversal. If Gitea exposes authorization check logs, alert on authorization decisions made on wrong repository object.

suggestion.title: Anomalous actor updating pull request branch metadata
suggestion.rationale: PR branch updates are typically initiated by repo owners, PR authors, or CI systems. Attack would originate from an unexpected user/token pair with insufficient default privileges. Baseline legitimate PR update actors to detect outliers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build baseline of legitimate PR-update initiators per repository (usually PR author, CI/CD service accounts, repo admins). Alert on requests from users/tokens outside this baseline, particularly if they carry limited-scope tokens (public-only) attempting updates to private repositories.

suggestion.title: Cross-repository artifact access (same HMAC, different repoID)
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'can turn a signed URL for an attacker-controlled artifact into a URL that reads artifacts from another task context'—specifically mentioning cross-repository access. UC_3_2 detects same-sig-different-taskID but doesn't flag repository boundary crossing, the exploit's defining characteristic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Same HMAC signature appears in requests to ArtifactService endpoints with different repoID parameters. This indicates attacker rewrote the URL to escape their repository context while preserving the signature.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized artifact download by principal
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'reads artifacts from another task context'—attacker exfiltrates data. Need detection for: principal downloading artifacts from repositories not in their RBAC grant, or from task contexts they did not create.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Principal requests DownloadArtifact for repoID/taskID pair where they have no create/read permission (cross-reference against RBAC policy). Combine with UC_3_2 (HMAC replay) to flag high-confidence exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Artifact upload state write to unauthorized task
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can perform 'cross-task upload-state write'—modification of another task's artifact metadata or state. Detection for: principal writing to UploadArtifact endpoint for taskID they do not own.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: UploadArtifact requests (PUT/POST) from principal for taskID not matching their own job context. Cross-reference job ownership logs to identify state writes to foreign tasks.

suggestion.title: HMAC validation bypass or signature omission
suggestion.rationale: Core technical vulnerability is HMAC ambiguity. Detection should flag: missing sig parameter, invalid/expired signatures, or direct requests to artifact endpoints lacking signatures entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Requests to */ArtifactService/* endpoints lacking the sig query parameter, or sig values that fail HMAC validation. Flag as attempted signature bypass.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation: single-task access to multi-repository artifact reads
suggestion.rationale: Attacker with permission to run ONE job gains access to artifacts across multiple repositories (lateral privilege escalation). Detection for: single source spawning artifact requests across N unrelated repositories within short window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Single job principal triggers DownloadArtifact across 3+ distinct repositories not listed in job dependencies/permissions within 60 seconds. Suggests URL crafting to escape intended scope.

suggestion.title: X-WEBAUTH-USER header injection from untrusted source IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'any source IP impersonate any user via `X-WEBAUTH-USER`' — direct header injection is the core attack. Neither existing UC detects the header itself in HTTP requests from non-trusted sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor reverse proxy and web server logs for requests containing X-WEBAUTH-USER headers originating from IP addresses outside the configured trusted proxy list (anything other than loopback). Flag any requests where the source IP does not match the reverse proxy IP and X-WEBAUTH-USER is set, indicating direct injection by a client.

suggestion.title: Gitea authentication event source IP mismatch with X-WEBAUTH-USER
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impersonation via injected headers. Detection should look for login events where the authenticated user (via X-WEBAUTH-USER) does not match the source IP of the reverse proxy or contains mismatched geolocation/ASN data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Gitea authentication logs with reverse proxy logs. Flag login events where X-WEBAUTH-USER value does not match expected pattern or where source IP is unexpected for the authenticated user. High-risk indicator: same X-WEBAUTH-USER from multiple distinct IPs within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: REVERSE_PROXY_TRUSTED_PROXIES misconfiguration exposure via app.ini
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes insecure default: 'Gitea Docker images ship an `app.ini` template that hard-codes: `REVERSE_PROXY_TRUSTED_PROXIES = *`'. Configuration disclosure is recon/discovery indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests attempting to access or enumerate Gitea configuration files (app.ini, custom/conf/app.ini) or responses that leak configuration contents. Detect via 200 responses with config file content, directory listing responses, or configuration parsing errors that reveal REVERSE_PROXY_TRUSTED_PROXIES settings.

suggestion.title: ENABLE_REVERSE_PROXY_AUTHENTICATION state changes in Gitea
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'When an admin enables `ENABLE_REVERSE_PROXY_AUTHENTICATION = true`' — this setting change initiates the vulnerability window and should trigger alert when combined with REVERSE_PROXY_TRUSTED_PROXIES = *.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when ENABLE_REVERSE_PROXY_AUTHENTICATION is set to true or modified. Higher-risk: correlate with REVERSE_PROXY_TRUSTED_PROXIES = * setting in same config. Audit admin actions preceding this change.

suggestion.title: Gitea token hash mismatch followed by authenticated action (session persistence exploit)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'when handling a compromised token (hash mismatch)...the attacker's session is NOT invalidated.' This is the core attack—hash validation fails but session survives. Requires correlation of failure event with successful action, not isolated detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: User account logs ErrAuthTokenInvalidHash for gitea_incredible cookie, then within 5 minutes performs an authenticated action (POST to repo endpoint, API call with valid session, file push/pull) from the same source IP. Indicates vulnerability exploited: token detected as compromised but session remains valid.

suggestion.title: Gitea remember-me token hash error from multiple source IPs (distributed token replay)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes stolen token, but if hash-mismatch errors appear for one user from 3+ distinct IPs in 30 min, suggests token theft + distribution or attacker controlling multiple compromised endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Single Gitea user account receives ErrAuthTokenInvalidHash errors originating from 3+ unique source IPs within 30 minutes. Indicates token shared/replayed across attacker infrastructure or token database leaked (allowing multiple IPs to forge the same hash).

suggestion.title: Gitea account privilege escalation or credential modification post-token-theft
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1098.001 (Account Manipulation: Additional Cloud Credentials). Attacker with hijacked session may add SSH keys, create API tokens, alter email, or disable 2FA. These are post-compromise persistence steps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After an ErrAuthTokenInvalidHash event from an IP, the user account sees sensitive modifications: new SSH public key, new API token generation, email change, password reset, or 2FA disablement. Timeline correlation proves attacker used hijacked session to establish persistence.

suggestion.title: Gitea autoSignIn abuse on unauthenticated or dormant-user endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article names vulnerable code path: 'any endpoint triggering autoSignIn via the Remember-Me cookie.' Detection should catch autoSignIn activation on unexpected endpoints or from dormant accounts, indicating token reuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Request to authenticated endpoint includes valid gitea_incredible cookie but user account had no login activity in past 7 days, or autoSignIn triggered on endpoint that normally requires explicit authentication. Combined with public-facing app scans (T1190), suggests attacker reusing stolen session across multiple targets.

suggestion.title: Gitea /user/login endpoint scanning for token-validation bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable endpoint: POST /user/login and vulnerable function path in services/auth/auth_token.go. Attackers will scan/fuzz this endpoint to trigger hash-mismatch conditions and test session persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Repeated POST requests to /user/login with malformed, expired, or tampered gitea_incredible cookie values from single IP. Look for rapid retry patterns (>5 attempts in 60 sec), scanner User-Agents, or known exploit-kit signatures. Early indicator of active CVE-2026-56750 probing.

suggestion.title: Gitea concurrent session validation bypass (attacker and legitimate user same account)
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: attacker's stolen session and legitimate user's session both remain valid despite token failure. Look for conflicting authentication states: token error + valid session + different behaviors (geographic impossible travel, agent mismatch).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: User account shows simultaneous valid sessions from two distinct IPs with >1000 km geographic distance and <5 min time delta, AND one of the IPs previously triggered ErrAuthTokenInvalidHash. Indicates session non-invalidation vulnerability: attacker's stolen session coexists with legitimate session despite detection of token compromise.

suggestion.title: SharePoint /_trust/default.aspx RCE via Malicious BinaryFormatter
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'malicious .NET BinaryFormatter payload as the cookie of a forged SecurityContextToken within a WS-Federation sign-in response posted to SharePoint's /_trust/default.aspx endpoint' — this is the core exploitation vector and must be detected before execution succeeds
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST requests to /_trust/default.aspx with SecurityContextToken cookie containing serialized .NET BinaryFormatter content (detectable by magic bytes or token patterns). Correlate with unexpected process spawns from w3wp.exe or SharePoint worker processes within seconds of the request.

suggestion.title: Machine Key File Access and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'started to leverage CVE-2026-50522 against on-premise vulnerable SharePoint deployments' and 'stealing machine keys that allow them to maintain long-term access on breached systems' — machine key theft is the persistence mechanism and must be detected
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor reads of machine.key files and web.config files in SharePoint directories (%ProgramFiles%\Microsoft Shared\Web Server Extensions\*) by non-SYSTEM processes. Flag file reads immediately following /_trust/default.aspx exploitation attempts or by unusual process contexts (cmd.exe, PowerShell spawned from IIS).

suggestion.title: Forged Authentication Token Usage Post-Patch
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'maintain access even after affected servers are patched' and 'create valid authentication tokens to impersonate users and access available resources' — attackers bypass patches via credential abuse, requiring persistence detection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication token claims (via Kerberos, SAML, or SharePoint session cookies) that reference stolen machine key signatures and appear after known exploitation windows. Correlate forged tokens with impossible travel patterns or access to resources inconsistent with the impersonated user's baseline behavior.

suggestion.title: Deserialization Attack Pattern in SharePoint Worker Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article classifies vulnerability as 'deserialization-of-untrusted-data flaw' — deserial attacks are a known execution vector and must be detectable at runtime
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .NET runtime deserialization calls (System.Runtime.Serialization namespace) in w3wp.exe and SharePoint processes, particularly BinaryFormatter.Deserialize() on untrusted streams. Flag deserialization attempts on data sourced from HTTP request bodies, cookies, or WS-Federation protocol messages.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated WS-Federation Request to Trust Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article notes flaw 'allows a remote attacker to execute code over a network without authentication' specifically via WS-Federation mechanism — unauthenticated sign-in attempts are baseline detectable
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthenticated POST requests to /_trust/default.aspx containing WS-Federation markers (wctx, wresult, SecurityContextToken parameters). Baseline expected sign-in traffic and flag anomalies in source IPs, payload sizes, or token structure deviations.

suggestion.title: Public PoC Exploitation Pattern Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Within hours, our global honeypot network, Attacker Eye, captured exploitation attempts using this PoC that successfully compromised target systems' — the Janggggg GitHub PoC has identifiable structural signatures suitable for detection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Develop YARA-like signatures for the published PowerShell PoC structure (SecurityContextToken cookie construction, malicious BinaryFormatter payload patterns). Match HTTP requests to /_trust/default.aspx against PoC-indicative patterns: specific cookie value lengths, parameter ordering, payload entropy characteristics.

suggestion.title: Docker config file access by build-context processes during credential confusion window
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes `getRegistryCredentials()` reading from `~/.docker/config.json` with substring-matching logic. No detection covers defensive access monitoring of this file during abnormal registry connections. Article states: 'selects an entry by checking whether any configured auth key **contains** the target registry string.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes matching node/build tools (npm, yarn, docker, sigstore, etc.) accessing ~/.docker/config.json immediately prior to or concurrent with connections to non-canonical OCI registries. Substring-matching confusion often manifests as rapid sequential auth attempts to different registry variants (e.g., registry.example.com vs attacker-registry.io both matching 'registry' substring).

suggestion.title: Lateral movement via credential confusion — compromised build host propagating to downstream registries
suggestion.rationale: Article does not detail post-exploitation behavior but describes how leaked credentials can be used against legitimate registries. Missing detection for attacker using stolen credentials to push malicious images. Article mentions exfiltration technique T1048 but no detection for the re-use phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node/build processes using stolen registry credentials (extracted from docker config) to authenticate to legitimate registries (docker.io, ghcr.io, etc.) from non-canonical source IPs or at unusual times outside normal CI/CD windows. Cross-reference successful auth to legitimate registries with prior access to suspicious registries.

suggestion.title: Supply-chain pivot — @sigstore/oci dependency injection in transitive build dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Article classifies as T1195.001 (Supply Chain Compromise) but no UC detects when @sigstore/oci is installed transitively (not directly in package.json) or when other packages depend on vulnerable version. Article body notes package version <=0.7.0 but lacks detection for hidden transitive deps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager operations (npm audit, yarn list, pip show) on build hosts for @sigstore/oci in nested dependency trees where the direct parent is a less-scrutinized supply-chain tool (attestation libraries, provenance generators, SBOM tools). Flag if the vulnerable package is in a transitive dependency that developers may not expect.

suggestion.title: Defensive — registry auth credential validity check and substring-match sanitization
suggestion.rationale: Article root cause: substring matching in credential selection. No detection for misconfiguration or policy bypass. Organizations should detect/alert on docker-config entries where overlapping substrings exist (e.g., 'registry.example.com' and 'example.com' both present), which enables the confusion attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Periodically parse ~/.docker/config.json on build/CI hosts and detect entries with dangerous substring overlaps (e.g., one auth key is a substring of another, or matches multiple registries). Alert on configurations that create ambiguity in credential selection logic. Also detect if docker login/config manipulation commands are run without corresponding legitimate image pull operations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 UPnP Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP' — exploit attempts must be detected before payload execution
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for malformed or abnormal UPnP traffic targeting DD-WRT devices on ports 1900/UDP and associated high-numbered TCP ports. Flag payloads matching known CVE-2021-27137 exploit signatures or exhibiting buffer-overflow patterns (oversized/crafted input fields). Cross-correlate with asset inventory to isolate exposed DD-WRT nodes.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Asset Exposure and Patch Status Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'public-facing application' vulnerability and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' with federal due date 2026-07-24 — exposure + patch status is core compliance hunt
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all DD-WRT devices accessible from untrusted networks; flag those with unpatched CVE-2021-27137 status. Validate scanner detection consistency; investigate false negatives. Track patch deployment and post-remediation re-scan confirmation against federal deadline.

suggestion.title: UPnP Service Crashes or Anomalous Restarts
suggestion.rationale: Buffer overflow 'could allow code execution' — exploitation often triggers daemon segfaults, crashes, or unexpected service restarts on vulnerable UPnP services
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT device logs for abnormal UPnP daemon terminations, segmentation faults, or service restarts. Flag repeated crashes on same device within hours, especially if preceded by network anomalies or unusual traffic patterns.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution from UPnP Context
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms 'code execution vulnerability' — successful RCE spawns processes or establishes C2 channels executing with UPnP service privileges
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual shell invocations, process spawning, or outbound network connections originating from UPnP service user/daemon context on DD-WRT. Flag reverse shells, packet-grabbers (tcpdump), wget/curl downloads, or lateral movement reconnaissance commands running with UPnP privileges.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Exploit Payload Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'stack-based buffer overflow' with known CVE identifier — signature-based detection on network and endpoint logging should complement vulnerability scanning
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy or update network IDS/WAF signatures for CVE-2021-27137 exploitation attempts. Monitor UPnP ports for payloads exceeding expected buffer sizes, control flow hijack patterns, or known public exploit artifacts (e.g., Metasploit module indicators if publicly released).

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Scanner Match – DD-WRT Buffer Overflow
suggestion.rationale: Article is a CISA KEV entry, the federal baseline for active exploitation. Pipeline must surface vulnerability-scanner detections immediately. 'CVE-2021-27137' is the scannable identifier; any vuln-scan hit requires urgent triage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vulnerability scanner reports for any hosts returning CVSS CRIT matches against CVE-2021-27137. Cross-check affected asset inventory against patch deployment records. Given federal due-date 2026-07-24, any unpatched DD-WRT appliance is priority-1.

suggestion.title: UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article names UPnP as the attack surface: 'unauthenticated attacker to overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP.' Network-based detection for malformed UPnP payloads or oversized buffers is essential for zero-day or pre-patch windows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal UPnP traffic patterns on internal networks and DMZ. Alert on abnormal packet sizes, malformed UPnP protocol structures, or repeated failed UPnP handshakes indicative of buffer-overflow fuzzing. Correlate with DD-WRT appliances (identify by MAC, hostname, or geoip).

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Post-Exploitation Code Execution Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow... code execution.' After successful buffer-overflow exploitation, attackers gain unauthenticated RCE on the appliance. Look for unexpected child processes, outbound connections, or privilege escalation on compromised DD-WRT devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT syslog or remote-logging endpoints for unexpected process creation (e.g., shells, reverse shells, curl/wget downloads). Alert on outbound connections from DD-WRT LAN IP ranges to external C2 infrastructure. Establish baseline for dd-wrt cron jobs and scheduled tasks; anomalies post-patch-due-date are high-signal.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Device Reboot / Crash Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Stack-based buffer overflows frequently cause application or kernel-level crashes before successful exploitation. Sudden reboot cycles or service crashes on DD-WRT devices prior to patching may indicate exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DD-WRT devices logging unexpected reboot cycles, UPnP daemon crashes, or kernel panics in the 48 hours before patch due-date (2026-07-24). Cross-correlate with network telemetry to detect incoming exploit traffic preceding crashes.

suggestion.title: Unpatched DD-WRT Inventory – Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requires immediate remediation by federal due-date. Standard asset-exposure hunt: identify all DD-WRT devices across your enterprise and confirm patch status against CVE-2021-27137 by 2026-07-24.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query CMDB/asset management for all DD-WRT appliances (routers, firewalls, access points). Cross-check against patch-management system or SSH-fingerprinting of installed firmware versions. Generate list of non-compliant assets and assign remediation tickets with priority escalation prior to 2026-07-24.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT CVE-2021-27137 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2021-27137 affecting DD-WRT and describes 'unauthenticated attacker' exploitation of exposed devices. CISA KEV status implies active wild exploitation. Article even references template guidance for asset-exposure hunts but pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory DD-WRT instances via UPnP SSDP fingerprinting or web UI detection; cross-reference against patch-status records for CVE-2021-27137. Prioritize externally-routable devices or those accessible from untrusted VLANs.

suggestion.title: UPnP Service Crash or Memory Corruption Signals
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'stack-based buffer overflow...in UPnP' as the exploitation method. No use case captures process crashes, memory-access violations, or core dumps from UPnP daemon that would indicate active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UPnP service processes for abnormal termination (SIGSEGV, abort), memory exhaustion, or repeated restart cycles. Stack-overflow exploits frequently leave crash artifacts in kernel logs or application event logs.

suggestion.title: Malformed UPnP Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is 'overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP.' No network-based use case for detecting oversized, malformed, or malicious UPnP protocol messages (NOTIFY, M-SEARCH, SOAP) that would trigger buffer-overflow conditions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag UPnP HTTP requests with Content-Length headers exceeding normal service thresholds, or SOAP/XML payloads with excessive nesting or encoding anomalies. Exploitation typically requires crafted payloads that overflow stack buffers.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Spawn from UPnP Service
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability 'could allow...unauthenticated attacker to...trigger a code execution.' Article offers no post-exploitation hunting; pipeline generated nothing. Code execution from buffer overflow manifests as child processes or shells spawned in UPnP service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any child process spawned by UPnP daemon (upnpd, miniupnpd) or reverse-shell callbacks initiated from UPnP process context. Attacker code running in UPnP privilege level often spawns shells for persistence or lateral movement.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 asset exposure hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [`../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`]' and calls out patch lag as 'the silent killer.' Pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for CVE-2021-27137 in vulnerability scanner results across all DD-WRT devices. Correlate with missing or stale patch dates. Cross-reference with external asset inventory to identify exposed instances; federal due-date of 2026-07-24 provides a hard compliance checkpoint.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated UPnP buffer overflow exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated attacker to overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP and trigger a code execution vulnerability' — this is the core attack vector but no UC was generated to detect UPnP-based buffer overflow attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for malformed UPnP requests (port 1900 UDP, SSDP protocol) exceeding typical buffer sizes. Flag unusual process spawning or shell escapes originating from UPnP daemons (e.g., miniupnpd, upnpd). Baseline normal UPnP traffic to detect injection-style payloads.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT device configuration post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article's RCE via buffer overflow would grant attacker ability to modify device state, but no UC detects suspicious configuration changes post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT config backups and syslog for unexpected modifications to firewall rules, user accounts, or service enablement (SSH, Telnet, HTTP auth) immediately following network-detectable exploitation attempts or time-cluster with CVE-2021-27137 scanner events.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'match against your vulnerability scanner' for CVE-2021-27137. Pipeline failed to generate detection UC for this core indicator despite article guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when vulnerability scanner detects CVE-2021-27137 on DD-WRT instances. Correlate scan date (post 2026-07-21) against federal patch due date (2026-07-24) to prioritize unpatched systems requiring immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: Exposed DD-WRT UPnP Service Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability affects 'internal buffer used by UPnP' and requires unauthenticated access — indicating exposed UPnP service on network perimeter. No UC for asset exposure hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound UPnP traffic (port 1900/UDP, SSDP protocol) from external sources targeting DD-WRT devices. Flag exposed instances, prioritize those failing CVE-2021-27137 scanner checks.

suggestion.title: UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'stack-based buffer overflow' via UPnP service as exploitation vector. No UC generated for detecting malformed/oversized UPnP payloads targeting the vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal UPnP traffic: packets exceeding standard SSDP message size, malformed XML in device descriptions, or rapid repeated exploitation attempts to port 1900. Correlate with unexpected process spawning or crashes on vulnerable DD-WRT instances.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution on DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article states overflow 'trigger a code execution vulnerability.' Pipeline missed detection UC for command execution indicators following successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected shell spawning, command execution, or binary invocation on DD-WRT devices following external UPnP service interaction. Flag reverse-shell patterns, persistence mechanisms, or outbound C2 connections.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2021-27137 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and is CISA KEV (active exploitation). Zero scanner-based detection rule was generated despite clear directive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and CMDB for assets reporting CVE-2021-27137 or DD-WRT firmware versions matching CVSS 9.8+ criteria. Prioritize externally-facing devices. Cross-reference against patch timeline (due 2026-07-24).

suggestion.title: UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability...in UPnP' and 'unauthenticated attacker can overflow an internal buffer.' UPnP port (1900/udp) activity is the exploitation surface but generated no detection rule.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UPnP multicast (239.255.255.250:1900/udp) and unicast responses for suspicious payloads, oversized M-SEARCH requests, or malformed SOAP/XML that trigger segfaults. Baseline normal UPnP chatter and alert on anomalies from internal DD-WRT devices.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Asset Inventory and Exposure Validation
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies 'observed exploited in the wild' against exposed assets. Article recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' but pipeline generated zero inventory or discovery use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query firewall/network logs for web traffic to standard DD-WRT admin ports (80/tcp, 443/tcp, 8443/tcp) from external sources. Cross-check User-Agent and HTTP headers for DD-WRT signatures or typical UPnP device discovery patterns. Correlate with CMDB for devices claiming to run DD-WRT firmware.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution Forensics
suggestion.rationale: Article describes outcome as 'trigger a code execution vulnerability' but no detection for post-compromise indicators (shell spawning, persistence, outbound C2) was generated despite clear execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For compromised DD-WRT instances, monitor for unexpected shell processes (sh, bash) spawned by UPnP daemons, outbound connections from device to external C2 infrastructure, or file modifications in web-accessible directories (/www, /etc) after timestamps correlating with exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Release tags reassigned to non-branch commits in popular Actions
suggestion.rationale: Article core mechanic: 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit, which was the orphaned commit. The attacker re-pointed several existing release tags to their malicious commit.' Explicit obfuscation tactic enabling supply-chain poisoning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when release tags on high-dependency repositories (>1000 direct references in GitHub Actions workflows) are repointed to commits not reachable from any active branch. Cross-reference tag metadata timestamps to detect retroactive updates. Priority: tags on Actions with >10k dependent repos.

suggestion.title: Secrets plaintext exposure in GitHub Actions logs
suggestion.rationale: Primary attack outcome stated explicitly: 'encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs.' This could lead to 'devastating breach on a public repo where the Action logs are also public.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions workflow logs for high-entropy strings matching credential patterns (base64-encoded 32+ char strings, AWS key prefixes, JWT structures, API tokens). Correlate against repository secrets configuration. Alert on first plaintext occurrence + count affected workflows. Track which Actions injected secrets into logs.

suggestion.title: Supply-chain compromise: write-access abuse in popular GitHub Actions
suggestion.rationale: Root attack vector: 'a malicious actor had write access to a repo that 23,000 other repos relied on.' Unknown how access was obtained but it enabled commit injection + tag manipulation at scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag commits in top-100 GitHub Actions (by downstream usage) that: originate from new/unusual committer identities, add external network calls or credential-access code, are not integrated into main branch, yet are deployed via release tag. Baseline normal commit patterns; alert on deviations + infrastructure changes.

suggestion.title: Orphaned commits in public GitHub repositories
