Monitor for DNS queries from IoT hosts to high-entropy or algorithmically-generated domains. Flag successful connections on non-standard ports (8080, 443 from embedded device context).

suggestion.title: IoT SSH/Telnet Brute-Force and Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Initial Access phase not reconstructed. IoT botnets universally attack via weak credentials and unpatched remote services on ports 22, 23, 8080. Must be detectable at network egress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated failed SSH/Telnet login attempts from external sources to IoT device IP ranges. Alert on successful login from non-approved administrative sources. Correlate successful SSH access with subsequent process execution and network callbacks on same host.

suggestion.title: LLM-Generated Payload Execution via Scripting
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically flags 'LLM-Assisted' malware development as novel threat. Pipeline missed Execution and Defense Evasion phases. LLM-generated code may exhibit unusual entropy, imports, or obfuscation signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bash/sh process spawning from /tmp, /var, or world-writable paths on Linux IoT devices. Alert on curl/wget downloading and piping to shell. Monitor for code obfuscation indicators (base64 decoding in scripts, XOR loops) consistent with LLM-generated evasion.

suggestion.title: Cron/Init Persistence Mechanisms on Compromised IoT
suggestion.rationale: Botnet 'evolution' implies active persistence and upgrade capability. Persistence phase entirely absent from reconstruction. Cron and init.d are canonical IoT foothold mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation/modification of /etc/cron.d entries, /etc/cron.daily scripts, or /etc/init.d services on IoT endpoints. Monitor rc.local and SystemV init script changes that execute network tools. Correlate cron modifications with C2 callbacks.

suggestion.title: DGA/Fast-Flux C2 Domain Resolution Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Botnet 'evolution' suggests sophisticated C2 evasion (DGA, flux). Zero C2 detection use cases created despite this being definitive botnet signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect IoT devices performing DNS queries to high volumes of unique subdomains under seed domains. Flag DNS resolution patterns where subdomains resolve to multiple IPs within short windows (fast flux). Correlate failed DNS resolutions with subsequent C2 IP-direct connections.

suggestion.title: Token scope escape: Public-only credential performing private repository writes
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'public-only,write:repository token can update a private pull request head branch'. Detection should key on token capability mismatch (public-only scope attempting private resource modification), not just endpoint pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate token scope metadata (public-only, read-only) against actual API operations. Alert when a token declared with public-only permissions successfully modifies private repository resources. Requires capturing token identity and scope in audit logs alongside the resource being accessed.

suggestion.title: Authorization check bypass: Public route used to modify private branch target
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause: 'Gitea checks token restriction against the route repository (public base), UpdatePullRequest() then accesses the private head branch' — this is the check-use-time gap; detect mismatches between authorization context and actual resource modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse POST /api/v1/repos requests to extract base repository visibility from the route. Cross-reference with the PR's head branch destination repository. Alert if the route repository is public but the head branch is in a private repository—indicates the vulnerability being exploited.

suggestion.title: Service token permission escape: Cross-repository write via public API surface
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability uses a single public-scoped token to write private resources; this is a common pattern in credential compromise or configuration error. Article states 'UpdatePullRequest() then authorizes' after route check—indicating late-stage authorization is insufficient.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for single API credentials that perform successful write operations against multiple repositories of differing visibility levels in a short window. Flag if a token is observed writing to both public and private repos, as this violates intended scope restrictions.

suggestion.title: Gitea Artifacts: Signed URL parameter reordering or injection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'signed URL can be rewritten to access a different running task and repository context while preserving the original HMAC signature.' Rewriting implies URL structure manipulation (param reordering, duplicate params, injection). No detection catches URLs with identical sig/taskID/artifactName in different orders.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Group requests by signature and taskID to detect requests where the same (sig, taskID) pair appears with differing parameter order or conflicting artifactName values. Attackers rewrite URLs to bypass intended context boundary.

suggestion.title: Gitea Artifacts: Enumeration of taskID/artifactName prior to cross-task access
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires attacker to discover valid taskID and artifactName combinations in target repos. Article implies 'attacker with permission to run a Gitea Actions job' must probe accessible artifacts. Pattern: failed/404 DownloadArtifact requests followed by successful access to different taskID.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sources with high fail-rate (HTTP 404/403) on DownloadArtifact URLs, followed within 10 minutes by HTTP 200 success on DownloadArtifact with distinct taskID from the failed attempts. Indicates enumeration → exploitation.

suggestion.title: Gitea Artifacts: Cross-repository artifact access (repo context bypass)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly cites 'cross-repository artifact read' as attack impact. Vulnerability allows accessing artifacts from repo_B while acting in repo_A context. Detection requires comparing repository/project ID in request path vs. job/runner context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If Gitea logs include repository context, flag DownloadArtifact requests where the repo in the URL/context differs from the calling job's repo. Indicates abuse of signed URL to breach repo boundary.

suggestion.title: Gitea Artifacts: Signed artifact URL used from unauthorized runner/IP
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires 'permission to run a Gitea Actions job.' Artifact downloads should originate from known CI/CD runners or authorized build agents. Access from arbitrary external IPs or non-runner accounts indicates stolen/reused signed URL.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate artifact download sources (CI runner IPs, authenticated user networks). Flag DownloadArtifact/UploadArtifact requests from untrusted IPs or outside normal CI agent subnets. Indicates signed URL theft/reuse.

suggestion.title: Gitea Artifacts: Rapid sequential artifact reads across unrelated jobs
suggestion.rationale: Cross-task exploitation allows single attacker to exfiltrate artifacts from many tasks. Rapid sequential DownloadArtifact requests across unrelated job IDs (different repos, projects, teams) from one source indicates bulk exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sources downloading artifacts from 5+ distinct taskIDs within 5 minutes. Filter out known admin/backup tools. High-confidence indicator of cross-repo data theft.

suggestion.title: Gitea Artifacts: Modified artifact content in cross-task write scenario
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'cross-task upload-state write' allowing staging manipulation. If artifact content/checksum is available in logs, a cross-task UploadArtifact write (UC_4_5) that modifies existing artifact size/hash indicates tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For same artifactName across different taskIDs in UploadArtifact requests, compare file size/hash/timestamp. Detect writes where content differs significantly from baseline, indicating integrity compromise.

suggestion.title: SharePoint /_trust/default.aspx POST with SecurityContextToken Cookie
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes exploitation vector: 'malicious .NET BinaryFormatter payload as the cookie of a forged SecurityContextToken within a WS-Federation sign-in response posted to SharePoint's /_trust/default.aspx endpoint.' Pipeline missed the only named POST endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP POST requests to /_trust/default.aspx from external sources where the Cookie header contains 'SecurityContextToken' values >8KB (BinaryFormatter payloads are verbose) or contains unexpected serialization markers. Correlate with lack of valid pre-authentication on the same session.

suggestion.title: Suspicious BinaryFormatter Deserialization Attempts on SharePoint
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation mechanism: 'deserialization-of-untrusted-data flaw' triggered by 'malicious .NET BinaryFormatter payload.' Pipeline did not surface .NET deserialization as an observable attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for CLR (.NET) processes on SharePoint servers spawning child processes or accessing unexpected modules immediately after HTTP requests to /_trust/default.aspx. Detect ObjectInputStream, BinaryFormatter, or LosFormatter use in SharePoint w3wp.exe process memory via ETW or CLR profiling logs.

suggestion.title: Machine Key Access and Exfiltration Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers are 'stealing machine keys that allow them to maintain long-term access on breached systems.' Machine keys (typically %WINDIR%\Microsoft.NET\Framework*\machineKey.xml or IIS metabase) are the persistence objective; detecting access is post-compromise validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file access or reads to %WINDIR%\Microsoft.NET\Framework*/machineKey.xml, IIS configuration files, or registry paths containing machine validation keys (HKLM\Software\Microsoft\...asp.net\). Correlate with unexpected child processes from w3wp.exe or unusual outbound traffic.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Authentication Token Generation via Compromised Machine Keys
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation impact: 'An attacker obtaining them can create valid authentication tokens to impersonate users and access available resources.' Pipeline missed detection of token creation outside normal authentication flows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication tokens generated with unusual or impossible cryptographic properties (validated against known machine key material) or tokens created outside normal IIS/ADFS token issuance paths. Look for tokens with extended validity or escalated claims issued from non-standard processes.

suggestion.title: Credential Impersonation via Forged SecurityContextToken
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector involves forging SecurityContextToken within WS-Federation response. Article states goal is 'impersonate users and access available resources.' Forged token use is a key behavioral indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful authentications to SharePoint where the authentication path (token issuer, creation timestamp, cryptographic signature validation) does not match expected ADFS/IIS patterns, especially when paired with unusual user-agent strings or geographic anomalies in login source.

suggestion.title: WS-Federation SignIn Response Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation delivers 'malicious .NET BinaryFormatter payload...within a WS-Federation sign-in response.' Pipeline missed this as a network-observable attack pattern (HTTP response tampering or injection).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP responses from /_trust/default.aspx for Response Content-Length anomalies (payloads significantly larger than typical WS-Federation responses), unusual Content-Type handling, or the presence of binary/serialized data in XML-expected response fields. Correlate with failed or unusual SAML/WS-Fed token validation.

suggestion.title: Vitest Browser Mode provider command invoked with path traversal patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'commands accept a file path from the browser and act on it without checking the allowWrite permission gate and without confining the path'. Pipeline missed detection for the actual exploitation—malicious paths like `../../../windows/system32/config/sam` sent to screenshot/trace commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for vitest provider command execution (takeScreenshot, saveTrace, uploadFile, compareScreenshots) with arguments containing path-traversal sequences (../ or ..\ patterns). Correlate with file writes outside project root to sensitive system directories.

suggestion.title: Test file modification introducing hardcoded system paths for vitest provider commands
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability can be exploited 'via malicious test code' invoking provider commands. Pipeline missed detection of test file injection or suspicious test modifications with hardcoded paths to system resources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for modifications to .test.ts/.test.js files or vitest config files that add calls to browser provider commands with paths pointing to Windows system directories, sensitive data folders, or absolute paths outside the project root.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration via vitest screenshot/trace files containing sensitive data
suggestion.rationale: Article notes provider commands 'touch the local filesystem (taking screenshots, managing Playwright traces...)'. Large or unusual screenshot/trace exports could indicate data exfiltration via test artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusually large PNG or ZIP files created by node.exe via vitest commands, or trace files being copied to external storage/network shares. Correlate file creation with data classified as sensitive.

suggestion.title: Vitest allowWrite permission bypass via provider command redirection
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'several of these commands accept a file path from the browser and act on it without checking the allowWrite permission gate'. Need explicit detection for permission-gate bypass attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for vitest Browser Mode command invocations where the calling process lacks expected file write permissions for the target path, yet the command succeeds in creating/modifying the file. This indicates permission gate bypass.

suggestion.title: Suspicious vitest test environment setup with exposed browser port
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability manifests when 'Browser Mode exposes a set of built-in commands'. Need detection for test environments exposing the browser command interface to unauthorized networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect vitest processes starting with --browser or --ui flags in environments where the bound port receives connections from untrusted networks, or where test code is sourced from external/untrusted repositories.

suggestion.title: Detection: CVE-2021-27137 Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated attacker to overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP' — this is the primary attack vector and should trigger scanner/WAF/IDS alerts. Article template requires hunt against `<CVE>: CVE-2021-27137`.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner flagging CVE-2021-27137 or UPnP-based buffer overflow signatures against DD-WRT devices. Monitor network IDS for crafted UPnP requests containing oversized payloads. Correlate with exposed device identification (UPnP multicast responses, HTTP server banners matching DD-WRT patterns).

suggestion.title: Hunting: Unauthenticated UPnP Service Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker' and 'UPnP' — this implies network-accessible UPnP services without authentication gates. Asset exposure hunting is explicitly required: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt...live once in templates'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query internal networks for devices responding to UPnP discovery (SSDP multicast on UDP 1900) or HTTP listening on UPnP ports. Cross-reference with inventory to identify unpatched DD-WRT instances. Flag any devices with UPnP services reachable from untrusted network segments.

suggestion.title: Detection: Post-Exploitation Code Execution on DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'trigger a code execution vulnerability' — successful exploitation results in command execution. No use cases capture post-exploitation execution patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT/Linux syslog and process logs for unexpected command execution originating from UPnP service process context (often runs as root). Look for child processes spawned by UPnP daemons (miniupnpd, upnpd), unusual network connections, or binary writes to system directories immediately following UPnP traffic.

suggestion.title: Compliance: Federal Patch Due Date Alert
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-24' — federal agencies must remediate by this date and auditors will validate compliance. No use case captures deadline-driven remediation tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create alert targeting federal civilian agencies (or regulated entities adopting federal standards): identify all DD-WRT instances, validate patch status for CVE-2021-27137, and escalate unpatched instances with automatic ticket creation for remediation by 2026-07-24. Link to CISA KEV status to justify priority.

suggestion.title: Detection: Buffer Overflow Attack Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'stack-based buffer overflow' in UPnP — WAF/IDS should detect malformed UPnP packets with oversized payloads or boundary-crossing payloads typical of buffer overflow exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Configure WAF/IDS rules to detect UPnP requests with payloads exceeding normal buffer sizes or containing null-byte sequences and stack-smashing patterns. Look for repeated probe attempts with incrementally larger payloads (typical fuzzing/exploitation testing). Flag anomalous UPnP user-agent strings or malformed XML in UPnP control protocol messages.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: CVE-2021-27137 Vulnerable DD-WRT Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs asset-exposure hunt with CVE-2021-27137 substitution. No use case generated despite clear template instruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Apply asset-exposure template to flag hosts with vulnerability scanner results positive for CVE-2021-27137. Cross-reference inventory to confirm DD-WRT product. Prioritize instances with public/perimeter exposure. Escalate unpatched for remediation by federal due date 2026-07-24.

suggestion.title: UPnP Stack Overflow Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability... used by UPnP'—execution requires triggering via UPnP protocol. No execution-phase use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UPnP traffic (UDP 1900/SSDP, TCP 49152+/SOAP) for malformed SOAP envelopes, abnormally large payloads, or buffer-overflow-consistent request patterns. Correlate with device resets, crashes, or service restarts. Detect sequences of failed UPnP requests followed by anomalous command execution.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Device Discovery and UPnP Service Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated attacker' and exposed UPnP service—requires identifying attack surface via network reconnaissance. No initial-access reconnaissance use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan network perimeter for DD-WRT device fingerprints: SSDP multicast responses (UDP 1900), HTTP/HTTPS banners on 80/443/8080 with DD-WRT signatures, X-Forwarded-For or User-Agent headers matching DD-WRT web interface. Identify UPnP services bound to public-facing or DMZ interfaces; cross-reference with patch inventory.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution on DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Successful buffer overflow results in 'code execution'; if router logs forwarded to SIEM, unexpected process spawning from UPnP service context is detectable post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In DD-WRT syslog streams, detect shell spawning (sh, bash, command) from UPnP or httpd parent processes, especially post-crash or restart. Flag outbound network connections from router to attacker infrastructure, reverse shells, wget/curl to external payloads, or modification of system files.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Vulnerable DD-WRT Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated attacker' can exploit DD-WRT buffer overflow; CISA KEV inclusion means active wild exploitation. Article recommends 'standard asset-exposure hunts' for CVE-2021-27137. Cite: 'Unauthenticated attacker to overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify DD-WRT devices with vulnerable firmware versions via UPnP fingerprinting (UDP 1900) or asset inventory. Correlate with network exposure (external-facing or untrusted segments) to surface exploitable assets. Flag devices without corresponding patch evidence by federal due date (2026-07-24).

suggestion.title: Detect UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is specifically 'stack-based buffer overflow' in 'internal buffer used by UPnP.' Active exploitation detection before code execution is critical. Cite: 'overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP and trigger a code execution vulnerability.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UPnP services (UDP/TCP 1900) for abnormal packet sizes, protocol violations, or patterns consistent with buffer overflow attempts. Alert on UPnP traffic anomalies followed by process creation or unexpected outbound connections from the target device.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Execution on DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Successful buffer overflow 'trigger[s] a code execution vulnerability,' resulting in arbitrary command execution. Detection of unexpected processes on compromised devices closes the exploitation-to-impact gap. Cite: 'trigger a code execution vulnerability.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT syslog and telemetry for unexpected process spawning, shell commands, or binary execution correlated with inbound UPnP traffic anomalies. Establish baseline of normal DD-WRT process activity and alert on deviations following potential exploitation windows.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Device Inventory and Vulnerable Version Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'DD-WRT contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability'—assets must be identified and catalogued. No inventory hunt exists to locate DD-WRT instances or enumerate firmware versions against CVE-2021-27137 affected releases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to DD-WRT default ports (80, 443, 8080) or UPnP SSDP multicast announcements (UDP 1900). Cross-reference User-Agent strings, SSL certificate metadata, and DHCP fingerprints against known DD-WRT signatures. Correlate device inventory with vulnerability scanner output to identify instances vulnerable to CVE-2021-27137 not yet patched.

suggestion.title: UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated attacker to overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP'—this is the primary attack surface. No use case monitors for UPnP protocol violations or oversized payloads targeting vulnerable daemons.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for UPnP/SSDP traffic (UDP 1900, TCP/UDP 5000-5001) to DD-WRT devices with abnormally large payloads, malformed SOAP messages, or requests exceeding normal parameter boundaries. Flag protocol violations and multi-stage SSDP requests indicative of buffer overflow exploitation.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Artifact Detection on DD-WRT Targets
suggestion.rationale: Article describes successful 'code execution vulnerability'—no use case detects execution artifacts (unexpected processes, file writes, persistence mechanisms) following exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate UPnP exploit attempts against device logs for coredumps, unexpected child process spawning from UPnP daemons, new SSH/Telnet listeners, outbound C2 connections, or writes to /etc or /usr/bin. Flag suspicious binaries or shell spawning in context of prior UPnP anomalies.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Patch Compliance Audit for CVE-2021-27137
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-24'—no compliance hunt validates patch status across fleet. CISA KEV prioritization requires due-date tracking and remediation verification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and device management systems for DD-WRT firmware versions classified as vulnerable to CVE-2021-27137. Generate compliance report flagging systems not remediated by federal due date; cross-check against patch history to identify lag.

suggestion.title: Data Quality Alert: CVE Title-Body Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article title references CVE-2025-30066 but body discusses CVE-2021-27137—this inconsistency prevents proper threat correlation and IOC extraction. Pipeline should validate intra-article coherence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement schema validation on threat-intel ingestion to detect when article title CVE differs from body CVE or content. Flag for manual review when multiple CVE IDs appear in single document. This prevents false negatives from split IOC extraction and dropped alert correlations.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: DD-WRT CVE-2021-27137 Fleet Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly instructs: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt...Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>: CVE-2021-27137' with federal due date 2026-07-24. Pipeline generated zero UCs despite direct template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate DD-WRT devices on network via asset management and port discovery. Cross-reference vulnerability scanner data for CVE-2021-27137. Flag devices with UDP 1900 (UPnP) accessible from untrusted network boundaries.

suggestion.title: Malformed UPnP Buffer Overflow Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploit 'triggered...by UPnP' via buffer overflow—malformed SSDP/UPnP requests are the attack vector. Pipeline produced no network-based exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UDP port 1900 for anomalous SSDP traffic from external sources: oversized payloads, malformed M-SEARCH requests, or non-standard UPnP message structures indicative of buffer overflow exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution on DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow...code execution' but pipeline produced no behavioral detection for successful command execution post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT devices for unexpected process spawning, shell command interpretation, or suspicious outbound connections from system daemons. Detect reverse shells, downloaded binaries, or script interpretation from UPnP-related processes.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Modification to Attacker Commit
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Changing existing release tags to point to the attack commit' and 'the attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit'. This is a primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for release tag modifications that point to commits not on main/release branches or to newly-created orphaned commits. Alert on tags being moved backward in commit history or to unrelated commits. Correlate with changes in Action file content.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit Detection in CI/CD Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies orphaned commits as an 'enabling factor': 'Having the attack commit orphaned from any branches, including the main branch These factors added a bit of obfuscation to hide the attack.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits that are referenced by release tags but do not appear on any branch. Query Git history for commits reachable only via tags. Alert on orphaned commits in security-sensitive repositories like GitHub Actions or build tooling.

suggestion.title: Encrypted Secrets Exposed in Plaintext in GitHub Actions Logs
suggestion.rationale: Core attack impact: 'caused encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs'. This is the direct exfiltration path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions workflow logs for patterns matching credential formats (API tokens, SSH keys, database passwords). Cross-reference against known secret prefixes. Alert if secrets defined in repository settings appear in cleartext in public Action runs. Monitor for log export or archival to external systems.

suggestion.title: Suspicious External Network Call from GitHub Actions Workflow
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network requests initiated during GitHub Actions execution. Alert on DNS queries or HTTP/HTTPS connections to domains not in a whitelist, especially to domains registered recently or associated with anomalous activity. Track data transfer volume in Action logs or network egress.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Commit by Non-Standard User to Widely-Deployed GitHub Action
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit that caused encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext'. Attacker access is foundational.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For high-impact repositories (Actions, build tools used by 1000+ repos), flag commits from users outside the expected maintainer list. Alert on commits during off-hours or from unusual IP addresses. Cross-reference with user access reviews. Escalate if commit modifies security-critical workflow files.

suggestion.title: Version Tag Regression or Anomalous Tag Movement in Release Repository
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack pattern: legitimate tags moved to compromise commit. Article shows: 'he attacker re-pointed several existing release tags to their malicious commit.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track Git tag history. Alert if a tag points to a commit older than its previous reference (version regression) or to a commit by an unexpected author. For popular Actions, require maintainer approval for tag changes. Monitor consumers of Actions for sudden version inconsistencies in pinned tags.

suggestion.title: npm Package Dependency Hijacking via Typosquatting
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords reference 'supply chain' attacks on npm packages; Shai Hulud and similar campaigns leverage dependency confusion and typosquatting to distribute malware. Article explicitly addresses attack surface against package.json dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install/require calls to packages with suspicious names similar to popular libraries (edit distance <2 from known packages), or packages installed from unusual registries. Monitor process creation from npm postinstall scripts executing with high privileges or network I/O.

suggestion.title: npm postinstall Hook Code Execution & Obfuscated Payload Staging
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes 'obfuscation' and 'payload' in context of npm attacks; postinstall scripts are primary vector. Article keywords explicitly cite 'worm propagation' suggesting malware self-replication via install hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm postinstall scripts containing base64, hex, or ROT13 encoding; process creation from npm/node with cryptographic or deobfuscation library imports; network callbacks during postinstall execution phases.

suggestion.title: npm Worm Propagation via package.json Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'worm propagation' as attack pattern; npm supply chain attacks often modify local package.json or lock files to inject malicious dependencies into downstream projects.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modification of package.json, package-lock.json, or yarn.lock by process trees rooted in npm/node; new dependency entries pointing to non-standard registries or typosquat packages; file writes from npm cache directories to project root.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via npm CI/CD Pipeline Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords cite 'credential harvesting' and 'CI/CD persistence' as distinct attack patterns; attackers compromise npm dependencies to intercept credentials passed through build pipelines (npm tokens, registry auth).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm processes reading ~/.npmrc or .env files containing authentication tokens; network exfiltration of npm_TOKEN environment variable values; process injection into npm audit or npm publish workflows.

suggestion.title: Shai Hulud Campaign IoC Tracking & Signature Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article description explicitly references 'Shai Hulud' as named campaign subject; pipeline failed to surface actor name or associated file hashes, domains, or malware families despite critical severity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm package checksums and download metadata for packages in Shai Hulud campaign; detect C2 domains associated with malware payloads; monitor for typosquat or lookalike package names known from campaign indicators.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Authentication Bypass & Account Takeover Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article's supply chain attack surface includes compromised maintainer accounts; detection should flag unusual npm publish patterns, authentication from new geolocations, or bulk package version uploads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm publish API calls from IP addresses or user agents not associated with known maintainers; multiple package versions published in short time windows; authentication tokens used across geographically distant regions within short intervals.

suggestion.title: UPnP Service Exposure on Non-Standard Ports
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker' exploits 'UPnP' service and implies exposure to public-facing assets. No detection for network exposure of the vulnerable service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on discovery of open UPnP (UDP 1900) or SSDP services responding to multicast queries, particularly on DD-WRT or embedded Linux devices. Cross-reference against asset inventory to identify out-of-compliance exposed services.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Vulnerable Firmware Identification
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies DD-WRT as vulnerable product. No detection for inventory-based identification of affected devices or firmware version fingerprinting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2021-27137 matches on DD-WRT devices. Correlate with network exposure scans to identify DD-WRT appliances with open UPnP services reachable from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Buffer Overflow Payload Patterns in UPnP Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'stack-based buffer overflow' as attack mechanism. No detection for characteristic overflow patterns (overlong strings, NOP sleds, shellcode signatures) in UPnP protocol traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UPnP traffic (UDP 1900, TCP device/description requests) for payload anomalies: abnormally long header fields, repeated byte patterns, or binary payloads in XML/SOAP responses. Flag any UPnP transaction >2KB.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution via DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'trigger[s] a code execution vulnerability' but pipeline captured no indicators of successful exploitation or shell access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT devices for unexpected process spawning, shell interpreter invocation, or network connection initiation from UPnP daemons or root context. Flag any shell access (ssh, telnet, web shell) from external sources immediately after UPnP anomalies.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2021-27137 — match against your vulnerability scanner' but pipeline emitted zero IOCs. No detection logic references the CVE identifier.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all network-exposed appliances quarterly with vulnerability scanner rules for CVE-2021-27137. Alert on any positive match with CVSS ≥9.8. Escalate DD-WRT matches to critical and enforce remediation by federal due date 2026-07-24.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised DD-WRT Gateway
suggestion.rationale: If exploited, DD-WRT typically functions as a network gateway; pipeline missed post-exploitation lateral movement risk. Article describes code execution but not pivot detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT devices post-exploitation for abnormal outbound traffic (scanning, lateral spreads, C2). Flag any new port-forwarding rules, DNS hijacking, or traffic redirection configured after compromise. Correlate failed SSH/RDP attempts to internal hosts with UPnP exploit timeline.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Asset Discovery via UPnP
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'unauthenticated attacker' exploitation of UPnP service. Defenders must identify vulnerable DD-WRT instances on the network; the article provides no attack-infrastructure IOCs, making asset discovery the primary detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DD-WRT instances via UPnP SSDP broadcasts (port 1900/UDP), HTTP banner grabbing on ports 80/443, or mDNS queries. Correlate with vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2021-27137.

suggestion.title: UPnP Stack Overflow Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability' in UPnP. Exploitation requires sending malformed UPnP payloads to overflow the buffer and execute code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal UPnP packet sizes, malformed SOAP requests, or oversized payloads to UPnP service ports (typically 1900, 5000). IDS rules should detect buffer-overflow-like patterns in UPnP traffic from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Vulnerability Scanner Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article is CISA KEV with federal remediation deadline 2026-07-24. Defenders will conduct scanning activity; detecting scanner traffic identifies both defensive and potential offensive reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Nessus, OpenVAS, Qualys, or custom script-based scanning of UPnP endpoints. Look for scanner user-agents, sequential port probing of UPnP ranges, or repeated exploit-attempt signatures against the same target.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution on DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article states overflow 'trigger a code execution vulnerability.' Successful exploitation enables attacker to execute arbitrary commands on the router; unexpected process spawning or shell invocation indicates compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT syslog for shell invocation (sh/bash), unexpected process spawning from UPnP service, or unauthorized SSH/telnet connections. Baseline normal UPnP service behavior and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2021-27137 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and mandates federal remediation by 2026-07-24. Pipeline omitted baseline vulnerability scanning detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for CVE-2021-27137 matches across DD-WRT asset class. Alert on any unpatched instances. Correlate with asset criticality and network exposure tier to prioritize remediation. Track closure status against federal due date.

suggestion.title: UPnP Service Exposure on Untrusted Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector as 'unauthenticated attacker to overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP', implying network-accessible UPnP services. Pipeline missed exposure detection for this attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify DD-WRT devices responding to UPnP discovery (SSDP on UDP 1900 or non-standard ports) from external/untrusted network segments. Alert on public-facing UPnP services. Track via asset inventory correlation to identify vulnerable instances before exploitation.

suggestion.title: Malformed UPnP Packet Delivery to DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability' in UPnP handler. Pipeline should detect exploitation attempts via malformed or oversized UPnP payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormally large or malformed UPnP packets (SSDP M-SEARCH, SOAP requests) to DD-WRT targets, especially with excessive header lengths or binary payloads designed to trigger buffer overflow. Tune IDS signatures to DD-WRT UPnP stack boundaries.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Processes from UPnP Daemon
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates remote code execution via buffer overflow would manifest as process execution in UPnP service context on vulnerable DD-WRT devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On DD-WRT hosts, monitor for anomalous child processes spawned by UPnP daemon (upnpd) or related network services with unexpected names, command-line arguments, or outbound network connections. Establish baseline for normal UPnP-spawned processes.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Configuration Modification Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE attackers typically persist via firmware or UCI configuration tampering. Article's exploitation path establishes persistence vector but pipeline missed detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT NVRAM and UCI configuration file checksums/modification times for unauthorized changes. Alert on unexpected firewall rule additions, SSH key installations, or cron job modifications correlating with exploitation detection windows.

suggestion.title: CVE-2021-27137 Vulnerable DD-WRT Inventory Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies CVE-2021-27137 as exploited in the wild (CISA KEV) and states federal patch due 2026-07-24. Pipeline generated zero asset-exposure detections despite this being the primary IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all DD-WRT devices in the environment running firmware versions vulnerable to CVE-2021-27137. Cross-reference network inventory with vulnerability scanner results. Flag any devices not patched by federal due date 2026-07-24 as critical exposure.

suggestion.title: Malformed UPnP Requests Targeting DD-WRT Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP'—exploitation requires sending crafted payloads to UPnP endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UPnP traffic (port 1900/UDP, port 5000/TCP) to DD-WRT devices for oversized payloads, malformed SOAP XML, or repeated probing. Stack-based buffer overflows require payloads exceeding expected buffer sizes. Alert on external-source UPnP requests to internal routers.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution on DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploit 'could allow...code execution.' Successful overflow would trigger unexpected process activity or network connections from the compromised device.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor compromised DD-WRT devices for unexpected child process spawning, system file modifications, or outbound connections (reverse shell, C2). Post-exploitation typically manifests as new listening ports, firmware modifications, or connection attempts to external IP addresses from the router.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance and Risk Acceptance for CVE-2021-27137
suggestion.rationale: Federal agencies required to remediate by 2026-07-24 per CISA KEV. Compliance and risk management is mandatory—any device still running vulnerable firmware post-deadline must be documented.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate automated compliance report tracking DD-WRT patching status. Flag unpatched devices as critical. For any device still vulnerable after due date, require documented risk acceptance or removal from network. Include in SOC escalation workflow.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability...overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP.' This is the attack vector and execution mechanism—must detect malformed UPnP payloads and service crashes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UPnP service (UDP 1900) for abnormally large SSDP packets or malformed requests from external IPs. Correlate with UPnP daemon crashes, segmentation faults, or memory access violations on DD-WRT devices. Flag immediate code execution attempts post-crash.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Web Interface Exposure and Scanning

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify externally accessible DD-WRT management interfaces via banner fingerprinting (HTTP/HTTPS ports with DD-WRT signatures). Correlate with vulnerability scanner traffic patterns (Shodan User-Agent, common CVE scanners). Alert on any external connection attempts to typical DD-WRT ports (80, 443, 8080).

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution Post-Exploitation on DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'trigger a code execution vulnerability.' Must detect execution phase beyond buffer overflow—child processes, shell invocations, outbound callbacks from compromised device.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by UPnP daemon or httpd service. Flag shell invocation (/bin/sh, /bin/bash, telnetd) from non-standard parents. Detect outbound TCP connections from router context to non-RFC1918 destinations or known C2 ranges immediately following exploit timing.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Vulnerable Version Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due date '2026-07-24' and CISA KEV context requires remediation tracking. Must inventory vulnerable firmware versions across fleet to measure compliance risk and patch progress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract DD-WRT firmware version from web interface fingerprinting and version strings. Maintain inventory of devices running versions vulnerable to CVE-2021-27137 (released before patch date). Track remediation progress week-over-week; alert on any new instances added post-remediation deadline.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT UPnP Service Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies UPnP as the attack surface: 'overflow an internal buffer used by UPnP.' Must detect exposed UPnP instances on DD-WRT routers before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify DD-WRT devices exposing UPnP (UDP 1900 or typical UPnP ports). Correlate with firmware fingerprinting (HTTP banner grabs, SSDP responses containing DD-WRT signatures). Flag as high-risk for active exploitation.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable DD-WRT Firmware Inventory

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Passive network scanning for DD-WRT HTTP banners (port 80/443), UPNP device descriptors containing DD-WRT firmware strings, or SSH/Telnet version strings. Correlate with vulnerability scanner output to map inventory to known vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempt

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Firmware Patch Compliance Inventory

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DD-WRT devices for unexpected process creation (especially shell spawning), unexpected outbound SSH/telnet connections from devices, or HTTP requests to management interfaces immediately following UPnP exploit attempts.

suggestion.title: UPnP Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempt Detection

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Execution on DD-WRT Devices

suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated exploitation requires prior discovery. Scanner fingerprinting of vulnerable UPnP services is precursor to buffer overflow delivery.

suggestion.title: DD-WRT Kernel/Privilege Escalation Post-Compromise

suggestion.title: IoT Botnet C2 Beaconing via Non-Standard Ports
suggestion.rationale: TuxBot v3 is an IoT botnet; the article title signals LLM-assisted evolution implying novel C2 communication patterns. Standard botnet detection should focus on command-and-control beaconing. No use cases were generated for this core attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect IoT devices (based on user-agent, device OS metadata) initiating outbound connections to rare external IPs on non-standard ports (not 80, 443, 22) with periodic re-connection attempts every 300–900 seconds. Flag if connection initiator is a known consumer IoT device class (camera, NVR, router, HVAC controller).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution on IoT/Linux Systems from Downloaded Binary
suggestion.rationale: Botnet infection typically begins with dropped/downloaded payload execution. Article describes TuxBot v3 evolution but pipeline captured no initial-execution indicators. No detection for malware execution on edge/IoT Linux systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of binaries from /tmp or /var/tmp with low prevalence on IoT/embedded Linux systems. Correlate with recent file-write events from curl/wget. Flag if parent process is a shell spawned by unauthenticated remote session or web server.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Cron or Init Script Modification on Linux IoT Devices
suggestion.rationale: IoT botnets require persistence; TuxBot v3 would need to survive reboots. Article describes evolution and sophistication but no persistence-layer detections were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to /etc/cron.d, /etc/crontab, /etc/init.d, or systemd service files on IoT devices. Detect creation of new cron jobs or init scripts by non-root or unexpected UIDs. Alert on cron entries pointing to /tmp paths or downloading remote scripts.

suggestion.title: LLM-Generated Obfuscation in IoT Malware Strings
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'LLM-assisted IoT Botnet Development'—a novel indicator that the malware payload likely contains AI-generated obfuscation or anti-analysis code. No use cases address detection of LLM artifacts (encoded config blocks, polymorphic shellcode signatures).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag IoT malware samples with anomalously high string entropy or packed/obfuscated config blocks. Cross-reference against known LLM output patterns (repetitive token sequences, unusual Unicode escaping, atypical variable naming).
