Correlate with failed auth followed by successful admin action in same session.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-16232 Vulnerability Detection & Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies CVE-2026-16232 as the primary identifier and cites federal patch due date 2026-07-25. Scanner matches are baseline blocking for KEV entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and software inventory for Check Point SmartConsole instances matching CVE-2026-16232. Flag any unpatched instances; cross-reference patch date against federal deadline 2026-07-25.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Unauthenticated Token Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: 'unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token'—requires direct log-based detection of token issuance without prior auth handshake.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole authentication service for token generation events originating from unauthenticated sessions or missing required auth credentials. Baseline normal token issuance and alert on deviations; correlate token ID with subsequent admin API calls.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Administrative Privilege Escalation Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'authenticate with full administrative privileges'—privilege escalation phase requires detecting unauthorized admin role activation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on admin API operations or privilege escalation events tied to tokens generated without prior authentication. Flag sudden elevation of account permissions or first-time admin role assignments tied to suspicious tokens.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Internet Exposure Verification
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation premise is 'unauthenticated remote attacker'—implying internet-reachable console. Article describes public-facing application vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify SmartConsole instances (ports 4434/tcp, SSH 22) are NOT externally routable. Hunt for inbound internet traffic to SmartConsole that bypasses corporate VPN/bastion hosts. Cross-check Shodan and Censys for public-facing SmartConsole fingerprints.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Anomalous Token Usage Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain pivots on token abuse after initial compromise: 'obtain token and use it to authenticate with full admin privileges'—behavioral detection of token misuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for SmartConsole token lifecycle (issue rate, geographic source consistency, operation frequency per token). Alert on tokens performing high-privilege operations (policy changes, credential manipulation) inconsistent with their requester's normal RBAC profile or geographic origin.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated SmartConsole Token Acquisition
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token' — core exploit path requiring direct detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP(S) requests to Check Point SmartConsole authentication endpoints (default ports 4434–4435) from external sources receiving successful token responses (200 OK, token in response body) without prior password-based login context. Alert on rapid token requests from single source IP.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Admin Privilege Escalation via Stolen Token
suggestion.rationale: Article: token used to 'authenticate with full administrative privileges' — requires detection of administrative actions performed via non-standard auth paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole for administrative configuration changes (policy modifications, user additions, export operations) performed by sessions where authentication was token-based (not password) and token issuance timestamp is anomalous (outside business hours, new source IP, or immediately following reconnaissance activity).

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole Instance Exposure and Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry explicitly states 'observed exploited in the wild'—active scanning of exposed instances is critical. Article: 'Anything in CISA KEV is *currently* being exploited.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory query: identify all externally-reachable systems responding on SmartConsole ports (4434, 4435, 18196). Correlate against patch version database for CVE-2026-16232 applicability (affects unpatched versions). Flag any unpatched instances for immediate emergency remediation by federal deadline 2026-07-25.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Authentication Endpoint Scanning and Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation pattern implies reconnaissance phase. Article describes unauthenticated access, suggesting attacker must first locate and probe endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect patterns of failed HTTP requests to SmartConsole paths (/login, /api/auth, /console) from single source, followed by successful token acquisition (asymmetric success rate). Alert on enumeration activity: sequential requests to multiple management ports or API endpoints within short time window.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole: Token Generation Without Prior Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'obtain an application login token' *unauthenticated*; pipeline missed the core credential-access pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for authentication tokens issued to Check Point SmartConsole without preceding successful login events or with blank/null user context. Look for token creation from external IPs not in baseline. Correlate against failed login attempts—a spike in token issuance *without* matching auth successes suggests exploitation.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole: Administrative Access via Fraudulent Token
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies tokens grant 'full administrative privileges'—this is privilege escalation and deserves standalone detection, separate from token theft.
log_sources: Check Point SmartConsole admin audit logs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on admin-level actions (policy creation, user provisioning, firewall rules) performed by tokens that lack corresponding prior authentication audit trails or originate from unexpected geographies/ASNs. Compare token first-seen timestamp against initial auth event.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole: Unauthenticated Remote Access Attempts to Default Ports
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated remote attacker' can exploit SmartConsole; network-layer detection for port access is missing. KEV entries imply active scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound connections to Check Point SmartConsole default ports (typically 18190, 18191) from external/untrusted sources without corresponding VPN or allowlist membership. Flag rapid connection attempts or scanning behavior. Correlate with CVE-2026-16232 scanning activity if threat intel surfaces it.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole: API Calls with Invalid or Suspicious Token Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Improper auth may result in malformed or replayed tokens; detection of token anomalies in API requests is a direct validation hook.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point SmartConsole API calls for tokens with invalid signatures, expired timestamps, or mismatch between token claims (user, role, IP) and actual request context. Flag tokens reused across multiple IPs or used after policy-based revocation.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole — Unauthenticated Token Issuance
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'obtain[s] an application login token' without authentication. This is the root exploitation step: 'unauthenticated remote attacker'. Detection must catch token generation that lacks a corresponding successful authentication event.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for SmartConsole authentication token issuance events (successful token responses, session creation) that occur without a prior successful login or MFA validation. Correlate API token generation with absence of password validation, LDAP bind, or SAML assertion in the preceding 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole — Admin Operations via Unauthenticated Token
suggestion.rationale: Article describes token is used 'to authenticate with full administrative privileges'. This is privilege escalation: a token obtained outside normal auth pathways is used for admin-level operations. Detectable via anomalous permission elevation in a single session.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sessions that perform administrative operations (policy changes, user/role modifications, system configuration writes) without a valid login record or with login events tagged as 'failed' or 'unauthenticated' preceding the operation. Focus on token-based access patterns.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole — Token Extraction via Remote Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated remote attacker' accessing SmartConsole. Implies network-exposed endpoint being probed for token endpoints or authentication bypass. Should detect suspicious remote requests to auth/token endpoints from sources with no prior SmartConsole user or API history.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP/HTTPS requests to SmartConsole authentication or token endpoints (e.g., /api/login, /auth/token, /console/authenticate) from external IP addresses that have no history of SmartConsole API usage, followed by successful token responses (HTTP 200 with token payload) without username/password submission.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole — Admin Console Access Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Once a token is obtained with admin privileges, the attacker can interact with the console. Article implies full administrative control ('full administrative privileges'). Detection should focus on lateral movement, policy deployment, or system changes following the token compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate anomalous admin-level changes (firewall policy deployments, rule additions, gateway reconfigurations) occurring within 10 minutes of unusual token issuance events. Flag if the authenticated user has no prior change history in the last 30 days or if the change originates from a geoIP location mismatched with org baseline.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Unauthenticated Token Generation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token.' Core attack vector missed—detection should trigger on token issuance to sources that never authenticated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole authentication endpoints for successful token/session grants from previously-unauthenticated or external sources. Correlate token issuance with subsequent administrative API calls from same IP. Alert on token generation without prior successful login.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Unauthorized Admin Actions via Compromised Token
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use it to authenticate with full administrative privileges.' Pipeline missed detection of elevated actions (policy changes, user creation, exports) from external/untrusted sources using stolen tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate SmartConsole admin users and their typical actions. Alert on administrative operations (configuration changes, user mgmt, policy export) from non-baseline tokens, external IPs, or after recent authentication anomalies. Flag bulk policy queries or exports.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-16232 Vulnerability Scan & Asset Inventory Match
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates federal remediation by 2026-07-25. Pipeline should generate asset-exposure hunt: identify Check Point SmartConsole instances and cross-match against scan results for this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Check Point SmartConsole deployments. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-16232 and patch status. Flag instances with internet-facing exposure, prioritize by CVSS 9.8 (critical) and active exploitation in CISA KEV.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Remote Console Access Baseline Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated remote attacker' implies exposed management interface. Pipeline missed detection of access pattern deviation from known legitimate admin sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate SmartConsole console access (IPs, times, geographies, user agents). Alert on access from new external sources, off-hours access, or suspicious protocol/port combinations. Cross-correlate with successful token generation immediately after baseline violation.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole API Exploitation via Token Reuse Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article describes obtaining 'application login token' for authentication. Pipeline missed detection of rapid or unusual API activity chains using same token (bulk exports, policy discovery, user enumeration).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole API endpoints for token-authenticated requests showing exploitation patterns: rapid-fire policy queries, bulk configuration exports, user account enumeration, or policy cloning. Alert on same token issuing calls across disparate endpoints within short window.

suggestion.title: Successful pheditor.php authentication with no subsequent password change
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'no mechanism to force a password change on first login'—default credential compromise leaves no post-auth password mutation. Direct indicator of default-cred use: login(user=admin OR POST /pheditor.php with auth) NOT FOLLOWED BY password-change operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for successful HTTP 200/302 responses to pheditor.php auth POST requests from accounts with 'admin' username or unauthenticated access to admin panel. Correlate with absence of subsequent password-change requests (PATCH/POST to password-reset endpoints) within 15 minutes. Survivors indicate potential default-cred compromise.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded hash integrity check failure (pheditor.php line 11 SHA-512 modification)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'SHA-512 hash stored at pheditor.php:11'—attackers modifying hash to add backdoor account. Requires baseline of known-good hash and detection of divergence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare SHA-256 of pheditor.php against known-good baseline. Alert on any modification. Supplement with file-content scan for embedded password strings or eval() in line 1-20 range to catch hash-rewrite persistence.

suggestion.title: Pheditor file-upload feature abuse (multipart form submission to upload handler)
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'file upload' as a capability enabling compromise, but no UC specifically hunts file-upload POST operations before webshell-creation events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP POST requests to pheditor.php with multipart/form-data Content-Type and file-upload parameters. Correlate upload operations (POST /pheditor.php?action=upload OR equivalent) with PHP file creation in web-root within 30s, especially if upload filename does not match created .php filename (indicates renaming/obfuscation).

suggestion.title: Pheditor terminal feature abuse without prior file-operation activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'file editor, file upload, and terminal' features—terminal RCE is high-risk. Legitimate use typically follows file editing. Immediate jump to terminal after login may indicate automated exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to pheditor.php with action=terminal or command= parameters occurring within 5 minutes of authentication, without intervening action=editor or file-browse requests. This breaks typical user workflow and signals possible automated tool usage.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Unauthenticated Authentication Token Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token'—direct evidence of auth bypass leading to token issuance. Pipeline generated zero UCs despite this being the core exploitation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful authentication token generation (status 200/201) from source IPs that have no prior valid credentials, or detect auth_level='admin' in token response when source sent no or invalid credentials. SmartConsole typically logs token grants to `/api/login` or similar endpoints; alerting on success without prior password authentication is the key signal.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Admin Privilege Escalation from Null Auth
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use it to authenticate with full administrative privileges'—attacker moves from zero credentials to admin in single step. This privilege jump is abnormal and detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any session upgrade from 'unauthenticated' or 'guest' role to 'admin' or 'superuser' without an intermediate password reset or MFA challenge. Look for token claims or session objects where privileges escalated within a single request or within seconds of token issuance.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole External Remote Access via Public Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote attacker' accessing public-facing authentication; no mention of VPN requirement. Detect internet-routable access to SmartConsole services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful connections to SmartConsole ports (typically 443, 8443, or 4434) originating from public/internet IP ranges. Cross-reference with internal SmartConsole access logs—any auth attempt from non-RFC1918 source should trigger review.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Authentication Failure Loop Followed by Token Grant
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation likely involves probing auth endpoints. Detect pattern of failed auth requests (wrong creds, malformed payloads) followed by unexpected successful token issuance from same source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline: N failed auth attempts within T seconds typically precede credential-stuffing activity. Vulnerability exploitation may show 1–5 failures then immediate admin token grant. Alert on any auth success immediately following auth failures from same IP, especially if success omits password field or logs show NULL/empty credentials.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Token Reuse and Lateral Privilege Expansion
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'obtain an application login token and use it'—implies token persists and is reusable across multiple actions. Detect abnormal token usage patterns suggesting attacker pivoting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track active tokens and flag if a single admin token is used across multiple management actions (e.g., policy modification, user creation, export) within a short window or from disparate geographic/network contexts. Cross-reference token TTL; if a token issued by unauthenticated flow is used post-TTL, that indicates refresh or persistence exploit.

suggestion.title: Zimbra Zero-Day Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article lead states Russian group 'exploited Zimbra zero-day' — core attack vector entirely missing from pipeline output. No IOCs, no exploitation signatures, no kill-chain phase mapped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Zimbra mail servers for non-standard POST/PUT requests to /service/* endpoints, unusual XML-RPC call sequences, POST payloads to admin interfaces from non-admin source IPs, or authentication errors followed immediately by successful mailbox access from same IP.

suggestion.title: 2FA Code Extraction from Compromised Mailbox
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'steal mail and 2FA codes' — credential-access phase missing. Requires detection of mass email reads targeting authentication message keywords post-Zimbra-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid email access (>50 messages/minute) from single mailbox post-compromise, filtering by subject keywords ('verification', 'code', 'OTP', 'confirm', 'authenticate'). Correlate with external IP accessing mailbox for first time; trigger if 2FA code forwarding rules or export operations detected.

suggestion.title: Mailbox Data Bulk Export Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Successful Zimbra exploit enables 'steal mail' objective — collection phase absent. Pipeline should flag PST/archive creation, attachment bulk download, or email export to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect mailbox export requests, PST file creation via Zimbra APIs, high-volume email sync to external IMAP/POP accounts, or forwarding rules targeting non-organization domains created immediately after Zimbra server compromise detection.

suggestion.title: Stolen 2FA Code Reuse for Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 2FA codes stolen; pipeline should surface lateral-movement detection when those codes bypass MFA on downstream systems (VPN, cloud platforms, HR systems).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate: (1) Zimbra compromise IP, (2) email message access to '2FA', 'code', 'TOTP' threads, (3) successful MFA logins from *different* IP 1–2 hours later using credentials from stolen mailbox, (4) unusual resource access post-MFA (cloud admin portals, sensitive file shares). Flag if logins originate from Russian ASNs or known SVR/GRU infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Persistent C2 Beaconing from Compromised Zimbra Server
suggestion.rationale: Russian APT persistence not modeled in empty kill-chain. Pipeline should detect outbound C2 infrastructure maintaining attacker access to stolen mailbox/2FA credential stores.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Zimbra server egress for: (1) encrypted tunnels to residential Russian IPs, (2) DNS queries to domains with low passive-DNS history, (3) repeated POST/GET to attacker-controlled domains with encrypted payloads, (4) beacons at consistent intervals (typical C2 heartbeat). Correlate ASN geolocation to known Russian intelligence infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Hidden Admin Account or Service Account Creation on Zimbra
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation persistence mechanism entirely missed. Article describes ongoing compromise implying sustained access; pipeline lacks detection for attacker-created backdoor accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-admin principals creating new Zimbra users/service accounts, especially with names resembling system accounts ('sync', 'backup', 'admin2'). Detect delegation of mailbox permissions to external addresses, API token creation for non-standard accounts, or calendar/contact synchronization enablement to third-party services.

suggestion.title: MSI File Masquerading as Windows Update Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states threat uses 'deceptive MSI file masquerading as a Windows update' and advises to 'Scrutinize unexpected MSI files impersonating Windows updates.' This is the primary initial-access vector with concrete detection signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on MSI file creation in user-writable directories (Downloads, Desktop, AppData, ProgramData) with filenames containing Windows update keywords ('WindowsUpdate', 'KB', 'patch', 'Update'). Correlate with source URL (email, web download) and immediate execution by cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or rundll32.exe without preceding legitimate Windows Update Manager process.

suggestion.title: Suspicious curl Downloads to ProgramData
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'monitor for unusual curl commands, especially those downloading MSI files to the ProgramData directory' as primary detection signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect curl.exe process execution with CLI arguments targeting .msi URLs and output path containing ProgramData or system temp directories. Flag parent processes that are not native Windows (e.g., browser, script engine). Exclude WSUS/patch management channels via whitelist.

suggestion.title: Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) Hijacking for C2
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies msaRAT 'hijacking Chrome or Edge browsers via the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP)' and mandates 'implement behavioral monitoring to catch Chrome DevTools Protocol abuse.' CDP is the core C2 evasion mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for chrome.exe or msedge.exe listening on or connecting to localhost CDP ports (9222, 9223, or dynamic high ports) without corresponding DevTools debugging session from user profile. Detect via TCP socket monitoring, EventTracing, or absence of user-initiated debugger attachment. Alert on non-interactive process spawning CDP-enabled browser instances.

suggestion.title: HTTP Protocol over Port 443 (Protocol Mismatch)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies defender signal: 'sending plain HTTP traffic over port 443' as anomaly indicating msaRAT communications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag network events where RemotePort=443 AND Protocol='HTTP' (no TLS handshake) OR where TLS handshake fails but HTTP payload bytes follow. Correlate with browser processes. Establish baseline of legitimate port-443 HTTP for known apps (e.g., QUIC, custom protocols) and exclude.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized WebRTC Connection Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article warning: 'implement behavioral monitoring to catch... unauthorized WebRTC connections' establishes WebRTC as secondary/alternate C2 channel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WebRTC port allocation (UDP 3478-3479, STUN/TURN) initiated by chrome.exe or msedge.exe without active video conferencing process or user GUI interaction. Monitor browser API calls (RTCPeerConnection, getUserMedia, addIceCandidate) in process memory for non-video-conferencing contexts. Baseline against Teams, Meet, Zoom.

suggestion.title: Memory-Resident Payload Injection from MSI via Tokio Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Article states payload 'loads the payload directly into memory' and identifies Tokio async runtime as execution engine. This establishes memory-injection and unsigned-binary loading as core evasion mechanism separating this from baseline MSI attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on MSI execution (msiexec.exe, rundll32.exe) followed by unsigned/suspicious DLL injection into chrome.exe or system process address space. Monitor for CreateRemoteThread, SetThreadContext, or VirtualAllocEx targeting browser processes from MSI-related parent. Flag unsigned binaries with Tokio-related exports or Rust artifacts (panic, tokio, async) in VirtualQuery results.

suggestion.title: Notepad++ Plugin DLL Load from Non-Standard Path
suggestion.rationale: Article states malicious NppExport.dll 'loaded via the application's normal plugin-loading mechanism' from a randomly-named directory. Standard plugins live in %APPDATA%\Notepad++\plugins; loads from temp or user-controlled paths indicate plugin hijacking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when notepad++.exe loads a .dll from outside standard plugin paths. Correlate file timestamps (recently modified vs. app version release date). Cross-reference loaded DLL against official Notepad++ plugin registry and Notepad++ team signing certificates.

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task Created by Plugin or Temp-Resident DLL
suggestion.rationale: LunchPoke 'creates a scheduled task on Windows' to establish persistence. Scheduled task creation via DLL processes loaded from non-standard locations signals post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor schtasks.exe spawned by DLL processes or registry write attempts to HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Schedule\TaskCache. Alert on tasks with random names, no description, or pointing to executables in temp directories created within hours of Notepad++ launch.

suggestion.title: Chained Archive Extraction (VBS → ZIP → RAR)
suggestion.rationale: Attack narrative: 'VBS script...retrieves another compressed file named Evernote.zip. The second archive contains...a password-protected archive (updater.rar).' Each extraction stage is a separate file-write event; chained extraction sequences from scripting engines are rare in legitimate workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect parent chain: wscript.exe → WinRAR/7-Zip → file extraction into randomly-named subdirectories. Alert on archive utilities invoked with non-interactive flags from script context or when extraction target directory is deleted immediately after executable extraction.

suggestion.title: Resource Exhaustion Attack (CPU/RAM Spike from Malware Loader)
suggestion.rationale: Article states BurnyBear fallback 'triggering a resource exhaustion attack targeting the host's RAM and CPU.' This non-standard attack vector creates detectable resource consumption signature and subsequent scheduled-task creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes consuming >85% sustained CPU or memory over 2+ minute windows originating from temp directory, plugin directory, or loader executables. Cross-correlate with scheduled task creation in same timeframe and lack of known performance baseline for that binary.

suggestion.title: File Masquerade: VBS Execution from PDF-Named Container
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline notes 'VBS script disguised as a PDF document'—a file-type mismatch attack. User expects PDF handler; receives script execution via double-extension or misleading MIME-type attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when wscript.exe or cscript.exe execution is preceded by opening a file with .pdf extension from within an archive, especially if the archive itself has masqueraded filename. Monitor for VBS/WSF execution initiated from archive-extraction sequence.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-56383 Exploitation: DLL Hijacking in Notepad++ v8.8.3
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly cites CVE-2025-56383 as 'DLL hijacking flaw in Notepad++ v8.8.3' exploited in this campaign. Despite vendor claiming 'plugin loading is standard functionality,' plugin directory abuse is a hostile loading scenario when DLL is unsigned or from untrusted source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unsigned DLLs or DLLs with suspicious metadata loaded from Notepad++ plugin directories on v8.8.3 systems. Correlate with process-creation events showing Notepad++ launched from temp directory or archive-extraction context. Check plugin DLL timestamps against application installation and Notepad++ release dates.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with AiTM Proxy Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords include 'Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM)' but no detection logic was generated. AiTM attacks on email typically involve malicious proxies intercepting OAuth flows or credential submission—requires monitoring for redirects to attacker-controlled domains and unusual authentication patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify email messages with URLs pointing to attacker infrastructure masquerading as legitimate OAuth/SSO endpoints, or sign-in events from anomalous geographies immediately following phishing delivery. Look for recipients who clicked suspicious links followed by sign-in failures or MFA challenges from unexpected IPs.

suggestion.title: Bulk Phishing Campaign Detection via Email Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies phishing as core threat vector but pipeline produced no behavioral rules. Standard email threat landscape reporting covers mass-phishing envelope patterns (same subject, sender display-name variations, similar body templates).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect campaigns by clustering emails on subject-line similarity, sender domain (spoofing common orgs), and URL patterns. Baseline legitimate bulk email senders (notifications, alerts) and flag deviations. Correlate click/open telemetry across recipients to identify coordinated phishing waves.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft via HTML Form Injection or Fake Login Pages
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 'Credential theft' but no use case maps detection of injected HTML forms, spoofed login pages in email, or file-based HTML credential harvesters. Q2 2026 trends should address evolved phishing payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTML attachments or links hosting fake login forms mimicking O365, Gmail, or banking portals. Detect credential-submission activity to attacker-controlled endpoints. Correlate file downloads (HTML) with subsequent unusual authentication attempts or password-reset requests from same user.

suggestion.title: Social Engineering via Email: Pretexting & Authority Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Social engineering' but produces no rules for pretexting scenarios (impersonation of executives, vendors, IT). Email social-eng attacks are narrative-driven; behavioral detection focuses on recipient response (credential entry, wire transfer, data-sharing requests).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails impersonating known executives or vendors using display-name spoofing, lookalike domains, or internal email forwarding rules. Flag unusual outbound sharing of sensitive file types (contracts, financial docs) or mailbox forwarding rules set by low-risk users post-phishing delivery.

suggestion.title: Email-to-Endpoint Lateral Movement via Macro/Script Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Email threat landscape articles typically cover post-click payload execution. Pipeline captured zero execution-phase use cases despite phishing+social-eng focus. Missing: Office macro detection, script-block telemetry post-email delivery.

Detect script-block execution or suspicious child processes (rundll32, regsvcs) invoked within 10 minutes of macro-enabled document open.

suggestion.title: Correlation: /api/auth/* 500 error → protected endpoint access with same source/session within 2m
suggestion.rationale: Article states applications checking for 'existence of the auth object' fail open when config produces an error. Detection must correlate the error surfacing with immediate unauthorized access by same actor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify patterns where /api/auth/session or /api/auth/* returns HTTP 500, followed within 2 minutes by same source IP accessing protected routes (e.g., /api/user/*, /dashboard/*, /admin/*) with HTTP 200/302 response, indicating failed auth check was bypassed.

suggestion.title: Auth.js 500-error spike with concurrent increase in protected-route access from external IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article describes configuration errors producing 500s. If a misconfiguration is deployed, auth endpoint failures + surge in external access to protected routes suggests exploitation window opened.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when /api/auth/* endpoint returns 500 (status=500) more than baseline in 1h window AND concurrent external IPs successfully access protected routes with 200/302 status (not normally seen from external source) in same 1h window.

suggestion.title: Application logs: Auth.js config error surfaced + no corresponding HTTP 500 logged (fail-silent pattern)
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates configuration errors cause the auth object to be populated with error. Detection should identify errors in application logs without a corresponding HTTP 500 response to client, suggesting the error was silently swallowed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Auth.js/NextAuth error strings in application logs (MissingSecret, InvalidEndpoints, auth config error) against HTTP response logs, alerting when error is logged but endpoint returned 200/302 instead of 500—indicating silent failure mode.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Token Generation Without Prior Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article core narrative: 'unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token.' Detection must flag token generation via API without corresponding login event.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole token endpoints (/mgmt/session-new, etc.) for successful token issuance lacking prior login success event. Correlate unauthenticated API requests with subsequent valid session tokens from same source IP.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Administrative Operations via Compromised Token
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use it to authenticate with full administrative privileges.' Attacker with admin token will immediately perform privileged actions. Detect admin operations from unusual accounts/sources/timing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on administrative operations (policy pushes, user modifications, gateway reconfigurations) from service accounts, impossible geographic locations, or IPs never previously associated with admin access.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Remote Access Attempts to SmartConsole
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated remote attacker' exploiting public-facing SmartConsole instance. Detect exploitation probes bypassing standard login flow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for direct API calls to SmartConsole admin endpoints without prior authentication, HTTP 401→200 response chains indicating auth bypass, or requests from unexpected external networks to SmartConsole ports (443, 4434).

suggestion.title: Firewall Policy Mass Changes from Single SmartConsole Session
suggestion.rationale: Once attacker gains 'full administrative privileges,' detection must capture impact: bulk policy/rule modifications disabling protections or opening backdoors.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Admin Token Replayed Across Geographies
suggestion.rationale: Article: token can be 'used to authenticate.' Extracted tokens are portable; detect reuse from impossible locations within same session.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate SmartConsole session tokens across requests; alert if same token appears from multiple distinct IP geolocations or exhibits impossible travel times between API calls.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthenticated Token Generation on SmartConsole
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'obtain[s] an application login token' without authentication. Pipeline generated zero UCs for this core attack step.

Flag tokens issued to unauthenticated sessions or with anomalous source IPs, user agents, or request patterns that differ from normal admin access.

Look for admin actions (policy changes, user creation, configuration export) executed immediately after token acquisition.

suggestion.title: Detect Exploitation of CVE-2026-16232 via Abnormal SmartConsole Access Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-16232 and notes federal due-date urgency; pipeline must flag reconnaissance and exploitation attempts against this specific vulnerability in SmartConsole endpoints.

Flag repeated requests with varying payloads, HTTP 401→200 response pairs, or token-generation endpoints accessed without matching login records.

suggestion.title: Detect Abuse of Stolen Admin Tokens for Lateral Movement or Configuration Changes

suggestion.title: Alert on SmartConsole Public Exposure via Vulnerability Scanner / External Scan Detection

suggestion.title: Canary: Monitor SmartConsole for Denial-of-Service or Crash Attempts (Exploitation Probe)
