Correlate token identity against active-user directories; flag tokens associated with disabled/deleted accounts or from external sources.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Remote Access to SmartConsole Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated remote attacker.' Pipeline should detect connection attempts to SmartConsole ports (typically 4434/TCP for SmartConsole server) from external networks that bypass authentication or trigger auth-bypass exploit patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for TCP connections to SmartConsole management ports (4434, 18264) from non-corporate networks or untrusted IP ranges. Alert on exploitation signatures (malformed auth requests, auth-bypass payloads). Correlate with successful token-generation events to detect post-compromise token usage.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Policy Deployment / Config Push from Suspicious Auth Context
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'full administrative privileges.' Once authenticated as admin via stolen token, attacker can push malicious policies or configs. Pipeline should detect policy-change events with admin tokens lacking legitimacy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on policy-deployment or configuration-push events to production firewalls authenticated by tokens issued outside normal change-management windows or by accounts/tokens not on the approved-admin roster. Compare policy-push timestamps and source tokens against CMDB and approved-deployment schedules.

suggestion.title: Cross-Datacenter Admin Token Usage Post-SmartConsole Compromise
suggestion.rationale: SmartConsole token grants access to managed firewalls; article implies lateral movement risk. Pipeline should hunt for admin-authenticated firewall operations from IPs/tokens not previously associated with those assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for administrative commands on managed firewalls (config changes, rule additions, account creation) authenticated via SmartConsole tokens or sessions. Flag operations from source IPs / admin identities with no prior approval or RBAC linkage. Correlate with token-generation anomalies.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Exposed Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article prescribes 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' to find Check Point SmartConsole instances; pipeline generated no inventory or detection rules despite this explicit guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Check Point SmartConsole management console ports (typically 4434/TCP HTTPS), banner-grab to identify version, and correlate with asset inventory. Query proxy/firewall logs for outbound HTTPS connections to known SmartConsole C2 server patterns (e.g., admin.company.com:4434). Enumerate internal Check Point agent callbacks to management plane to build topology of exposed instances.

suggestion.title: Authentication Token Generation Without Login
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'obtain[s] an application login token' without credentials; pipeline missed this core anomaly—token creation must be audited and correlated against login events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point SmartConsole audit logs for admin-level tokens (e.g., session IDs, API keys) issued where no corresponding authentication event precedes them within 1 minute. Flag any token grant at privilege level > user default without a login record. Alert on tokens issued to service accounts or built-in admin IDs without explicit admin-level login request.

suggestion.title: Admin API Calls from Unexpected Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker 'use[s]' token 'with full administrative privileges'; pipeline missed post-compromise lateral movement via stolen admin credentials calling infrastructure management APIs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point SmartConsole API calls (REST or proprietary) made with admin-level tokens. Baseline legitimate admin IPs/hostnames; alert when admin APIs are invoked from IPs outside expected admin workstation ranges, at unusual times, or in rapid succession (bulk queries). Cross-reference suspicious admin API calls with Check Point agent logs to detect infrastructure compromise via token reuse.

suggestion.title: Check Point Vulnerability Scanner Positive + Exposure Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and directs to substitute CVE-2026-16232 into asset-exposure templates; pipeline must tie vuln-scanner hits to network exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Nessus/Qualys/Rapid7 detections of CVE-2026-16232 on Check Point SmartConsole with network reachability proof (inbound port 4434 accessible from untrusted networks). Flag any unpatched instance as exploitable until patch date 2026-07-25 is confirmed installed and verified.

suggestion.title: Check Point Infrastructure Mass-Compromise via Admin Token
suggestion.rationale: Article implies attacker can then use admin token to pivot to managed gateways/agents; pipeline missed detection of bulk infrastructure tampering post token-theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point managed gateways/agents for bulk policy changes, rule modifications, or agent uninstalls originating from a single admin token/session ID. Alert on administrator API calls that target 20+ gateways within minutes, which would indicate mass compromise or lateral movement across the managed firewall estate.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-16232 Scanner Bypass Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states CISA KEV entry means 'currently being exploited'; pipeline should surface attempts to exploit this specific CVE in real-time, not just patch status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point SmartConsole application logs and reverse-proxy logs for payloads known to trigger CVE-2026-16232 (specific API endpoint + malformed request, if public PoC released). Look for 401/403 followed by successful API calls without re-authentication, rapid authentication retry loops, or token-issuing API calls preceded by unauthenticated requests. Correlate with IDS/WAF alerts for known CVE-2026-16232 exploitation signatures.

suggestion.title: Detect n8n Process Spawning Command Interpreters
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'Lets Workflow Editors Run OS Commands as the n8n Process'—any shell spawn (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh) from n8n binary is direct exploitation indicator or malicious workflow execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation events where parent process matches n8n service binary. Flag spawning of shell interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, /bin/sh, sh, csh) or system utilities (whoami, curl, nc, netcat). Establish baseline for legitimate workflow integrations and escalate deviations.

suggestion.title: Detect Workflow Code Injection via API or File Modification
suggestion.rationale: Sandbox escape exploitation requires injecting malicious code into workflow definitions. Article implies 'Workflow Editors' trigger the escape—monitor workflow creation/modification API calls and file writes containing shell syntax or process invocation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor n8n workflow definition files or API audit logs for updates containing suspicious patterns: embedded shell commands (${...}, exec, eval), process invocation keywords, or base64-encoded payloads. Alert on non-standard nodes or expressions executing system calls. Correlate write events with user identity.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized File System Access from n8n Context
suggestion.rationale: Sandbox escape enables the process to access files beyond intended scope. Monitor n8n process reading/writing credential stores, configuration files, or parent directories outside its working directory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of n8n file access patterns. Alert on reads from /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, SAM registry, browser credential stores, SSH keys, or API token files. Flag directory traversal attempts or access to system-level directories (/etc, /opt, C:\\Windows\\System32).

suggestion.title: Detect Privilege Escalation from n8n Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: If n8n runs with elevated privileges or sandbox escape allows token manipulation, attackers escalate from workflow editor to admin. Monitor for privilege escalation techniques initiated from n8n spawned processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for token impersonation, access token duplication, or UAC bypass attempts from n8n child processes. Alert when n8n spawns processes requesting higher privileges than parent. Cross-reference process creation with privilege escalation events and user account context.

suggestion.title: Detect n8n Process Establishing Unexpected Network Connections
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation of sandbox escape typically includes C2 beaconing or data exfiltration. Monitor n8n process for connections to non-whitelisted external IPs, suspicious ports, or known malicious domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of expected n8n egress (API calls to legitimate SaaS integrations). Alert on connections to external IPs not in whitelist, non-standard ports (4444, 5555, 8888, 9999), or known C2 domains. Correlate with workflow execution timestamps to identify payload delivery.

suggestion.title: Detect Anomalous Workflow Execution Frequency and Timing
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation triggers malicious workflows—detect unusual execution frequency, concurrent runs, or execution outside business hours indicating automated compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor n8n execution logs for anomalies: execution outside user's active hours, bulk parallel executions, rapid retry loops, or execution by service account outside normal patterns. Alert on failed authentication followed by workflow execution (compromised credentials). Correlate with API key rotation or credential reset events.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Vulnerable Driver Loading (BYOVD Exploit Pattern)
suggestion.rationale: Article names BYOVD as a core evasion technique; pipeline extracted nothing. BYOVD involves loading legitimate-but-vulnerable drivers to escalate or bypass security controls. Detection hypothesis should target unusual driver loads from non-system directories or unsigned driver loads with suspicious parent processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or out-of-policy driver loads (*.sys files) from temporary, user-writable, or unusual directories. Correlate with process execution from same directory tree or spawned by crypter-staging processes (dropped by initial payload). Flag when legitimate driver names are loaded from non-Windows\System32 paths.

suggestion.title: Process Ghosting Memory/Disk Evasion Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Process Ghosting is explicitly named as an evasion method in the title. This technique unmaps a process's memory backing from disk while maintaining execution, evading static analysis and full-disk scanning. Pipeline failed to suggest detection for this Windows-specific technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation where the on-disk image is deleted or inaccessible immediately after spawning (file unlink concurrent with process birth or before child module loads). Monitor for CreateRemoteThread + NtSetInformationFile(DELETE) patterns. Flag processes where executable path resolves as deleted.

suggestion.title: Cruciferra Crypter File Signature and Behavioral Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Cruciferra Crypter' as a specific malware tool; pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Even without hash indicators in article text, behavioral patterns (crypter-specific PE mutations, obfuscation markers, encryption routines, payload delivery methods) should trigger use-case generation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish file signature detections for known Cruciferra samples (via VirusTotal or threat feeds if hashes published). Behavioral detection: monitor for process execution with suspicious file properties (packed/obfuscated sections, entropy spikes), combined with subsequent driver loading or process hollowing attempts.

suggestion.title: Elevation via Vulnerable Driver with Subsequent Privilege Abuse
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD's purpose is privilege escalation; pipeline did not map the chain from driver-load → privilege-elevation → malware-execution. This is the kill-chain core and central to detecting Cruciferra's attack flow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate process execution of low-integrity or user-mode process → driver load from same session → child process spawned with elevated token or altered DACL. Look for SYSTEM/TrustedInstaller processes launched from unexpected parents after vulnerable driver load in same session tree.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated File Delivery and Staging Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Crypter tools always involve obfuscation/encryption of payloads. Article emphasizes both BYOVD and Process Ghosting for *hiding*—implying payload staging, encryption, and decryption routines. Pipeline generated zero detection use cases for these behavioral indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation with high entropy (packed/encrypted), followed by loading into a parent process's memory, followed by code injection or child execution. Monitor for temporary file staging in user directories with unusual creation/access/delete sequencing (decrypt-in-place pattern).

suggestion.title: Telegram Bot API Calls for C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes Telegram is the C2 channel; this is the primary attack delivery mechanism and should be the lead detection. Detect Telegram API endpoints (api.telegram.org) contacted by unexpected processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process-to-Telegram API communication (api.telegram.org, core.telegram.org). Flag processes outside browser/messaging apps initiating HTTPS to Telegram ports (443, 8443) with bot token patterns in TLS SNI or HTTP headers.

suggestion.title: TELESHIM Executable Characteristics
suggestion.rationale: Article names TELESHIM but pipeline extracted no file hashes, names, or process signatures. Malware family should surface associated hashes and executable metadata from threat feeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline TELESHIM samples by hash and code-signing characteristics. Alert on execution of unsigned PE files matching TELESHIM signatures, or on processes spawning with command-line tokens matching Telegram bot patterns.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Telegram Messages
suggestion.rationale: Attacks against government imply data theft; Telegram C2 typically exfiltrates via encrypted messages. Article context ('attacks against Middle East governments') suggests espionage objective but no exfiltration detection surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes writing credential files, registry hives, or documents immediately before initiating Telegram API connections. Flag for high-volume message sends to single Telegram chat ID that correlate with sensitive data access.

suggestion.title: Initial Access via Spear Phishing or Watering Hole
suggestion.rationale: Article title does not detail initial compromise vector explicitly in truncated body, but C2-centric attacks require initial infection. Pipeline should have surface techniques even if delivery mechanism unclear from title alone.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate government-sector email with macro-enabled documents, suspicious links, or weaponized PDFs. Alert on Office process spawning unusual children (cmd, powershell, rundll32) that subsequently contact external C2.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Unauthenticated Token Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token' — this is the exploit and should be directly detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole authentication logs for login tokens issued without preceding successful authentication or from unauthenticated API endpoints. Flag token generation where the originating request lacks valid credentials.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Admin-Privileged Token Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Attack flow explicitly: 'use it to authenticate with full administrative privileges' — privilege escalation via token must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect assignment of full admin privileges to SmartConsole tokens that originated unauthenticated or from anomalous sources. Flag admin-level actions performed by tokens created outside normal provisioning workflows.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-16232 Vulnerability Presence
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly instructs: 'match against your vulnerability scanner' — standard asset-exposure hunt per template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner data for CVE-2026-16232 matches against SmartConsole instances. Cross-correlate with patch status and federal remediation deadline of 2026-07-25 to identify non-compliant assets.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Internet Exposure Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: KEV status implies 'active exploitation against exposed assets' — internet-facing SmartConsole is the attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate SmartConsole instances with inbound access from untrusted networks (internet-routable addresses). Flag any externally-accessible SmartConsole running vulnerable versions without WAF/EDR protection.

suggestion.title: Anomalous SmartConsole Administrative Actions Post-Token Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Attack persists via token reuse with 'full administrative privileges' — detect admin actions anomalous to normal baselines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal SmartConsole admin action patterns. Detect admin-level configuration changes, user provisioning, or policy modifications performed by tokens with suspicious acquisition (unauthenticated origin, non-US geolocation for federal environments).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated SmartConsole Admin Token Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'obtain[s] an application login token and use[s] it to authenticate with full administrative privileges' without legitimate credentials — core exploitation pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole authentication endpoints for token generation requests lacking standard credential exchange (username/password POST, certificate validation, etc.). Look for token issuance followed immediately by administrative API calls. Baseline legitimate token patterns first; anomalies = exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Exposed SmartConsole Public-Facing Service Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote attacker' and 'public-facing application' — exploitation requires network exposure. Scanning/enumeration of exposed ports is prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Proactively scan for publicly routable SmartConsole services (TCP 443 on typical Check Point ports; banner identifies SmartConsole). Correlate with vulnerability scanner data for unpatched instances. Alert on any new public exposure of SmartConsole.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Authentication Bypass Token
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attacker gaining 'full administrative privileges' after token theft — privilege escalation without role-based access control enforcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track token lifecycle: when a token issued from unauthenticated or low-privilege context is used to execute administrative operations (user/group management, policy changes, configuration export). Baseline legitimate admin paths; deviations indicate token hijacking.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole CVE-2026-16232 Exploitation Attempt Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Generic exploitation signature for known-exploited CVE — CISA KEV indicates active weaponization; organizations need signature-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS payloads targeting SmartConsole authentication endpoints with patterns known to bypass validation (missing/malformed auth headers, token injection into request parameters, etc.). Correlate with CVE-2026-16232 PoC indicators if available. Flag all attempts regardless of success.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Auth Bypass: Unauthenticated Token Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token.' Core exploitation step requires detection on SmartConsole auth service logs for tokens issued without valid credential exchange.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point SmartConsole authentication service for token issuance events where the requesting principal is unauthenticated or lacks credentials. Flag token generation to null/empty identities or rapid-fire token requests from anonymous sources.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation: Unauthenticated to Admin Session
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use it to authenticate with full administrative privileges.' This is explicit privilege escalation from no auth to admin; must alert on unexpected admin session creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect administrative session creation in SmartConsole originating from unauthenticated or untrusted callers. Alert when a session's privilege level exceeds the authenticated identity's assigned role or when admin grants are issued outside normal workflow.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Check Point SmartConsole Internet-Facing
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires 'remote attacker' network access. KEV active-exploitation context implies public-facing SmartConsole instances; asset inventory must identify these.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan asset inventory and configurations to identify Check Point SmartConsole instances listening on public-facing IPs or accessible from untrusted networks. Cross-reference with threat intel feeds for active exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: Alternate Auth: Stolen Token Usage
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'obtain an application login token and use it to authenticate.' Attacker uses stolen/obtained token as alternate authentication material for lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole API and management interface logs for authentication using tokens that originated from unauthenticated or exploited auth flows. Correlate token creation timestamps with subsequent API calls; alert on token reuse from unexpected geographic IPs.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Detection: CVE-2026-16232 Attack Traffic
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation means active wild exploitation. Network and IDS logs should contain exploitation attempts exploiting CVE-2026-16232 improper authentication flaw.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate inbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic to SmartConsole authentication endpoints with known exploit payloads for CVE-2026-16232 authentication bypass. Flag requests using malformed auth headers, null credentials, or known bypass parameters.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scan: CVE-2026-16232 Unpatched Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-16232 — match against your vulnerability scanner' with federal patch due 2026-07-25. VulnMgmt systems must flag any unpatched instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanning tools for CVE-2026-16232 findings on Check Point SmartConsole. Flag any unpatched systems with exposure older than federal due date as compliance violation and immediate remediation requirement.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-16232 Token Issuance to Unauthenticated Clients
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token' — this is the exploitation vector and must be detectable
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point SmartConsole for API endpoints (/api/login, /auth/token, /api/admin) issuing authentication tokens (Bearer tokens, session cookies, JWT) to requests originating from unauthenticated or external-network sources. Correlate token issuance with absence of prior multi-factor authentication events.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Administrative Privilege Escalation via Stolen Token
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use it to authenticate with full administrative privileges' — exploitation pivots from initial token theft to admin abuse
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SmartConsole administrative actions (policy writes, user provisioning, credential changes) performed by newly-minted tokens originating from external IPs or unauthenticated sessions. Look for token reuse patterns: token issued <5 min prior to high-risk admin API call.

suggestion.title: Unpatched CVE-2026-16232 Exploitation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CISA KEV 'currently being exploited' with federal due date 2026-07-25 — need active scanning correlation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner results (unpatched Check Point SmartConsole < fix version) with network telemetry showing unauthenticated token requests to those same hosts. Exclude patched systems from hunt; prioritize hosts that fail patch-status queries but show active token-issuance patterns.

suggestion.title: Remote Administrative Access Without Prior MFA Enrollment
suggestion.rationale: Article describes authentication bypass entirely; SmartConsole admin access should always require MFA but exploited token bypasses this
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag SmartConsole administrative sessions where (a) session token originates from public internet, (b) no MFA event precedes authentication, (c) administrative actions occur from unexpected geolocation, or (d) token lifetime/issuance timestamp indicates synthetic generation outside normal auth flow.

suggestion.title: Asset-Exposure Hunting: SmartConsole Internet-Facing Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article cites template [`../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`](../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure) — standard CISA KEV hunt is required
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all Check Point SmartConsole instances for external-facing ports (TCP 443, 8443, 19009 default); cross-reference with vulnerability scanner to identify unpatched versions. Measure exposure window: patch-due date 2026-07-25 means active exploitation window likely 2026-07-22 onward (KEV publish date).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated SmartConsole Token Issuance
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token.' Pipeline generated zero token-related detections. Need UC monitoring SmartConsole authentication endpoints for successful token grants missing auth validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole token endpoints (/api/login, /auth, service ports) for successful auth responses (HTTP 200, token granted) lacking prior credential submission or POST body. Cross-reference source IPs against known-user login geography and timing. Flag any token issuance where auth-step logs are absent or timestamps show auth bypass.

suggestion.title: Admin Action via Fraudulent SmartConsole Token
suggestion.rationale: Article: '...use it to authenticate with full administrative privileges.' Pipeline missed detection for privilege-escalation via token abuse. Need UC correlating admin-level API calls to SmartConsole with tokens issued without proper validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate token creation timestamp against first admin-action timestamp; if <2 seconds apart and token issuer logs show no auth challenge, flag as privilege escalation. Monitor for admin config changes (policy deploy, user creation, permission grant) where source token cannot be traced to valid auth event.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole CVE-2026-16232 Exploitation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists vulnerability by CVE ID; pipeline returned zero CVE-specific IOCs. Need UC matching exploitation signatures for this auth-bypass vulnerability in vulnerability scanner results, IDS/WAF logs, and proxy records.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all SmartConsole instances (product version, endpoints) against CVE-2026-16232 patch status. Monitor network traffic to SmartConsole ports/endpoints for request patterns consistent with unauthenticated token-request exploitation (rapid sequential auth calls, error-response chains typical of bruteforce/bypass attempts).

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Service Exposure & Asset Inventory Reconciliation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal due-date' and 'patch lag is the silent killer' require asset-level detection. Pipeline omitted network-exposure hunting despite this being the canonical initial-access vector for public-facing app exploits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all internet-routable SmartConsole instances (port 8285, 443 + SmartConsole User Interface cert strings, X-SmartConsole-* headers in HTTP responses). Cross-check against patch inventory; flag instances where version is pre-2026-07-25 patches. Generate alert for any external network access to SmartConsole ports from non-VPN sources.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Auth Log Anomalies & Token Validation Failures
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'improper authentication validation' logic flaw. Pipeline missed application-log-level detection for auth-engine failures. Need UC for auth-log patterns indicating exploit triggering.
log_sources: OS syslog (if SmartConsole logs to syslog)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search SmartConsole logs for auth failures followed by token-grant (contradictory state), or log messages indicating 'null auth', 'validation bypass', 'unauthenticated token'. Count auth-reject→token-grant pairs per source IP; if count > threshold in 5-min window, flag as exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Lateral Movement Post-Admin Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'full administrative privileges' on SmartConsole opens lateral movement to managed firewalls/infrastructure. Pipeline ignored post-compromise hunting. Need UC for suspicious SmartConsole admin commands targeting downstream security appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole policy-deploy and config-sync logs for deployments initiated <5 minutes after CVE-2026-16232 exploitation indicators (token issuance anomaly). Flag any policy changes that open firewall rules, disable logging, or push reverse shells to managed gateways.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Unauthenticated Token Issuance
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'obtain an application login token' without authentication. Pipeline missed the core exploit mechanism entirely. Log source: SmartConsole authentication/API logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole authentication endpoints for token issuance (successful session creation, JWT generation, OAuth tokens) originating from unauthenticated or anonymous sources. Correlate token issue timestamps with failed authentication attempts from the same IP. Flag any tokens issued without a corresponding login attempt or LDAP/RADIUS validation.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Unauthorized Administrative Privilege Grant
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states token 'authenticate[s] with full administrative privileges' without proper authorization. Pipeline missed privilege-escalation codification entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole role assignment and privilege escalation events. Flag cases where administrative roles (full admin, policy admin, etc.) are granted to user accounts that lack corresponding directory/identity-store permissions, or where privilege escalation occurs without an approved change request. Alert on 'admin role grant' events missing a corresponding RBAC policy update.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Successful Authentication After Failed Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Improper authentication vulnerability implies attackers bypass standard login validation. Look for anomalous auth patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole for sequences: N failed authentication attempts from IP A, immediately followed by successful session creation from IP A, especially with admin token. Baseline normal auth failure rates; alert when exceeded before success.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole API Calls from Unauthenticated Session Origin
suggestion.rationale: Article describes obtaining 'application login token' suggesting token-based API abuse. Pipeline did not model post-exploitation reconnaissance or command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole API calls (policy queries, object retrieval, configuration export) that originate from tokens issued by the authentication bypass. Establish baseline of normal SmartConsole API patterns; flag high-volume policy/object enumeration or export attempts from newly-created admin tokens, especially from external IPs.

suggestion.title: External Remote Access to SmartConsole Without VPN/Proxy
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-16232 affects 'public-facing application' exposed to remote, unauthenticated attackers. T1133 (External Remote Services) is implicit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify SmartConsole instances exposed directly to the internet (not behind VPN/corporate proxy). Monitor for authentication attempts from non-corporate IP ranges or countries with no legitimate business activity. Flag first-time access from new external IPs that immediately obtain or escalate privileges.

suggestion.title: CloudTrail Kiro Configuration Change Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Title phrase 'Rewrite Its Config' establishes attacker moves to configuration tampering after web compromise. Requires detection of API calls modifying Kiro state without legitimate authorization context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PutConfiguration, UpdateSettings, or equivalent Kiro API calls originating from web-compromised hosts or lacking expected IAM role context. Correlate with preceding suspicious web access or process execution events.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Code Execution in Kiro Service Boundary
suggestion.rationale: Title phrase 'Run Code' after web compromise requires execution detection. Exploit likely achieves code execution within Kiro process space or related compute context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process spawning, Lambda invocations, or remote code execution events within Kiro service contexts, particularly those initiated by web-facing services or lacking explicit administrator approval.

suggestion.title: Drive-by Compromise: Malicious Web Payload Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Title phrase 'Poisoned Web Page' identifies attack vector. Requires detection of web-based payload delivery mechanisms targeting Kiro.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for access to attacker-controlled domains, malicious script execution in browser context, or suspicious HTTP responses that deliver Kiro-targeting exploits. Flag anomalous JavaScript execution or iframe injection patterns.

suggestion.title: Kiro Authentication Bypass or Authorization Boundary Violation
suggestion.rationale: Phrase 'Poisoned Web Page Rewrite Its Config' implies unauthenticated or cross-boundary modification of protected resources—suggests auth/authz bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track configuration changes without corresponding IAM policy authorization, failed authentication spikes followed by successful privileged API calls, and cross-account or cross-role access patterns that violate expected Kiro boundaries.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Unauthenticated Token Acquisition
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker can 'obtain an application login token' without authentication. Core attack primitive requiring monitoring for successful token issuance without prior credential submission.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point SmartConsole authentication logs for login tokens issued without corresponding username/password authentication events. Track API tokens or session tokens generated from requests lacking credential submission. Alert on token acquisition from unexpected source IPs, especially external/non-enterprise ranges.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Admin Privilege Escalation via Token
suggestion.rationale: Article states obtained token grants 'full administrative privileges' to unauthenticated attacker. This privilege escalation without approval/elevation request is the immediate post-exploitation impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect accounts or service principals gaining SmartConsole admin roles immediately after token generation, especially accounts without prior admin entitlements. Flag admin-level API calls or configuration changes authenticated by newly-generated tokens. Cross-reference token creation timestamp with privilege grant timestamp.

suggestion.title: Exposed SmartConsole Public Network Access
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'public-facing application' as prerequisite for exploitation. Detection should identify SmartConsole admin interfaces reachable from external networks or lacking network segmentation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Check Point SmartConsole management interfaces (typically ports 4434/HTTPS) accessible from untrusted networks. Alert on successful connection establishment to SmartConsole from non-enterprise IP ranges or known proxy/VPN exit points. Correlate network exposure with authentication failure spikes.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Authentication Bypass Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is categorized as 'improper authentication'—authentication mechanism itself is broken, not just weak. Detection should capture bypass or circumvention patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole logs for successful authentication events that lack expected credential validation markers (no password hash comparisons, no MFA challenges, no 2FA logs). Track HTTP/API requests that return valid session tokens without traversing normal login endpoints. Flag 401 → 200 sequences that skip credential submission.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-16232 Vulnerability Scanner Lag
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal patch deadline 2026-07-25. Pipeline should flag instances where vulnerability scanner reports 'not vulnerable' but firmware/patch dates indicate exposure window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results against Check Point SmartConsole asset inventory. Alert on scanner misses (reported as patched or N/A) when actual firmware version falls within CVE-2026-16232 vulnerable range. Identify instances past federal deadline (2026-07-25) still running vulnerable builds.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Unauthenticated Token Acquisition Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token.' Pipeline generated zero detections for auth bypass or token generation from nulled/missing credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST/GET requests to SmartConsole authentication endpoints (login, token-grant, session-init) that succeed (200 OK, token in response, Set-Cookie) despite missing or invalid Authorization headers, Basic auth credentials, or session cookies. Flag if response contains valid session token.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Admin Privilege Escalation from Stolen Token
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use it to authenticate with full administrative privileges.' Stolen tokens will immediately be exercised for admin actions (policy changes, user creation, config modification). Pipeline did not generate UC for privilege escalation or anomalous admin activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful SmartConsole authentication followed within 60 seconds by administrative operations (user/object creation, policy modify, system reconfig) where the authenticated session does not have prior logged-in history, originates from unexpected geography/ASN, or corresponds to a known service account that should not perform admin actions.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Exposed Instance Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV explicitly states 'observed exploited in wild'—attackers are scanning external networks for exposed SmartConsole. Article implies public-facing risk ('unauthenticated remote attacker'). No asset inventory UC present.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Check Point SmartConsole instances reachable from untrusted networks (external IPs, VPN, cloud providers). Correlate with patch status for CVE-2026-16232 (published 2026-07-22, federal due 2026-07-25). Flag any unpatched instance or instance lacking firewall ingress restrictions.

suggestion.title: Anomalous SmartConsole Authentication Token Reuse
suggestion.rationale: Stolen tokens will be replayed or reused from attacker infrastructure. Article describes token misuse; pipeline generated zero behavioral detections for token anomalies (IP hop, geographic impossibility, time gap).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For each valid SmartConsole authentication token, detect reuse across different source IPs, impossible travel (e.g., same token used from US and China within 120 seconds), or usage outside normal business hours by known service accounts. Correlate source IPs against threat feeds and geoIP databases.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole CVE-2026-16232 Patch Compliance Check
suggestion.rationale: Article stresses 'patch lag is the silent killer' and sets federal due date 2026-07-25. No compliance or patch-status detection UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all Check Point SmartConsole instances across the environment, verify installed version against patched release for CVE-2026-16232. Alert if any instance is pre-patch and internet-reachable. Track patch installation completion and flag any instance still unpatched after federal due date 2026-07-25.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated authentication token acquisition attempt against SmartConsole
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token'—this is the primary attack mechanism and must be detectable via web logs or API audit trails showing token issuance without prior authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole web service logs for token generation (login endpoint responses) that lack corresponding authentication success events or originate from unexpected IP ranges. Look for repeated 401→200 sequences or abnormal bearer-token issuance patterns preceding privileged API calls.

suggestion.title: Administrative privilege escalation via obtained SmartConsole authentication token
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'use[s] it to authenticate with full administrative privileges'—detection should focus on admin-level operations performed immediately after suspicious token generation or from previously-unauthorized sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious token acquisition with downstream administrative operations (user/policy changes, rule modifications, system reconfiguration). Flag tokens that perform privileged actions without corresponding interactive login sessions or from IPs not in admin allowlists.

suggestion.title: Failed SmartConsole authentication bypass probe attempts
suggestion.rationale: Threat actors will probe for the auth bypass; the article implies exploitation is possible, so detection must include attack attempts even before successful token acquisition. Look for repeated auth manipulation or protocol-level probing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated requests to SmartConsole auth endpoints with malformed credentials, missing auth headers, or known CVE-2026-16232 payload signatures. Spike in 401/403 responses followed by successful token issuance from same source is high-fidelity indicator.

suggestion.title: Post-exploitation suspicious administrative commands in SmartConsole
suggestion.rationale: Once attacker has admin token, they will modify firewall policies, rules, or user accounts. The article does not specify exploitation payloads post-token-acquisition, but defenders should detect anomalous admin activity following token compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect administrative configuration changes (firewall rules, admin accounts, network policies) occurring within seconds/minutes of suspicious token acquisition. Flag bulk or unusual policy modifications originating from external IPs or off-hours access patterns.

suggestion.title: Release Tag Retroactive Reassignment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit, which was the orphaned commit. The attacker re-pointed several existing release tags to their malicious commit.' This is the core obfuscation technique and should trigger alerts on tag history changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when release tags (v*.*.* pattern) are reassigned to commits not on main/master branches or when tag commit history changes retroactively. Correlate with recent repository writes to identify coordinated tag moves within short timeframes.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit Reference in Workflow Runners
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes orphaned commits as key enabling factor: 'Having the attack commit orphaned from any branches, including the main branch.' When workflow uses action@<hash> or @tag pointing to orphaned commit, it bypasses normal branch-based code review.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions execution logs for commits not reachable via `git log <any-branch>`. Flag when workflows reference commits that exist in git but have no branch ancestry. Cross-reference against scheduled release dates.

suggestion.title: Secrets Exposure in Public GitHub Action Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article core impact: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit that caused encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs. This could lead to a devastating breach on a public repo.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions workflow logs for patterns matching AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, private_key, token=, GITHUB_TOKEN patterns. Alert when secrets appear in logs of public repositories or when log retention extended beyond normal policy.

suggestion.title: Unexpected External Network Call from GitHub Actions Runner
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTP(S) requests from GitHub Actions runners to non-whitelisted external IPs/domains during workflow execution. Correlate with workflow file changes in same repository. Alert on DNS queries for newly-registered or suspicious domains from runner IPs.

suggestion.title: Write Permission Grant to CI/CD Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article prerequisite: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo' and 'it's unknown why the attacker had write permissions on the repo.' Detection should flag anomalous permission elevation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on write permission grants to widely-used GitHub Action repositories. Flag if granted to newly-created accounts, inactive accounts re-activated, or accounts outside expected organization zones. Correlate with subsequent commit/tag changes.

suggestion.title: Mass Action Version Pinning Changes
suggestion.rationale: 23,000 repositories reference this action; pipeline should track when these dependents shift from stable tags to commit hashes or vice versa, or when downstream repos suddenly fail action validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub search/API for workflow files referencing tj-actions/changed-files. Alert when version pinning diverges dramatically across fleet (e.g., 23k repos suddenly all pin to same commit hash). Correlate with GitHub Actions execution failures.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Token Issuance to SmartConsole
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'obtain an application login token' without authentication credentials. This is the core exploit and must be hunted as anomalous auth flow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for session/token creation in SmartConsole without corresponding successful credential validation. Monitor for unauthenticated HTTP requests to /api/login, /auth/token, or equivalent endpoints that return valid administrative session tokens.

suggestion.title: Administrative Action via Unauthenticated-Origin Token
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'use it to authenticate with full administrative privileges'—privilege escalation via stolen/obtained token is the impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate tokens flagged as improperly-obtained with downstream administrative actions (policy modifications, rule changes, account creation). Alert on admin API calls using sessions that lack authenticated origin.

suggestion.title: Remote Exploitation of SmartConsole Public Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated remote attacker' accessing the application, confirming public-facing exposure and T1190 exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to Check Point SmartConsole ports (443, 8080, 8181 typical) originating from external/untrusted networks. Alert on patterns targeting token or authentication endpoints before successful user login.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole CVE-2026-16232 Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requires asset exposure hunt—CVE-2026-16232 is the direct vulnerability and must be cross-referenced against deployed inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset databases for Check Point SmartConsole. Confirm patch status for CVE-2026-16232. Perform HTTP banner grabs on suspected instances to detect version mismatches (scanner says patched but banner shows vulnerable version).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Token Issuance to SmartConsole
suggestion.rationale: Article core mechanic: attacker 'obtain[s] an application login token' without credentials. Detecting token generation outside normal auth flows is the foundational detection for this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole token-issuance endpoints (login, token-grant APIs) for successful responses where no preceding authentication event exists. Correlate token generation timestamps against auth service logs to surface tokens issued to unauthenticated sessions.

suggestion.title: Admin Actions via Hijacked Login Token
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker 'use[s] it to authenticate with full administrative privileges'—once token is compromised, privileged operations follow without legitimate auth context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag admin-level actions (policy changes, rule creation, credential updates) in SmartConsole where acting session lacks corresponding authentication records or where token was issued outside normal auth flow. Alert on API requests using valid tokens from IPs with no prior login event.

suggestion.title: Remote Exploitation of SmartConsole (T1190)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated remote attacker'—the attack vector itself (remote, no creds, public-facing) is the T1190 exploitation point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate remote connection attempts to SmartConsole against subsequent token-issuance events with no auth session in between. Flag clusters of failed auth followed by successful token grants from the same source IP.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole Internet-Facing Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV exploitation requires SmartConsole externally reachable. Article itself directs to 'asset-exposure hunt' as canonical detection—inventory and exposure monitoring is mandatory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit firewall rules and VPN configs to confirm Check Point SmartConsole is never directly exposed on public IPs. Cross-reference internal asset inventory against public scanning data (Shodan, Censys) to surface unintended exposure.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Unauthenticated Token Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'allow[s] an unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token.' No hunt surfaces token issuance without preceding credential submission.
log_sources: SIEM auth events tagged with SmartConsole
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag token-generation or token-issuance events lacking a corresponding prior authentication event. Check for authentication success or privilege elevation events where the source principal is undefined, 'null', or 'unauthenticated'. This CVE allows token issue without login ceremony.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Admin Privilege Grant to Unauthenticated Session
suggestion.rationale: Attack flow grants 'full administrative privileges' via the stolen token. Detect where admin roles or permissions are assigned to non-admin or unauthenticated principals in SmartConsole.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on administrative permission assignments to principals lacking prior admin role or where the assigning principal cannot be correlated to a legitimate admin account. Cross-reference token generation logs—if a token was issued without auth, then used for admin access within seconds, raise severity.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole Public Exploitation Attempts (CVE-2026-16232)
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status confirms active exploitation. Hunt for scanning, connection attempts, or known exploit payloads targeting SmartConsole endpoints from external sources or known threat IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP/HTTPS requests to SmartConsole default ports (443, possibly 18211) from external IP ranges with patterns consistent with exploitation: unusual User-Agent strings, authentication bypass payloads, or rapid token-endpoint requests. Cross-reference against public exploit PoCs and threat feeds.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Login Token Usage from Non-Originating IP
suggestion.rationale: Stolen tokens may be replayed from different source IPs. Detect token reuse patterns inconsistent with the originating connection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate token issuance IP with token usage IP. Flag significant geographic, ASN, or timing mismatches between token generation and token redemption, especially for administrative operations.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated SmartConsole Token Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token' — direct indicator of improper authentication check allowing token issuance without credential submission.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole token endpoints for successful token generation events with no preceding credential submission or valid session in the prior 60 seconds. Alert on token issuance from IP/geolocation never before seen issuing tokens.

suggestion.title: Admin Authentication Without Credential Entry — SmartConsole
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker obtaining token and using it to 'authenticate with full administrative privileges' — detection should flag admin-level logins not preceded by password entry, MFA challenge, or known session resumption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate SmartConsole authentication logs: alert on admin login event where the originating IP has no matching credential submission (password, certificate, MFA) event in the preceding 120 seconds. Cross-reference with token issuance logs if available.

suggestion.title: Anomalous SmartConsole Token Reuse for Administrative Actions
suggestion.rationale: Stolen tokens obtained via the improper auth flaw will be reused across multiple administrative changes; baseline normal token lifespan and identify outliers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of token reuse patterns in SmartConsole logs. Alert when a single token is observed performing multiple administrative policy changes, user management actions, or firewall rule modifications within 30 minutes or from geographically improbable locations.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Public Internet Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: CVE requires remote unauthenticated access; article references T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) — detect SmartConsole instances exposed to untrusted networks without protective controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for publicly routable SmartConsole instances (typically ports 443, 4434; TLS cert CN patterns matching SmartConsole; HTTP headers revealing Check Point software). Cross-reference with asset inventory for unsanctioned exposure; flag instances not behind VPN, WAF, or network segmentation.

suggestion.title: Failed SmartConsole Auth Followed by Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Improper auth implementation may leak tokens or allow reuse after failed attempts; pattern indicates exploitation of the flaw rather than legitimate admin activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for: (1) multiple failed login attempts to SmartConsole followed by successful admin action from same IP within 5 minutes, or (2) single request resulting in both failed auth log and successful token generation, or (3) admin action immediately after unauthenticated network connection with no credential submission event.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Login Token Issuance from SmartConsole
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token' — core detection gap. Look for token generation without preceding authentication events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point SmartConsole for authentication tokens (session IDs, JWT, bearer tokens) issued without a corresponding login event in the prior 5 minutes. Flag any token assignment to accounts with admin privileges when no authentication attempt precedes it.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Administrative Access via Unvalidated Token
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use it to authenticate with full administrative privileges' — direct privilege-escalation detection. Monitor for admin actions without expected authentication pre-requisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when administrative actions (policy changes, user creation, permission escalation) originate from sessions that lack a validated authentication event or whose token age predates the user's logon time.

suggestion.title: Remote Exploitation of Exposed SmartConsole Instance
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated remote attacker' + CISA KEV implies active targeting of internet-facing instances. Detect C2 or scanning attempts on SmartConsole ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate multiple failed authentication attempts or connection probes to SmartConsole listening ports (default 443, 18190) from external IPs in a 10-minute window. Cross-check against patch status; flagged by CISA means active exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Auth Token Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article core vector: 'unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token.' This is the vulnerability itself and must surface as primary detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole logs for authentication token/session creation events with null or missing user identity fields, or token generation via endpoints that should require pre-authentication. Cross-check external IP sources initiating token requests.

suggestion.title: Admin Actions from Newly-Acquired Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use it to authenticate with full administrative privileges.' Admin operations immediately following token acquisition from untrusted sources = privilege escalation abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect administrative actions (policy deployment, user/rule creation, security changes) performed by accounts with token acquisition events within preceding 5 minutes, especially if account has no prior SmartConsole history.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Access from External Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated remote attacker.' Asset-exposure hunt requires external connection detection to administrative console.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify successful network connections to SmartConsole ports (443, 4434) from IPs outside expected management network ranges, particularly those resulting in TLS completion and HTTP requests to auth endpoints.

suggestion.title: Auth Failure Spike Before Token Theft
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation of improper auth will generate failed attempts prior to token acquisition; KEV status implies scanning and attempted exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on 10+ authentication failures from single external IP within 5-minute window followed by successful token generation from same source within subsequent 10 minutes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-16232 Vulnerability Inventory Drift
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV articles recommend scanning; federal patch due date (2026-07-25) creates compliance and exploitation-risk indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query scanners for CVE-2026-16232 matches on SmartConsole systems. Flag unpatched instances after federal due date (2026-07-25) as priority remediation and potential breach indicators.

suggestion.title: Detect SmartConsole Unauthenticated Token Acquisition
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token' — core indicator of exploitation is token generation without prior authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to SmartConsole authentication endpoints (ports 443, 4434) where responses contain valid session tokens (Set-Cookie, Authorization headers) but source IP has no corresponding prior TLS handshake, SSL client certificate, or known-good authentication sequence. Baseline legitimate token patterns and alert on structural deviations.

suggestion.title: Detect SmartConsole Exposure to External Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation against 'public-facing application' — detection for SmartConsole reachable from non-corporate IP space.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound traffic to SmartConsole ports (443, 4434) originating from external IPs (non-RFC1918, residential ISP ranges, cloud providers). Cross-correlate with public-asset scans (Shodan, Censys, Internet-wide NVD queries) to identify SmartConsole banners on unexpected internet-routable assets.

suggestion.title: Detect Admin-Level Actions via Exploited Token
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'use it to authenticate with full administrative privileges' — exploitation success is measured by admin-account activity anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag login events to SmartConsole admin/root accounts from unexpected geolocations, times, or authentication protocols (token-based outside baseline). Correlate with admin-level policy changes, user provisioning, or configuration exports occurring within 5 minutes of token acquisition.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-16232 Presence in Asset Vulnerability Scans
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal mandatory patch deadline 2026-07-25 — must verify patch status across SmartConsole inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner API for detections of CVE-2026-16232. Prioritize findings on externally-routable SmartConsole instances. Alert on instances with 'vulnerable' status persisting past federal deadline (2026-07-25) or appearing after patch release.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole: Unauthenticated Token Generation Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states unauthenticated attacker 'obtain[s] an application login token.' This is the core exploitation technique and must be hunted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole for authentication tokens issued without a preceding successful user login session. Flag token-generation events where source IP, user account, or authentication method is anomalous or absent.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole: Administrative Action via Compromised Token
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker using stolen token to 'authenticate with full administrative privileges.' Detect admin actions following token misuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when administrative API calls (policy writes, user account changes, configuration edits) are executed within minutes of an anomalous token issuance, or from unexpected source IPs/user agents associated with that token.

suggestion.title: Internet-Facing SmartConsole Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated remote attacker,' implying externally-exposed SmartConsole. CISA KEV exploitation is in-the-wild; active reconnaissance for exposed instances is expected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for SmartConsole instances on internet-routable addresses (default ports 8123, 44333). Cross-check firewall rules—any externally accessible SmartConsole is critical and exploitable via CVE-2026-16232.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Authentication Bypass Probing
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'improper authentication'—attackers probe the bypass before exploitation. Look for failed auth patterns followed by exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated requests to SmartConsole authentication endpoints with missing/malformed credentials, followed by successful token issuance. Spikes in 401/403 responses preceding token generation indicate bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Token Refresh Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Exploited tokens will show suspicious refresh behavior (rapid reuse, unexpected source IPs, out-of-hours activity) after compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag rapid token refresh cycles or geographic-impossibility patterns (token issued from IP A, refreshed from IP B with impossible latency). Correlate with admin API activity.

suggestion.title: Detect CVE-2026-50522 Exploitation Attempts Against SharePoint
suggestion.rationale: Article headline and body explicitly establish this as 'Critical SharePoint RCE CVE-2026-50522 Under Active Exploitation'—the core attack vector. No use case generated despite active in-the-wild exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SharePoint servers for HTTP requests matching known CVE-2026-50522 exploitation signatures (malformed requests to vulnerable endpoints, encoded payloads in request body/headers). Correlate with w3wp.exe spawning child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe). Alert on any successful code execution post-attempt.

suggestion.title: Detect Public PoC Staging and Mass Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'After Public PoC'—this signals imminent mass exploitation. Pipeline missed reconnaissance-phase detection despite article's emphasis on PoC availability driving active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify downloads of CVE-2026-50522 PoC repositories from GitHub or pastebin. Monitor for repeated failed HTTP requests to SharePoint endpoints consistent with PoC scanning patterns. Alert on rapid-fire requests from single source across multiple internal SharePoint instances.

suggestion.title: Detect Anomalous Child Process Execution from SharePoint Application Pool
suggestion.rationale: RCE exploitation of w3wp.exe will result in execution of shell processes. Pipeline omitted post-exploitation execution behavioral detection despite clear RCE impact statement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on w3wp.exe or mssharepoint process spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, cscript.exe, or other interpreters. Establish baseline of legitimate child processes per environment. Correlate process execution timeline with suspicious HTTP activity to SharePoint in preceding minutes.

suggestion.title: Detect SharePoint Vulnerability Scanner Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Public PoC release generates automated scanning; article's 'active exploitation' context implies reconnaissance activity. Pipeline failed to model threat-actor scanning phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests bearing PoC-specific User-Agents, parameter injection patterns, or error responses typical of vulnerability scanning attempts. Detect repeated probing of SharePoint default paths and endpoints across non-prod or dev instances.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated SmartConsole Authentication Token Acquisition
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token and use it to authenticate with full administrative privileges' — core attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole authentication logs for admin token generation without preceding successful user login. Detect API calls to authentication endpoints originating from unauthenticated sources. Flag sessions assigned administrative privileges without credential validation in the audit trail.

suggestion.title: Exposed SmartConsole Public Internet Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'public-facing application' exploitation via T1190 — requires internet-routable SmartConsole instance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Check Point SmartConsole instances accessible from untrusted networks via port scanning or vulnerability scanner telemetry. Cross-reference internet-reachable SmartConsole ports against approved management network ranges. Alert on unexpected internet exposure of SmartConsole services.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Admin Privilege Escalation without Credential Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'full administrative privileges' granted to unauthenticated requester — privilege escalation is the attack outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect role/privilege elevation in SmartConsole where the authenticated user/token lacks corresponding credential validation records. Monitor audit logs for administrative access grants following unauthenticated or failed authentication attempts. Flag admin actions by sessions missing login history.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-16232 Exploitation Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status indicates active wild exploitation — detection must cover exploitation attempts and successful compromises.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole access logs for HTTP request patterns matching known CVE-2026-16232 exploitation techniques (malformed auth requests, direct token API calls, unauthenticated privilege-escalation endpoints). Correlate exploitation signatures with successful token acquisitions to confirm compromise.

suggestion.title: Anomalous SmartConsole Administrative Actions Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Once 'full administrative privileges' obtained, attacker can modify security policies and manage endpoints — look for administrative abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After exploitation detection, monitor SmartConsole audit logs for unusual administrative actions (unexpected policy deployments, firewall rule changes, endpoint modifications, security policy disablement). Baseline authorized administrative changes and flag deviations. Correlate policy changes with exploitation timing.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole Unauthenticated Token Acquisition
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'obtain[s] an application login token' without authentication. Core exploitation technique — token generated without prior auth session or with null credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole /login, /auth, or /api/login endpoints for token/session creation where source IP has no prior session history within lookback window. Alert on token issued immediately after first HTTP request from external source without valid credentials.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Admin-Level Operations Post-Token Acquisition
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker uses token 'to authenticate with full administrative privileges.' Detection gap: post-exploitation admin activity (policy changes, config exports, user creation) from newly-acquired session tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate token acquisition events with admin-level API calls (policy write, user management, object deletion) from the same session within 5-10 minutes. Flag when admin operations originate from tokens created by unauthenticated sessions.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Authentication Anomaly: Token Reuse Across Source IPs
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation pattern involves token theft and reuse. Article describes login tokens being used remotely; detect lateral movement or distributed exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single application session token (JWT, auth cookie, API key) used from 3+ distinct source IPs within 10-minute window, or geographic impossibility (e.g., token from 10.0.0.1 then 203.0.113.50 in 5 seconds). High fidelity indicator of token theft.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-16232 Network Exposure Sweep
suggestion.rationale: Article implies SmartConsole must be remotely accessible. 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' (T1190) requires the app exposed; detection requires identifying at-risk assets before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results (SmartConsole, port 4434/tcp, version matching CVE-2026-16232 range) with network boundary logs. Alert on any Check Point SmartConsole instance on externally-routable IPs or accessible via VPN/reverse proxy.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Brute-Force / Rapid Auth Failure Followed by Success
suggestion.rationale: Improper authentication vulnerability may be exploited via credential spray or replay. Article mentions unauthenticated access but doesn't rule out brute-force as secondary vector; standard detection for auth bypass attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect patterns of failed authentication attempts (10+ within 2 minutes from single source) followed by successful token acquisition with admin scope. Or, rapid auth attempts with null/empty/default credentials against SmartConsole.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole API Reconnaissance Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: After obtaining admin token, attacker will enumerate API endpoints, configurations, and user data. Article's 'full administrative privileges' implies broad access for data exfiltration or further lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag rapid sequential API GET requests (policy objects, user list, firewall rules, audit logs) from same admin session token within first 5-30 minutes post-authentication. Pattern indicates post-exploitation recon, not normal admin use.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Unauthenticated Token Issuance
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'obtain an application login token' without authentication. Need detection for token generation outside normal authenticated flows, correlated with session initiation without credential validation.
log_sources: HTTP request logs to SmartConsole endpoints
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for SmartConsole authentication token creation events (login_token, session_start, or similar) that lack corresponding valid credential submission, especially from external/untrusted networks.
