suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole Unauthenticated Auth Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an application login token'. Attack surface is the auth endpoint itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to SmartConsole auth paths (typically /api/auth, /login) from untrusted sources returning 200–302 without credentials, or issuing auth tokens to anonymous sessions. SmartConsole default ports: 4434 (HTTPS), 443.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Privilege Escalation via Stolen Auth Token
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use it to authenticate with full administrative privileges'. Implies token theft followed by admin-level actions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag auth tokens issued to anomalous contexts (new IP, off-hours, failed login immediately prior) that perform admin actions (policy write, account creation, config export) within minutes of issuance. Token lifecycle correlation is key.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole Network Exposure (CVE-2026-16232)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated remote attacker'. Standard asset-exposure hunt for internet-facing or untrusted-network-accessible SmartConsole instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory SmartConsole instances listening on ports 4434 or 443 from internet or untrusted segments. Cross-ref patch status against vendor advisory; any unpatched build is exploitable. Federal due date passed 2026-07-25.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Admin-Level API Activity from Stolen Sessions
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker gains 'full administrative privileges' after token theft. Lateral movement / privilege abuse use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole API calls (e.g., via /api/mgmt endpoints) for admin-gated operations (policy updates, user provisioning, gateway config changes) initiated by sessions lacking normal login audit trail. Correlate with external network access or off-hours activity.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-16232 Remediation Compliance Check
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references CVE-2026-16232 as CISA KEV (active exploitation observed). Compliance check: patch status across fleet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Check Point SmartConsole versions ≤ [vendor-specified build]. Cross-check with installed patches. CISA KEV entries carry mandatory federal remediation deadlines; non-compliance is auditable. Alert on any unpatched instance.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Token Generation in SmartConsole
suggestion.rationale: Article directly states attacker can 'obtain an application login token' without authentication. This is the root exploit — detect tokens issued to requests with no valid credential chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole /api/login and /api/auth endpoints for tokens issued without corresponding authentication events (MFA, username/password validation, or API key exchange). Successful token generation to unauthenticated sessions is anomalous; baseline token issuance rate and flag outliers.

suggestion.title: Administrative Privilege Escalation via Stolen Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes token grants attacker 'full administrative privileges.' Admin API calls using newly-minted tokens bypass normal authorization chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect admin-level API calls (policy modifications, user provisioning, gateway config export) executed by tokens lacking standard authentication path metadata. Flag tokens used for privilege-level operations that exceed the token's claimed identity.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing SmartConsole Authentication Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated remote attacker' — this is T1190 exploitation against exposed management interface. Detect scanning and exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to SmartConsole auth endpoints from external IPs with missing/malformed Authorization headers or known exploit payload signatures. Correlate failed auth attempts with successful token generation to identify successful exploitation windows.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-16232 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV catalog guidance requires asset-exposure hunts — scanner must match CVE-2026-16232 against Check Point inventory to identify unpatched internet-facing instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner CVE-2026-16232 matches against Check Point SmartConsole inventory. Even if patches reported, verify version compliance and confirm no unpatched SmartConsole 2024.x or earlier are externally reachable.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Admin Activity via Compromised Tokens
suggestion.rationale: After token theft ('obtain...login token'), attacker uses it to execute admin commands. Hunt for unusual admin activity from token-based sessions.
log_sources: Check Point SmartConsole command audit logs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify administrative commands (create/modify users, policy pushes, configuration exports) executed by tokens without associated session context (VPN, MFA, identity binding). Flag activity within 5 minutes of token issuance to external source.

suggestion.title: Blockchain-based C2 Beacon Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions 'Blockchain C2'—a fundamental shift from traditional IP/domain-based C2. No use case was generated for this novel infrastructure despite it being the headline innovation described.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on IoT and edge devices establishing sustained connections to Ethereum/Bitcoin RPC endpoints or blockchain API gateways with high-frequency command-like traffic patterns. Monitor for crypto library instantiation (web3.py, ethers.js) on systems not expected to interact with blockchains.

suggestion.title: IoT Peer-to-Peer Relay Node Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Victim Relays' as post-disruption resilience mechanism. This describes compromised IoT devices forwarding botnet traffic to evade centralized C2 takedown—critical persistence and distribution technique absent from UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag IoT/edge devices exhibiting atypical relay behavior: high-volume peer-to-peer connections, forwarding traffic between internal networks and external nodes, or acting as bridges with minimal direct outbound communication. Track connection symmetry anomalies (many inbound, few outbound).

suggestion.title: Dysphoria Malware Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Dysphoria is named explicitly in the title as the botnet family, yet pipeline extracted zero malware signatures, file hashes, process names, or behavioral IoCs. Malware-family-specific detections are foundational.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Dysphoria malware process artifacts (known hash signatures, embedded configuration strings, registry persistence paths). Detect spawned child processes attempting network socket setup for P2P relay participation or blockchain query tools.

suggestion.title: Post-Disruption IoT Device Re-infection
suggestion.rationale: Title references 'After JackSkid Disruption'—indicating this is a resurgence campaign. Initial access mechanism (credential compromise, exploitation) must be detected to block re-infection. No baseline provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IoT management ports (SSH:22, HTTP:80, HTTPS:443, Telnet:23) for brute-force attempts and exploitation payloads targeting known IoT vulnerabilities. Alert on successful credential use from untrusted sources followed by suspicious process execution.

suggestion.title: Blockchain Wallet Cluster Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Botnets monetize via DDoS-as-a-service; blockchain integration implies wallet addresses for payment collection. No wallet IOCs or blockchain transaction patterns were extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track publicly known Dysphoria botnet wallet addresses on blockchain explorers. Correlate internal hosts querying blockchain APIs for wallet balance checks or transaction confirmation patterns. Flag organizations whose compromised IoT subnets generate blockchain transactions.

suggestion.title: Machine Account Creation by Low-Privileged Users
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'a low-privileged user first creates a machine account, which is permitted under the default ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota configuration.' This is the attack's initial stepping stone that should trigger detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on machine account creation (event 4741) by non-service principals. Filter for accounts below helpdesk/sysadmin groups. Baseline ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota usage and flag when quota reached or multiple accounts created by single low-priv user in short window.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Certificate Authority Network Connections to Non-DC Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article details: 'the CA connects to the server specified in the cdc value and searches for the specified rmd'—the attack redirects CA to attacker-controlled SMB/LSA/LDAP. CA→non-DC endpoints are rare.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CA server (certutil, CertSrv processes) initiating outbound SMB (445), LDAP (389,636), or LSA (49152+) connections to non-whitelisted domain controller IPs. Flag connections to workstation or non-DC server IPs from CA service account.

suggestion.title: PKINIT Authentication as Domain Controller
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'using the certificate to authenticate through PKINIT as the targeted domain controller.' Kerberos AS-REQ with DC computer account using certificate-based auth is anomalous and precedes DCSync.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Kerberos AS-REQ (4768) where client is a Domain Controller computer account and authentication method is certificate-based (PKINIT). Cross-correlate with immediate subsequent TGS requests for directory replication rights.

suggestion.title: DCSync Activity from Non-Replication Service Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article demonstrates: 'With the resulting Kerberos credential, the attacker can request account secrets, including the krbtgt secret.' DCSync from an unexpected account principal should trigger immediately.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GetNCChanges RPC calls (event 4662, ObjectClass=domainDNS, replication rights check) initiated by non-replication-service principals. Flag any requester attempting replication for krbtgt account or multiple sensitive objects.

suggestion.title: Certificate Enrollment Requests Targeting Domain Controller Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Certighost: 'submit a certificate request that directs the CA to the rogue services and targets a domain controller account.' Cert requests for DC accounts are highly anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag certificate enrollment requests where subject CN is a Domain Controller computer account (name$) submitted by non-admin/certificate-requester account. Monitor for requests with unusual cdc or rmd attributes (if CA logs these).

suggestion.title: Kerberos Credentials Saved to Disk (.ccache files)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes PoC 'saving the resulting Kerberos credentials to a .ccache file.' Presence of .ccache files outside expected tool directories signals credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .ccache file creation outside /tmp and standard Kerberos paths. Flag if created by non-kerberos processes or in user home directories. Correlate with preceding certificate enrollment and PKINIT activity.

suggestion.title: vBulletin Pre-Auth RCE Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Public Exploit Released for Patched vBulletin Pre-Auth Code Execution Flaw'—establishes T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application). Pipeline must detect HTTP requests to vBulletin admin/api endpoints with known exploit payloads or suspicious parameter values characteristic of RCE attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server access logs for HTTP POST requests to vBulletin endpoints (e.g., /admincp/, /ajax.php, /api/) containing known exploit signatures or unexpected serialized PHP objects. Correlate with HTTP 200 responses followed by unusual process execution from web service accounts.

suggestion.title: Web-to-Process RCE Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: A pre-auth code execution flaw implies unauthenticated attackers gain arbitrary command execution. Article title confirms this attack vector; detection should cover process spawning from web server contexts (apache/www-data/iis apppool).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned from vBulletin web service accounts with suspicious parent process patterns. Flag cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or shell interpreters invoked by w3wp.exe, httpd, or apache with encoded arguments or suspicious LOLBins.

suggestion.title: vBulletin Web Shell Upload or File Staging
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of public RCE often leads to persistence via web shells. Article context implies potential for follow-on file writes to web-accessible directories post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new .php, .asp, .aspx, .jsp files created in vBulletin directories (includes/, upload/, cache/) within minutes of exploitation attempt logs. Correlate file creation with anomalous HTTP POST requests or web server process spawning child interpreters.

suggestion.title: vBulletin Vulnerable Version Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Public exploit disclosure typically targets specific patched versions. Detection must identify unpatched vBulletin instances via version headers, install paths, or /admincp/ responses that leak version info.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse HTTP response headers and error pages from vBulletin endpoints for version strings (e.g., 'vBulletin 5.6.x' in Server header or page source). Flag instances running versions known to be vulnerable to this RCE flaw based on CVE timeline.

suggestion.title: vBulletin C2 Callback Detection Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation enables reverse shells or data exfiltration. Article's critical severity and public exploit suggest rapid weaponization; detection must cover outbound network activity from compromised vBulletin servers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected outbound connections from vBulletin server IPs to high-risk TLDs or known C2 infrastructure. Flag DNS queries for suspicious domains resolved by web service accounts or child processes of vBulletin.

suggestion.title: vBulletin Data Exfiltration (Forum/User Database)
suggestion.rationale: RCE against forum software typically leads to database theft. Article context implies attacker can read database.php or execute queries; detection should cover bulk data reads or export patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large SELECT queries against vBulletin database (vbulletin.user table) or unexpected database table exports. Correlate with outbound HTTPS/HTTP traffic from vBulletin server carrying structured data (serialized PHP, JSON with user credentials).

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker exploits via 'crafted HTTP requests' against FortiOS. No use case generated despite CISA KEV status (active exploitation).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to FortiOS management interfaces with abnormal headers, payloads, or response codes. Correlate with known-bad user agents and POST patterns matching CVE-2025-68686 proof-of-concept signatures. Focus on unauthenticated requests given 'remote unauthenticated attacker' capability.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' as attack vector. Pipeline ignored filesystem-level persistence indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS application directories for symlink creation via `ln -s` or Windows equivalents post-compromise. Baseline FortiOS filesystem structure and alert on modifications to `/etc/`, `/var/`, or application startup paths containing symbolic references.

suggestion.title: Patch Status Verification vs. CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes patch bypass and federal due-date 2026-08-10. Pipeline did not generate compliance/asset-exposure use case despite CISA requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Fortinet FortiOS instances and compare running versions against patched versions post-2026-08-10. Alert on any instances vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686 even if patch claims exist—verify actual deployment via process enumeration or file hashes.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Traffic to FortiOS Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Attack path explicitly requires 'crafted HTTP requests' but no traffic pattern detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous HTTP request morphology: oversized headers, null-byte injection, malformed Content-Length, or request methods (TRACE, OPTIONS) to admin endpoints. Flag requests with exploit payload signatures (base64 binary, serialized objects, format strings) in URI or POST body.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: Patch Bypass Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' Implies active anti-forensic or evasion post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on deletion or modification of FortiOS security module files, patches, or logging directories after T1190 detection. Flag attempts to re-link or restore vulnerable symlinks post-patch. Monitor for file attribute changes (chmod 000, immutable flag removal) on security-critical paths.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exposure Post-CVE Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article concludes vulnerability 'may allow...exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' but no data-exfiltration or collection use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline FortiOS HTTP egress traffic size and patterns. Alert on anomalous data volume from FortiOS management interfaces post-CVE-2025-68686 exploitation window. Flag DNS queries or HTTP requests to attacker-controlled exfiltration endpoints from FortiOS network context.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerable FortiOS Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly establishes CVE-2025-68686 as 'observed exploited in the wild' CISA KEV entry with federal patch due 2026-08-10; vulnerability scan results must surface unpatched instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all FortiOS instances reporting CVE-2025-68686 as vulnerable or unpatched. Prioritize those exposed to public internet. Flag any systems past the 2026-08-10 federal patch deadline without remediation.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Exploitation Against FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector as 'remote unauthenticated attacker' sending 'crafted HTTP requests' to bypass patches; requires detection of malicious HTTP patterns against FortiOS endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor public-facing FortiOS instances for unusual HTTP request patterns: abnormal method/header combinations, path traversal attempts, polyglot payloads, or request sequences that match known CVE-2025-68686 exploitation signatures.

suggestion.title: Post-Filesystem-Compromise Exploitation Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' then exploits via HTTP; chain detection needed for two-stage attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for prior filesystem-level compromise indicators on FortiOS (unauthorized file writes, symlink creation, privilege escalation attempts). Correlate with subsequent HTTP exploitation attempts to catch the complete attack chain.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exfiltration from Compromised FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability described as 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'—requires detection of unauthorized access to config, credentials, or encryption material post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS configuration file access, credential API calls, and encryption key operations following successful HTTP exploitation. Flag abnormal egress traffic carrying configuration or credential data.

suggestion.title: Public Internet Exposure of FortiOS Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'public-facing application' as prerequisite for unauthenticated remote exploitation; requires pre-exploitation asset discovery hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference external internet-facing scan results (Censys, Shodan equivalents) against internal asset inventory. Identify and alert on FortiOS appliances accessible from the internet, prioritizing those matching CVE-2025-68686 vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests to FortiOS Administrative Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote unauthenticated attacker...via crafted HTTP requests' as the attack vector. Pipeline generated no detection logic for exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS admin interfaces for unusual HTTP request patterns, malformed headers, or suspicious parameter combinations. Baseline legitimate admin traffic and alert on requests matching known CVE-2025-68686 exploit signatures or polyglot payloads attempting authentication bypass.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Traversal on Compromised FortiOS Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' and 'post-exploit cases,' indicating attackers leverage symlinks for persistence. No persistence-phase detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation or traversal of symbolic links in FortiOS system directories (especially config, log, and data paths). Correlate with prior CVE compromises or unusual filesystem access patterns indicating post-exploitation activity.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Access and Exposure on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article core outcome is 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Pipeline missed data-access detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk or sequential access to sensitive configuration (VPN credentials, admin accounts, encryption keys, policy definitions) following successful HTTP exploitation. Flag export or copy operations on sensitive files by non-service accounts.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Asset Exposure and Patch Coverage Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Standard vulnerability hunting: 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-10' and CISA KEV imply active scanning requirement. Pipeline provided template reference but no actual detection scenario.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate all externally accessible FortiOS instances against CVE-2025-68686 patch status. Prioritize assets still running vulnerable versions; cross-reference with threat intel on active exploitation. Include network-accessible management interfaces, SSL VPN gateways, and SD-WAN controllers.

suggestion.title: Bypass of Symbolic Link Persistency Patch (CVE-2025-68686 Specific)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states this CVE 'bypass[es] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' This is a direct, testable attack path the pipeline completely missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify requests or filesystem operations that exploit the known patch bypass mechanism (e.g., specific HTTP parameter combinations, path traversal sequences documented in CVE-2025-68686 technical details). Alert on symlink creation attempts that succeed despite patch enforcement policies.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Detection (Scanner)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs to standard asset-exposure hunt: 'Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>'. Pipeline failed to generate the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL templates referenced in article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and CMDB for Fortinet FortiOS instances; cross-reference against patched versions post-2026-08-10. Article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer'—confirm actual patch status via device interrogation, not scanner state alone.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Exploitation (FortiOS)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases, via crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline missed HTTP-layer exploit detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS appliances (identify via product fingerprints: FortiOS banners, management IPs) for HTTP requests with patterns triggering symbolic-link traversal or path-traversal payloads. Flag requests from unauthenticated sources targeting known vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Symbolic Link Abuse (FortiOS Filesystem)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' and references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism'. Pipeline missed defense-evasion phase and filesystem-level IOC generation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On compromised FortiOS systems, hunt for suspicious symlink creation in directories typically targeted by privilege-escalation exploits (e.g., /usr/bin, /etc, /opt/fortinet). Correlate with evidence of prior filesystem access anomalies.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exfiltration (FortiOS Exposure)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names vulnerability class: 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor'. Pipeline missed the exfiltration/impact detection leg.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On vulnerable FortiOS appliances, flag file-read activity targeting sensitive paths: /etc/passwd, config backups, SSL certificates, admin credentials stores. Correlate reads with outbound network anomalies or unusual data volumes.

suggestion.title: Patch Lag Verification (FortiOS Version Audit)
suggestion.rationale: Article warning: 'Even if your scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, it's worth one quick check across your fleet — patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline should have generated a compliance/verification hunt distinct from vulnerability scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query actual FortiOS version/build running on each appliance (via SSH/API interrogation or certificate inspection) and cross-reference against Fortinet security advisories. Flag any device reporting version < patched build even if scanner marked 'patched' due to data staleness.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Alerts for CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CISA KEV entries are 'currently being exploited' and recommends matching 'against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline must surface scanner detections for Fortinet FortiOS systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Fortinet FortiOS instances flagged vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686. Cross-reference scan dates against patch due date (2026-08-10) to find systems with lag > 7 days. Alert on any unpatched public-facing FortiOS appliances.

suggestion.title: Symlink Abuse Detection on FortiOS File Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' exploited post-compromise; attacker needs 'filesystem level' access to abuse symlinks for persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS system logs for symlink creation in sensitive directories (e.g., startup scripts, cron paths). Track repeated symlink traversal in HTTP logs targeting config or cache paths. Correlate with prior exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Patched Bypass Attempts via Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'bypass[es] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism, via crafted HTTP requests.' Detection must target malformed or anomalous HTTP payloads to FortiOS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to FortiOS endpoints with unusual payloads: multiple path traversal sequences, null bytes, double-encoded characters, or requests targeting symlink-vulnerable paths. Baseline legitimate admin traffic first.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Information Disclosure from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: CVE title explicitly names 'Exposure of Sensitive Information.' Article notes attacker achieves information disclosure after filesystem-level compromise. Detection should identify exfiltration post-breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS for large outbound data transfers or reads of sensitive config files (e.g., admin credentials, VPN keys, session tables). Correlate with prior symlink or HTTP exploit attempts on the same appliance.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Inventory Drift for Fortinet FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV articles mandate checking fleet exposure even if patches appear applied. Article recommends 'one quick check across fleet' for patch lag. Pipeline should surface ongoing monitoring use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Weekly compliance scan: all internet-facing FortiOS instances must report patch status. Alert on any FortiOS CRITICAL severity CVE unpatched > 14 days. Flag instances where scanner version_detected mismatches vendor advisories.

suggestion.title: Public-only token used to modify private repository resources
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the vulnerability: 'public-only... token to update a private pull request head branch.' Core exploit is scope bypass—public-only token escaping sandbox to affect private resources. Pipeline missed this critical detection angle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Gitea token audit logs showing token scope (public-only) with repository access logs showing modifications to private repos. Flag when same token with public-only restriction performs write operations on resources marked private, indicating authorization bypass.

suggestion.title: Repository context mismatch in PR update API calls
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause: 'checks the token's public-only restriction against the route repository [public], [but] UpdatePullRequest() then authorizes the pull request based on [the PR's actual private repo].' Detection should flag API calls where the route parameter repo differs from the target resource's actual repo.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gitea API logs for PR update requests where the {public-repo} in the URL path differs from the PR's actual base repository. Mismatch indicates potential authorization context confusion attack.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized branch modifications in private pull requests
suggestion.rationale: Impact statement: 'update private PR head branch.' After bypass succeeds, detect the actual destructive action—unexpected branch ref changes in private repos via API tokens with limited scope. Article describes the attack outcome but pipeline did not generate impact-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gitea repository branch logs for unexpected head branch updates in private repos. Flag when branch refs change via API token activity (not direct commits), especially when the token's scope is public-only or narrower than the target repository's privacy level.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'CISA KEV entry. The U.S. federal Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild.' CVE-2025-68686 is the primary indicator; federal patch due 2026-08-10.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Fortinet FortiOS instances and correlate against known-vulnerable versions for CVE-2025-68686. Prioritize systems still unpatched relative to 2026-08-10 federal deadline. Cross-reference patch-management logs to confirm applied patches.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Creation and Modification on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' Symlink creation is the explicit post-exploit persistence mechanism described.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for symbolic link creation or modification on Fortinet FortiOS systems, particularly in non-standard directories or targeting sensitive configuration files, binaries, or credential stores. Alert on symlinks pointing outside their parent directory.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests Targeting FortiOS Patch Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'via crafted HTTP requests' bypasses the patch. HTTP-layer anomalies are the attack vector for the defense-evasion phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to FortiOS admin/API endpoints with suspicious payloads (encoded parameters, path-traversal-like structures, symlink-reference attempts, or malformed requests designed to bypass input validation). Baseline normal FortiOS traffic patterns and alert on outliers.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Access from FortiOS Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor vulnerability.' Post-compromise, attacker accesses protected data. Unusual credential/configuration file reads or API calls are detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthenticated or low-privilege access to FortiOS sensitive data (admin credentials, encryption keys, VPN configurations, firewall rules, audit logs). Flag reads from filesystem paths normally accessed only by root/system. Correlate data access with prior symlink-creation timelines.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Filesystem-Level Compromise Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Initial compromise is a prerequisite; detecting early filesystem indicators may reveal pre-exploit stage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual process execution (especially non-standard daemons), unexpected file modifications in FortiOS installation directories, privilege escalation attempts, or shell-command execution by web processes. Establish baseline of legitimate FortiOS file/process activity and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 exploitation via crafted HTTP
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated attacker ... via crafted HTTP requests'. T1190 exploitation against exposed FortiOS instances should trigger log/network patterns. Pipeline generated no use case despite citing the CVE in the template section.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS instances for HTTP requests with exploitation signatures (path traversal patterns, unusual query params, HTTP verb abuse). Alert if requests target admin/config endpoints from external IPs or contain patterns matching known CVE-2025-68686 POCs.

suggestion.title: Symbolic link persistence detection in FortiOS filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism ... observed in some post-exploit cases'. Symlink persistence is the defense-evasion mechanism; requires filesystem monitoring, not just network logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag creation or modification of symbolic links in FortiOS config directories (/etc/init.d, /etc/cron.*, system startup paths). Correlate with failed patch detection or version rollback indicators.

suggestion.title: Patch bypass: Unpatched FortiOS exposed after CVE-2025-68686 detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes patch bypass and lists federal due date 2026-08-10. Asset inventory + patch compliance is the primary hunt; article states 'patch lag is the silent killer'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results (FortiOS instances with CVE-2025-68686) against patch-management records. Flag any asset with known FortiOS version ≤ unpatched threshold that is also externally accessible or appears in honeypot/proxy logs.

suggestion.title: Sensitive data exfiltration via FortiOS configuration access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'. Attacker uses crafted requests to access config files (likely containing credentials, API keys, backup URLs). POST-exploitation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert if sensitive FortiOS configuration files (admin account hashes, API secrets, SSL certificates, backup credentials stored in /etc/fortios/config*) are accessed or read via HTTP requests from non-admin IP ranges or outside change-control windows.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CVE-2025-68686 is in CISA KEV (actively exploited in the wild) with 'remote unauthenticated attacker' attack vector. Article instructs: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt...Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>'—yet pipeline generated zero asset-exposure UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Fortinet FortiOS appliances accessible externally and cross-reference against CVE-2025-68686 patch status (due 2026-08-10). Prioritize unpatched instances; CISA KEV status confirms active wild exploitation. Check both scanner results and manual discovery methods (Shodan, Censys).

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism Detection on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' as a persistence tactic used after initial compromise via 'another vulnerability, at filesystem level.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS systems for unexpected symbolic link creation or modification in startup directories, driver paths, and configuration load points. Baseline legitimate FortiOS symbolic links and alert on anomalous additions that could persist post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: HTTP Patch Bypass Attempts Against FortiOS CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Article states the vulnerability 'may allow...attacker to bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism...via crafted HTTP requests.' This is an explicit exploitation vector for patch evasion on compromised appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to FortiOS appliances (ports 80, 443, 8080) for obfuscated payloads, unusual URI encoding, path traversal attempts, or requests targeting known patch/security endpoints. Look for byte-level anomalies that may indicate crafted requests designed to bypass patch protections.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Sensitive Data Access on Fortinet Appliances
suggestion.rationale: CVE title explicitly states 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor.' After filesystem-level compromise, attackers use CVE-2025-68686 to access or exfiltrate sensitive data. Article: 'attacker...bypass the patch...via crafted HTTP requests.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unauthorized access to sensitive FortiOS resources post-compromise: configuration file reads, certificate/key exports, VPN credential access, system log exfiltration. Correlate with preceding exploitation attempts or filesystem-level access anomalies.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage FortiOS Exploitation Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' before exploiting CVE-2025-68686. This is a chained attack—detect the earlier-stage filesystem compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate filesystem-level compromise indicators (privilege escalation, unauthorized file writes to restricted paths, process execution anomalies) with FortiOS security events. Establish baseline of legitimate FortiOS processes and escalation patterns; flag deviations as potential stage-1 compromise enabling CVE-2025-68686 exploitation.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Patch Compliance Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt... Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>: CVE-2025-68686'. Pipeline should have instantiated _TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure with this CVE. Cited phrase: 'Even if your scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, it's worth one quick check across your fleet.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query scanner for CVE-2025-68686 across all FortiOS deployments, prioritizing externally-exposed instances (edge FW, proxies). Flag unpatched assets and track against federal due date 2026-08-10.

suggestion.title: FortiOS HTTP Symbolic-Link Bypass Exploitation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is explicit: 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases, via crafted HTTP requests'. Pipeline should hunt HTTP patterns targeting this bypass. Phrase: 'remote unauthenticated attacker... via crafted HTTP requests'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt FortiOS HTTP logs for anomalous requests to management endpoints with path-traversal, symlink-targeting, or unusual encoding. Correlate alerts with CVE-2025-68686-vulnerable asset inventory.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Post-Compromise Sensitive Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability impact is 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'. After filesystem compromise, attacker exfiltrates config, certs, or credentials via HTTP. Phrase: 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS for processes reading sensitive files (system.conf, certificates, user database) with concurrent external data transmission. Flag unusual egress volume, non-whitelisted external IPs, or obfuscated protocols.

suggestion.title: Pre-Compromise Filesystem-Level Vulnerability Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' This two-stage kill chain means hunting for the initial vector before CVE-2025-68686 exploitation. Phrase: 'attacker would need first to have compromised... via another vulnerability'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In days/weeks preceding 2026-07-27, hunt FortiOS logs for pre-auth RCE, unauthorized filesystem access, or privilege escalation. Look for exploitation of prior FortiOS CVEs (auth-bypass, unauthenticated RCE) as the stage-1 compromise vector.

suggestion.title: FortiOS symbolic link manipulation post-compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism'—a clear persistence technique. This requires detection of crafted file/symlink structures on FortiOS after initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for anomalous symbolic link creation in system paths (e.g., /etc, /bin directories). Flag links pointing to unexpected locations or created shortly after vulnerability scan dates. Correlate with earlier compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: FortiOS crafted HTTP request anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass ... via crafted HTTP requests'. Requires detection of malformed or unexpected HTTP payloads targeting FortiOS endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to FortiOS admin interfaces containing unusual URL encoding, path traversal sequences, or payloads matching known symbolic link bypass patterns. Baseline normal admin traffic and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Sensitive information exfiltration from FortiOS post-CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability type is 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'—requires detection of data flows after successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS for unexpected outbound connections carrying config, credential, or policy data after exploitation window. Compare against baseline authorized data flows to C&C channels.

suggestion.title: FortiOS configuration integrity check post-patch bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions attacker bypasses 'the patch developed for' the mechanism—detection should verify patch presence and configuration state hasn't regressed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated scanning for FortiOS instances missing CVE-2025-68686 patch within 7 days post-KEV publication. Also check for config changes disabling logging or AV/IPS signatures post-initial compromise.

suggestion.title: Filesystem-level compromise prerequisites for CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'—prerequisite exploitation should be hunted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for prior exploitation attempts or successful compromises within 30 days before CVE-2025-68686 exploitation window. Focus on unauthenticated remote access, file upload endpoints, and known Fortinet pre-auth RCE patterns.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Reassignment to Unreviewed/Orphaned Commits
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit' and 'The attacker re-pointed several existing release tags to their malicious commit, thereby deepening the attack's impact.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when release tags on critical GitHub Action repositories are reassigned to commits that are orphaned, lack review history, or exist outside main/develop branches. Correlate tag changes with unusual commit metadata or author anomalies.

suggestion.title: Detect Orphaned Commits in High-Value CI/CD Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes orphaned commits as 'one of the key enabling factors': 'Having the attack commit orphaned from any branches, including the main branch' makes it invisible to normal browsing but available via direct reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when commits in Action repositories become orphaned (detached from all branches). Flag correlation between orphaned commit creation and subsequent tag reassignment or release operations within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Secrets Exposed in Plaintext in GitHub Action Logs
suggestion.rationale: Direct impact: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit that caused encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs.' This is the exfiltration payload and the exploitable output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect plaintext secrets/credentials in Action workflow logs. Monitor for Action code changes that disable secret masking, reference encrypted variables without redaction, or log environment variables containing secrets.

suggestion.title: Suspicious External Network Calls from GitHub Actions Runners
suggestion.rationale: Detection mechanism: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from GitHub Actions runners to non-whitelisted domains or suspicious IPs. Alert on HTTP requests that fetch and execute code from external sources, especially if signed requests or authentication patterns are anomalous.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized or Suspicious Commits to Critical GitHub Action Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Prerequisite: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit.' While initial access method unknown, writes to trusted repos are critical checkpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag commits to high-value Action repositories from unusual IP addresses, time patterns, or locations. Alert on commits lacking standard code review, containing obfuscated code, or using external curl/wget patterns.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise via Action Version Tag Drift from Expected Commits
suggestion.rationale: Attack leveraged consumers expecting stable versions: users 'reference that tag and assume that's what we'll be getting. Under normal circumstances, that is a reasonable assumption but GitHub tags are just convenient strings pointing to a particular commit - no magic.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Action tags in workflows against their current commits. Alert when tags deviate from historical commit authors, lack code signatures, or point to commits created outside normal release windows or review processes.

suggestion.title: Gitea artifact access with mismatched task owner context in audit logs
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'An attacker...can turn a signed URL for an attacker-controlled artifact into a URL that reads artifacts from another task context.' Pipeline missed log-level validation: Gitea audit logs should record artifact operations where the requester's task context does not own/match the target artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for DownloadArtifact or UploadArtifact API calls where RequestorJobID ≠ ArtifactOwnerJobID, especially across repositories. Legitimate artifact access is owner-scoped; cross-context access is exploitation.

suggestion.title: Rapid multi-artifact enumeration post-workflow dispatch
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker leveraging 'permission to run a Gitea Actions job' to access other tasks. Behavioral gap: exploitation would manifest as rapid sequential artifact downloads of varying artifactName values immediately after workflow start—scanning behavior distinct from legitimate workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 30s–2min post-workflow-dispatch, flag 5+ DownloadArtifact requests to distinct artifactName values from single source/job. Normal workflows fetch 1–2 known artifacts; enumeration attempts show randomization or path traversal patterns.

suggestion.title: HMAC signature parameter reuse across repository boundaries
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'can be rewritten to access a different running task and repository context while preserving the original HMAC signature.' Detection gap: same 'sig' parameter value appearing in signed URLs accessing artifacts in multiple distinct Git repositories within short time window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract sig parameter from UploadArtifact/DownloadArtifact URLs and correlate across repository names. Alert on same sig accessing 2+ distinct repositories in 10min window—indicates HMAC reuse exploitation across contexts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized writes to artifact staging areas from non-owner task processes
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'cross-task upload-state write' means attacker writes artifacts to another job's storage context. Detection gap: artifact staging/upload filesystem logs showing modifications from processes whose task context doesn't own the target path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor artifact upload directories for file writes from gitea-actions runner processes assigned to a different TaskID than the artifact's owner. Mismatch indicates cross-task write exploitation.

suggestion.title: Credential/secret material discovery via cross-task artifact content inspection
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'artifacts' without specifying content; but cross-task read attacks gain access to other jobs' build outputs, which often contain secrets, tokens, private keys. Detection: after cross-task artifact read is confirmed, correlate with sensitive patterns in artifact payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enrich cross-task artifact download detections with artifact content analysis: flag high-risk if downloaded artifacts contain regex patterns matching CI_TOKEN=, GITHUB_TOKEN=, AWS_ACCESS_KEY, RSA PRIVATE KEY, etc. Indicates credential exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Anomalous HTTP Requests to FortiOS Admin Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker uses 'crafted HTTP requests' to bypass the patched symbolic link mechanism. This is the exploitation vector and should be detectable via network/web log anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS admin portal and API endpoints for malformed or unusual HTTP requests with suspicious parameter patterns. Baseline normal admin traffic and alert on deviations, particularly POST/PUT requests with encoded payloads or requests to undocumented endpoints. Correlate with known-exploited CVE-2025-68686 patches.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Creation/Modification on FortiOS Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' as the target of the bypass. Detection must capture symlink activity on the filesystem, particularly in FortiOS config or system directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation or modification of symbolic links in FortiOS system paths (/etc, /var, /data), especially pointing to config files, diagnostic logs, or authentication modules. Audit the /tmp and /var/tmp directories for symlinks created by httpd or admin processes.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to FortiOS Sensitive Configuration/Backup Files
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' After successful bypass, attackers will access config files, certificates, credentials, or backups. Article states prerequisite is 'compromised at filesystem level.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor access to FortiOS backup files, private keys, and config exports. Alert on reads of /data/config.backup, /data/config, or certificate stores by unprivileged processes or from HTTP requests. Correlate file reads with preceding symbolic link creation or anomalous HTTP activity.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Bypass or Symlink Persistence After Mitigation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions attackers 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' This indicates continued exploitation even after vendor patches, suggesting monitoring for patch-bypass techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For patched FortiOS systems, monitor for re-exploitation attempts: modified symlinks created *after* patch application, HTTP requests with known-bypass payloads (check FortiOS advisories), or evidence of rolling back symlink mitigations. Alert if symbolic link activity resumes post-patch.

suggestion.title: Two-Stage Exploitation: Detect Predecessor Vulnerability Leading to FortiOS Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states prerequisite: 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' CVE-2025-68686 is stage-2; detection must identify stage-1 exploitation patterns that grant filesystem access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of active CVE exploits targeting FortiOS (e.g., remote code execution, auth bypass, file upload). Alert on successful exploitation indicators that would grant filesystem access, then raise tier-2 alerts for downstream symlink or HTTP bypass activity within 24-48 hours on same asset.

suggestion.title: Diagnostic Log or Configuration Export Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Symlink bypass enables unauthorized access to sensitive information. FortiOS diagnostic logs and exported configs contain credentials, encryption keys, and network topology. Article's impact is 'exposure of sensitive information.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation or transfer of FortiOS diagnostic tarballs (which contain sensitive configs, logs, and keys), particularly triggered via crafted HTTP requests or from non-admin sources. Monitor for exfiltration of .diag files or config backups via unexpected protocols or destinations.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacks against 'exposed assets' and federal agencies must remediate by 2026-08-10; pipeline must surface which FortiOS instances are internet-facing before due date.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and network telemetry for FortiOS instances (FortiGate, FortiManager, etc.) with public IPv4/IPv6 and inbound access from untrusted networks. Correlate with patch status to identify unpatched systems. CISA deadline 2026-08-10 is 13 days post-publication; prioritize by exposure surface.

suggestion.title: HTTP Request Bypass Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'bypass[es] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism, via crafted HTTP requests'; requires monitoring for HTTP payloads targeting this specific post-exploitation channel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiOS admin interfaces and APIs for request patterns attempting to read symbolic link targets or bypass link-resolution checks. Flag anomalous path traversal or file-descriptor manipulation in request bodies. Baseline: normal admin/API traffic to identify deviation.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Unauthorized Information Disclosure
suggestion.rationale: CVE is classified as 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'; detection must capture data exfiltration patterns following successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS systems for unusual data volume egress or sensitive-data-type exfiltration (e.g., config dumps, private keys, credentials). Correlate with HTTP bypass-exploit indicators to establish attack chain. Alert if system outputs config or secrets post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Compliance Verification
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requires federal remediation by 2026-08-10; pipeline must surface patch status and roadmap for non-compliant systems before deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and patch-management system for FortiOS systems running versions vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686. Identify patch availability date and apply to roadmap. Flag systems still vulnerable after 2026-08-10 as audit/compliance risk.

suggestion.title: Filesystem Symlink Abuse Detection on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' as the persistence channel for post-exploit access; filesystem monitoring is critical to detect this attack primitive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem (via auditd, syslog, or HIPS) for creation or modification of symbolic links in sensitive directories (e.g., web-accessible paths, config folders). Baseline normal symlink activity (e.g., from upgrades/patches) and flag anomalies, especially links pointing to sensitive files outside web root.

suggestion.title: Secondary Vulnerability Exploitation Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'; detection must cover the initial compromise vector and chain it to post-exploit patch bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Map other known FortiOS/Fortinet vulnerabilities (e.g., CVE-2024-XXXXX, CVE-2025-XXXXX) and flag evidence of chained exploitation: (1) initial vuln triggered, (2) filesystem access gain, (3) symlink creation/modification, (4) subsequent HTTP bypass attempts. Establish attack-chain timeline.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Malformed HTTP Request Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'crafted HTTP requests' as the attack surface; zero HTTP-layer detection proposed despite being the primary exploitation vector
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS-exposed HTTP endpoints for malformed requests: oversized headers, null bytes, unusual HTTP methods, path traversal patterns. Baseline normal traffic and alert on statistically significant deviations from established FortiOS communication profiles.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism Activation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism'—filesystem persistence technique with zero detection coverage
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for symlink creation/modification by FortiOS processes, especially targeting autorun paths, startup directories, or persistent config storage. Alert on symlinks pointing outside expected FortiOS installation scope.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Credential / Config Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'—no detection for unauthorized config/credential file access
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on abnormal reads to FortiOS credential vaults, config files, and certificate stores—especially from non-service-account processes or via HTTP request context. Baseline legitimate access patterns first.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Post-Exploitation Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability'—implies mandatory reconnaissance phase after initial compromise
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for enumeration commands (net.exe, whoami, dir, Get-Process) spawned in context of HTTP-serving process or suspicious parent. Correlation with compromise timestamps indicates post-exploit discovery activity.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Crafted HTTP Request Detection (Patch Bypass)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'via crafted HTTP requests' as the bypass mechanism—direct exploitation signature with no detection provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS HTTP logs for malformed requests, unusual header combinations, or request patterns targeting symbolic-link-sensitive endpoints. Spike detection around exploitation timeline; correlate against known FortiOS patch-bypass POCs.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Filesystem Abuse (Persistency)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' as the core post-compromise persistence vector; no filesystem-level detections specified.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on symlink() syscalls or equivalent API invocations targeting FortiOS config directories, binary locations, or library paths. Post-compromise activity marker following successful CVE-2025-68686 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exfiltration Post-Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article objective is 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' after filesystem-level compromise; no exfil detection logic provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-exploitation, monitor for bulk reads of config files, credential stores, or VPN user databases. Flag unexpected outbound connections or high-volume data transfer coinciding with crafted HTTP exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Two-Stage Exploitation Chain Entry Point
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'—requires detection of the initial access vector preceding CVE-2025-68686 bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of FortiOS exploit attempts in weeks prior to federal patch due date (2026-08-10). Alert on unknown vulnerability scanning or exploitation patterns against internet-exposed FortiOS instances; correlate with subsequent CVE-2025-68686 patch-bypass HTTP signatures.

suggestion.title: Patch Level Mismatch Detection (Defense Evasion)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes patch bypass—vulnerable patch levels post-due-date are detectable and correlate with exploitation risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag FortiOS instances reporting pre-patch versions after 2026-08-10. Cross-reference with HTTP logs for CVE-2025-68686 exploitation attempts (crafted requests). Alert on patch downgrade or version regression.

suggestion.title: Multi-Vulnerability Attack Chain (CVE Correlation)
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'another vulnerability' required for initial filesystem compromise, implying a CVE-chain attack. No correlation logic or secondary vulnerability hunting provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish timeline of recent critical FortiOS CVEs (pre-2025-68686). Cross-reference exploitation attempts: if attacker successfully exploits earlier CVE to reach filesystem level, downstream CVE-2025-68686 exploitation becomes high-confidence signal.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 FortiOS Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'remote unauthenticated attacker' via 'crafted HTTP requests' against exposed FortiOS instances. Federal patch due 2026-08-10 creates urgency.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset inventory check for FortiOS versions vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686. Cross-reference internet-facing FortiOS hosts from network telemetry against known vulnerable version ranges. Alert on any FortiOS instance not patched by 2026-08-10 deadline.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism Abuse Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'—indicates post-exploitation file-system trickery for maintaining access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected symbolic link creation in system-critical directories (/etc, /var/lib, /usr/bin on Linux; %SystemRoot%, %ProgramFiles% on Windows). Look for processes with FortiOS or authentication-service context creating symlinks to unexpected targets.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise HTTP Exploitation to FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker must first compromise via another vulnerability 'at filesystem level,' then exploits this via 'crafted HTTP requests.' Indicates multi-stage attack: initial filesystem access → subsequent HTTP-based exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests with malformed headers, oversized parameters, or URL-encoded payloads targeting FortiOS endpoints (e.g., /api/*, /admin/*, /system/*). Correlate with prior filesystem access anomalies or privilege-escalation events on same endpoint.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Filesystem-Level Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly requires 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' as precondition. This earlier-stage compromise must be hunted independently.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthorized writes to FortiOS system directories, unexpected process spawns with FortiOS service context, or privilege escalation to SYSTEM/root from a FortiOS process. Baseline and monitor filesystem ACL changes on FortiOS installation paths.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scan Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries indicate active wild exploitation. Attackers will scan for instances; defenders must baseline legitimate scans vs. attacker probing. Article severity is critical with federal patch due date.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Whitelist known enterprise vulnerability-management scanners (internal Nessus/Qualys IPs) scanning FortiOS. Flag non-whitelisted IPs probing FortiOS endpoints for CVE-2025-68686 indicators. Correlate scan attempts with HTTP 400/403 responses indicating exploitation probes.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Vulnerable Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes asset-exposure hunt as canonical detection. No UC generated despite explicit mention of 'exposed assets' and 'remote unauthenticated attacker'—implies FortiOS internet-facing; should baseline the fleet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Fortinet FortiOS instances with inbound internet access via network telemetry, vulnerability scanner, or DNS resolution. Correlate against asset inventory for unexpected exposure. Prioritize instances not yet patched for CVE-2025-68686.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation via Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker uses 'crafted HTTP requests' to bypass patch and leak sensitive info. No UC for HTTP anomaly or request-pattern detection—this is the exploitation signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic to FortiOS instances for requests bearing malformed payloads, uncommon methods, or path traversal patterns. Correlate with CVSS-9.8 post-exploitation behavior (data exfiltration). Alert on any requests matching known exploitation PoC signatures.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploit NTFS Information Disclosure Access Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'NTFS Information Disclosure'—article describes attacker gaining filesystem-level access post-compromise. Should hunt for suspicious NTFS/volume access (symbolic link abuse mentioned in patch-bypass context).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On compromised FortiOS systems, detect attempts to read sensitive system files via volume/filesystem APIs, especially patterns consistent with symbolic link traversal (article mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism'). Look for `Device\HarddiskVolume*` or direct volume access after lateral movement.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage FortiOS Exploitation Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'—describes chained exploitation. No UC for initial-exploit detection before CVE-2025-68686 is weaponized.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate exploit activity against FortiOS: flag any CVE exploitation (scanner or IDS alerts) against exposed FortiOS + subsequent HTTP anomalies within hours. This two-stage pattern—compromised-then-exploited—is the kill chain signature and warrants escalation.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration via FortiOS Channel
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability described as 'exposure of sensitive information to unauthorized actor'—implies data exfiltration. No UC for detecting data staging, compression, or egress via compromised FortiOS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound traffic from FortiOS for anomalous data volumes, archive formats (zip, tar), or DNS queries indicative of exfiltration staging. Correlate with NTFS access patterns. Alert if sensitive file types (credentials, configs, user data) are read then egressed.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Public-Facing Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote unauthenticated attacker' can exploit—implies internet-facing FortiOS instances are target surface. Pipeline generated zero asset-exposure hunts despite this being canonical for CISA KEV exploited-in-wild entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify FortiOS instances (port 443, HTTP-01 banner, certificate CN=FortiOS) reachable from untrusted networks. Cross-check against patch inventory for CVE-2025-68686 status. Flag unpatch lag >7 days before 2026-08-10 federal due date.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests to FortiOS (CVE-2025-68686)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'crafted HTTP requests' as attack vector. Pipeline did not generate HTTP anomaly or request-pattern detection despite this being the direct exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS access logs for anomalous HTTP requests: malformed headers, oversized payloads, symbolic-link path traversal patterns (e.g., `../`, `..\`), or requests targeting admin/api endpoints from non-admin source IPs. Alert on 50x / 40x response codes in clusters.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Disclosure Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article defines vulnerability as 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Pipeline generated no detection for post-exploitation data exfiltration or credential leakage—gaps in collection/exfiltration phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful compromise, hunt for bulk reads of FortiOS config files (system.conf, vdom.conf, user authentication logs, VPN tunnels, SSL certificates).
