suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiOS admin ports (typically 80, 443, 8080, 8443) from unexpected sources. Alert on POST/GET with non-standard parameters, unusual Content-Length patterns, or encoding anomalies that deviate from legitimate admin-tool traffic.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Post-Exploitation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'—a clear persistence technique. Pipeline must hunt for filesystem manipulation indicative of this mechanism being deployed or restored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for creation/modification of symbolic links in system directories, startup locations, or config paths. Correlate timeline with HTTP anomalies to establish attacker exploitation chain.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Pivoting from Compromised FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'—establishing FortiOS as a pivot point. Post-compromise, attacker will move laterally from appliance into internal network.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network traffic from FortiOS to internal infrastructure using protocols anomalous for appliance behavior (SMB, RDP, SSH, LDAP client queries). Alert on high-volume or sustained data transfer from appliance subnets.

suggestion.title: Patch Bypass Evasion Technique Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes attacker can 'bypass the patch developed for' the symbolic link mechanism—defense evasion through targeting unpatched code paths. Pipeline must surface signatures specific to patch-bypass payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP anomalies to FortiOS with exploitation signatures targeting patched code paths. Alert if modified binaries or libraries detected in FortiOS after patch. Compare firmware hashes against known good baseline.

suggestion.title: Unpatched FortiOS Exploitation Attempt Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Until 2026-08-10 deadline, many instances will remain unpatched. Pipeline must detect active exploitation attempts using CVE-2025-68686 attack patterns before defensive patching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy/activate IPS/IDS signatures for CVE-2025-68686 exploitation patterns. Alert on suspicious HTTP sequences matching known attack chains. Require immediate incident response escalation and emergency patching.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Detection via Vulnerability Scanner
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'CVE-2025-68686 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and emphasizes CISA KEV is currently exploited in the wild. This is the canonical hunt path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner result reporting CVE-2025-68686 against Fortinet FortiOS instances. Flag as critical given CISA KEV status and federal patch due-date of 2026-08-10.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Pattern to FortiOS Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch... via crafted HTTP requests.' This is the attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP access logs for unusual request patterns to FortiOS API/admin endpoints (e.g., /api/, /admin/). Look for requests that deviate from baseline authentication handshakes or carry malformed parameters targeting the CVE-2025-68686 bypass chain.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' This indicates filesystem-level persistence after initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS systems for unexpected symbolic link creation or modification in system directories (e.g., /etc, /usr/bin, startup paths). Correlate with prior evidence of CVE-2025-68686 exploitation or HTTP anomalies.

suggestion.title: Patch Bypass Attempts Against Symbolic Link Fix
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' This is active defense evasion post-patching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for attempts to access or modify the symbolic link validation/hardening code introduced in the patch. Look for process execution or file access patterns that circumvent the fix (e.g., direct inode manipulation, alternative paths to triggering the original flaw).

suggestion.title: Prior Filesystem-Level Compromise via Chained Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' This is the prerequisite condition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate FortiOS instances flagged for CVE-2025-68686 with evidence of other known FortiOS exploits or filesystem tampering in the same timeframe. Multi-stage attacks often chain multiple CVEs; this is a hunt for the predecessor.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Scanner Hit Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article is CISA KEV with federal patch due 2026-08-10. Pipeline must recommend vulnerability scanning. Article explicitly states 'remote unauthenticated attacker' and lists product/version — scanner baseline is foundational.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search vulnerability scanner output and asset inventory for Fortinet FortiOS and FortiProxy instances flagged with CVE-2025-68686. Prioritize exposed / internet-facing instances. Verify patch status against Fortinet advisories and flag unpatched systems for immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: FortiOS HTTP Exploitation — Crafted Request Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states threat 'via crafted HTTP requests' — yet pipeline generated zero HTTP-based detection UC. This is the active exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS and FortiProxy HTTP access logs for patterns associated with exploitation: unusual URI paths to administrative endpoints, malformed headers, encoding anomalies, or rapid sequences of failed authentication attempts followed by suspicious parameter injection. Baseline expected access and alert on deviations from authenticated administrative behavior.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Creation and Persistence Establishment
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in post-exploit cases' — pipeline missed post-exploitation persistence detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for symbolic link creation in persistence-relevant paths: startup scripts, cron/scheduler directories, library search paths, web root directories. Correlate symlink creation with file permissions changes and target linkage to sensitive config or credential files. Alert on symlink creation by non-standard processes or from unexpected source directories.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Config / Credential File Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: CVE is explicitly 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Pipeline should hunt for configuration, credential, or system information file access after initial foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect reads of sensitive FortiOS files: admin credential stores, VPN configurations, SSL certificates, system status output, routing tables, firewall rules. Correlate file access with indicators of prior system compromise or anomalous HTTP patterns. Flag file exfiltration via logs or memory dumps post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Attack Chain — Initial Compromise Plus CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' — Pipeline zero-filled the attack chain despite this describing a two-step exploitation sequence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create multi-event correlation: first detect exploitation of FortiOS/FortiProxy vulnerabilities granting filesystem-level access (e.g., RCE, path traversal). Then within 72 hours, detect HTTP anomalies matching CVE-2025-68686 exploitation patterns, symlink creation events, or sensitive file access. Correlated pair significantly raises confidence of coordinated two-stage attack.

suggestion.title: Title/Body CVE Discrepancy — Both CVEs Present
suggestion.rationale: Article title references CVE-2025-24472 (Authentication Bypass) but body discusses CVE-2025-68686 (Information Exposure). Pipeline should have flagged and generated detections for BOTH CVEs, not just one.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for presence of BOTH CVE-2025-24472 and CVE-2025-68686 in FortiOS/FortiProxy installations. Cross-reference asset inventory. The dual-CVE pattern may indicate the article conflates two related vulnerabilities or two exploitation sequences in the same product. Generate separate hunts for each CVE identifier.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Reassignment to Orphaned Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the attack mechanism: 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit, which was the orphaned commit.' This is the core obfuscation technique and is directly detectable through GitHub audit logs or API monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub repository audit logs for release tag modifications, particularly tags pointing to commits not on any active branch. Alert when a tag previously pointing to a release commit is reassigned to a commit with no parent branch or orphaned history. Correlate with write access by non-core maintainers.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit Detection in Release-Critical Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article demonstrates exploitation of orphaned commits: 'Having the attack commit orphaned from any branches, including the main branch' was a key enabling factor. Orphaned commits in repositories with many downstream dependencies are high-risk attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan repositories (especially those used as GitHub Actions) for commits reachable only via tags, not via any branch. Orphaned commits that receive tag pointers should trigger high-confidence alerts. Check frequency should increase for popular public actions.

suggestion.title: Secrets Exposure in GitHub Action Logs via Malicious Workflow
suggestion.rationale: Core impact of the attack: 'caused encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs.' This is detectable by monitoring GitHub Action logs for exposed credentials matching repository secret patterns, particularly base64-encoded or plaintext API tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Action run logs for patterns matching known secret formats (AWS keys, GitHub tokens, API credentials). Correlate log exposure with action version changes or unexpected external network calls. Alert on any plaintext credentials in public repository logs.

suggestion.title: Anomalous External Network Calls from GitHub Actions Workflows
suggestion.rationale: Article notes the attack was discovered through: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' Network egress monitoring from CI/CD is the most reliable detection vector.
log_sources: Network egress logs from GitHub Actions runners
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections from GitHub Actions workflows, particularly to unknown/suspicious domains or IP addresses. Establish baselines for expected external calls per repository. Alert on calls to domains not in the repository's documented dependencies or CI configuration. Cross-reference external URLs called against threat feeds.

suggestion.title: Unexpected GitHub Action Version Changes Across Dependent Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article describes workflow: users reference 'tj-actions/changed-files@v35' expecting a stable release. When tags are reassigned to malicious commits, all downstream repos suddenly execute compromised code. Detecting version anomalies across the ecosystem is a supply-chain early warning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For widely-used GitHub Actions (>1000 dependents), monitor for unexpected code changes or external calls between tagged releases. Alert when a release tag is modified post-publication or when downstream repositories suddenly execute significantly different code paths from a pinned tag. Correlate with commit history and author access logs.

suggestion.title: Repository Write Access Anomaly on High-Impact Public Actions
suggestion.rationale: Prerequisite attack condition: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit.' While the exact cause is unknown, detecting unexpected write access or new collaborators on critical dependencies is essential. Article notes 23,000 dependent repos—any write access anomaly deserves scrutiny.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub repositories used as Actions for new collaborators, permission escalations, or unexpected write access grants. Alert on any write access to repositories with >1000 direct dependents. Implement MFA enforcement and review justification for new permissions on critical supply-chain repositories.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2025-68686 — match against your vulnerability scanner'; scanner results are primary IOC source for this KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any FortiOS appliance without patch for CVE-2025-68686 applied before the 2026-08-10 federal deadline. Cross-reference scanner results with known-vulnerable versions of FortiOS.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests to FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker uses 'crafted HTTP requests' to bypass patch; FortiOS access/HTTP logs should show anomalous request patterns targeting known vulnerable endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS HTTP access logs and reverse-proxy logs for HTTP requests with unusual patterns, large payloads, or encoding attempts targeting known vulnerable paths in FortiOS (if endpoint signatures emerge post-disclosure).

suggestion.title: FortiOS Filesystem-Level Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'; this precondition should trigger filesystem access monitoring and integrity checks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious file writes/modifications in FortiOS system directories, particularly around symlink-related paths or configuration stores, preceding any observed HTTP exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Deployment Enforcement
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with mandatory federal remediation date 2026-08-10; compliance hunt should verify patch deployment across all FortiOS appliances in fleet before deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and patch management systems to identify all FortiOS instances and confirm patch version ≥ [vendor-provided patched version] deployed prior to 2026-08-10. Flag any system still running vulnerable version.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation — Crafted HTTP Requests to FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch...via crafted HTTP requests.' Direct exploitation vector requires signature-based or behavioral detection on FortiOS internet-facing interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiOS admin interfaces or known vulnerable endpoints for anomalous payloads: oversized headers, malformed syntax, or base64-encoded patterns matching known public exploits. Flag if source is external or non-trusted network segment.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Post-Exploitation Persistence — Symbolic Link Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' Attackers leverage this after CVE-2025-68686 compromise to maintain access; filesystem modification is detectible.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of symlinks (ln -s) in FortiOS critical directories: /etc/init.d, /lib/systemd/system, /etc/config, or /bin. Correlate with recent unpatched CVE-2025-68686 status. Symlinks pointing to attacker-controlled paths (especially /tmp, /dev/shm) are highest priority.

suggestion.title: Prerequisite Compromise Detection — Filesystem-Level Access Before CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Article critical qualifier: 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' The prior breach is the kill-chain start; detection must cover this stage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthorized file modifications in FortiOS system directories before HTTP exploitation occurs. Correlate filesystem audit logs with CVE-2025-68686 exploitation attempts (HTTP) to confirm two-stage attack chain. High urgency if non-root process modifies /bin, /etc, or /lib.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Exposure Scan — Unpatch Status for CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Article: CISA KEV entry with patch due 2026-08-10; 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Baseline asset-inventory hunt required for compliance and risk posture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for all Fortinet FortiOS appliances with CVE-2025-68686 status. Cross-reference with network-exposure inventory (internet-facing, DMZ, or untrusted-segment reachable). Flag unpatched instances with severity=critical and age-of-vuln >= 14 days. Report to vendor-patch-tracking workflow immediately.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement — FortiOS as Pivot Point Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Compromised FortiOS (via CVE-2025-68686) becomes network-access springboard. Article implies network-adjacent targets are at risk; detect abnormal egress from compromised appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS appliances for anomalous outbound connections (especially to non-RFC1918 addresses, high ports, or known C2 indicators) that follow successful HTTP exploitation attempts. Baseline: FortiOS should only communicate to Fortinet services, upstream ISP, and managed-client destinations.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exposure — Post-CVE-2025-68686 Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: CVE classifies as 'Exposure of Sensitive Information.' After exploitation via HTTP, expect data access. Detect anomalous data reads or exports from FortiOS config/logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes on FortiOS that read system configuration files (especially /etc/passwd, /etc/config/system.conf, VPN credential stores) without corresponding admin session. Detect unusual syslog forwarding destinations or config file exports via HTTP/FTP post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scanning Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE: CVE-2025-68686 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and explicitly recommends substituting this CVE into standard asset-exposure hunting templates. Scanning is the baseline detection mechanism for known-exploited vulnerabilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner detections of CVE-2025-68686 present on any Fortinet FortiOS device, with priority escalation for internet-exposed instances. Track patch status against the 2026-08-10 federal deadline. Correlate unpatched devices with network exposure data to identify at-risk assets.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Creation on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack vector as 'bypass[ing] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' Attackers create symlinks after initial compromise to establish persistence and evade remediation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of symbolic links in FortiOS system directories, especially in /bin, /etc, or configuration paths. Alert on symlink targets pointing to executables or persistence mechanisms. Correlate with evidence of prior filesystem compromise.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Exploitation Requests to FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is triggered 'via crafted HTTP requests' to exposed FortiOS systems. Detection should identify anomalous HTTP patterns characteristic of CVE-2025-68686 exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to FortiOS management/API endpoints containing path traversal, unusual parameter encoding, or payloads designed to trigger symbolic link creation. Baseline admin traffic patterns and alert on deviations targeting configuration-related paths.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Filesystem Access on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Detecting unauthorized filesystem access is critical for identifying the staging phase before CVE-2025-68686 is weaponized.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized filesystem writes to system directories on FortiOS outside of scheduled maintenance/patch windows. Alert on unexpected file/directory ownership changes, privilege escalation in file system context, or creation of files in restricted paths prior to symlink activity.

suggestion.title: Patch Bypass Detection via Failed Remediation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CVE-2025-68686 as a bypass of 'the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism,' meaning attackers use this CVE to prevent remediation of prior exploits. Detection should identify failed patching and rollback.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS patch application logs for failures, rollbacks, or disabled patching targeting symbolic link persistence remediation. Alert on evidence of patch-disabling attempts or configuration rollback around the time of compromised indicators.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Compliance Tracking vs. Federal Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 2026-08-10 federal patch due date and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Enterprises must track remediation progress and identify compliance gaps at scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain continuous inventory of Fortinet FortiOS instances, map exposure status (internet-facing vs. internal), track CVE-2025-68686 patch status per device, and alert on any unpatched system >30 days from deadline. Generate weekly remediation progress reports for compliance audit trail.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests Exploiting FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch...via crafted HTTP requests.' This is the primary attack vector requiring direct HTTP-pattern detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS management interfaces for HTTP requests with payloads matching symbolic-link traversal patterns (../, path manipulation, or directory bypass indicators). Establish baseline of legitimate administrative traffic; flag requests with path traversal indicators or unusual parameter encoding from unauthenticated sources.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Sensitive Information Exfiltration Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the vulnerability 'may allow...exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Detection must cover data exfiltration after successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual outbound data volume from compromised FortiOS instances. Monitor for DNS queries to suspicious domains from FortiOS hosts. Correlate large-volume egress with CVE-2025-68686 exploit attempts and filesystem-level persistence events.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch & Version Inventory Scan
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requires urgent patching; federal due date 2026-08-10. Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer'—asset inventory is the foundational hunt for this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run vulnerability scans against all FortiOS instances to identify versions vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686. Cross-reference CMDB; flag any unpatched systems post-deadline for immediate escalation. Report patch-coverage percentage against inventory.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence on Compromised FortiOS Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' and 'attacker would need first to have compromised...at filesystem level.' This describes filesystem-level persistence tactics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for creation of suspicious symbolic links in /var/www, /etc/fortisafe, or config storage directories. Detect symlinks pointing to credential files, logs, or sensitive data. Alert on link creation coinciding with filesystem-level compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: Patch Bypass & Masquerading Techniques on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'may allow...bypass the patch.' This is defense-evasion and must be detected as a distinct attack technique separate from the exploit itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests with encoding variations, header obfuscation, or payload mutation targeting the same FortiOS code path across multiple attempts. Monitor for repeated requests designed to circumvent patch signatures or WAF rules. Correlate patterns with known CVE-2025-68686 bypass tooling.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Patch Compliance Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2025-68686 and sets federal patch due date 2026-08-10. Pipeline template suggests asset-exposure hunt and scanner matching ("match against your vulnerability scanner"), but zero UCs generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and patch-management systems for FortiOS endpoints not patched against CVE-2025-68686. Escalate any findings given active in-the-wild exploitation and regulatory due-date.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request to FortiOS Symlink Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases, via crafted HTTP requests.' No UC captures the HTTP anomaly vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS request logs targeting FortiOS web interfaces for unusual request patterns, double-encoding, path traversal attempts, or headers consistent with symlink-bypass exploitation chains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Symlink Creation on FortiOS Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' as the persistence vector post-compromise. Pipeline did not surface detection for symlink creation or filesystem anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of symbolic links in FortiOS critical directories (config, binaries, init scripts). Correlate with evidence of prior compromise or failed patch validation.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploit Symlink Persistence Bypass Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker 'would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' then executes this exploit to bypass patches. Defense-evasion phase critical but absent from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect attempts to modify or bypass patch signatures or integrity checks on FortiOS via symlink redirection. Look for process execution anomalies post-link creation.

suggestion.title: Gitea: Public-only scoped token performing operations on private repository
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the vulnerability: 'public-only, write:repository token to update a private pull request head branch.' Pipeline misses the core detection: correlation between token scope (public-only) and target visibility (private). Phrase: 'The vulnerable endpoint is [on public repo] but Gitea checks the token's public-only restriction against the route repository, which is the public base repository' — missing cross-repo auth context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gitea API authentication logs for requests where token scope is 'public-only' but the target operation targets a private repository. Specifically, correlate public-repo endpoint paths (/api/v1/repos/{public}/*) with private-repo PRs in the request body or response context. Alert on scope-permission mismatches.

suggestion.title: Gitea: Token authorization scope violation detection
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability is fundamentally an authorization bypass—a token doing something its scope should not permit. Article: 'UpdatePullRequest() then authorizes the pull re[quest]' — the authorization check is insufficient. Pipeline generates traffic hunts but no auth-failure or privilege-escalation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect API responses indicating authorization failures or scope mismatches (HTTP 403, 401 with 'scope' in error message, or audit log entries showing 'permission denied'). Correlate failed attempts to escalate public-only token usage with successful attempts moments later, suggesting retry or token-refresh exploitation.

suggestion.title: Gitea: PR branch modification from unexpected token type
suggestion.rationale: The exploitation manifests as PR head-branch updates. Article describes the endpoint /pulls/{index}/update — but pipeline generates no detection of PR state changes themselves. Missing: what changed in the PR (branch pointer, target, title) and who changed it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gitea audit logs or Git reflog for PR branch pointer changes (head branch updates) initiated by API tokens marked as 'public-only' or with restricted scopes. Alert on any branch modification from such tokens, especially to private PR targets. Correlate with the /pulls/*/update endpoint POST.

suggestion.title: Gitea: Cross-repository operation correlation (public endpoint, private target)
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability exploits the fact that the endpoint is on a public repo but modifies a private one. Article: 'POST /api/v1/repos/{public-owner}/{public-repo}/pulls/{index}/update' — the base repo is public but the PR can reference private branches. No detection exists for this cross-repo mismatch pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse Gitea API request/response logs to extract repo visibility (public vs private) from both the route repo and the target PR's repo. Alert when an operation on a public repo (low-visibility) actually modifies resources in a private repo (high-visibility), especially via restricted tokens.

suggestion.title: Gitea: Application access token used outside documented scope
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1550.001 (Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token) as the mechanism. Pipeline never detects the actual misuse of the token—only the endpoint hit. Missing: token-behavior anomalies (e.g., a read-only token making writes, or a public-only token writing to private repos).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract token metadata (scope, intended use, permissions) from Gitea authentication logs. For each API request, verify that the token's declared scope matches the request context. Alert on mismatches: public-only token writing, read-only token modifying state, or token used against a repository tier (public/private) not in its allowed scope.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Fortinet FortiOS Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'remote unauthenticated attacker' access; foundational hunt to identify and inventory vulnerable FortiOS instances across network before exploitation window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query CMDB and vulnerability scanners for Fortinet FortiOS appliances. Correlate scan results with network exposure (DMZ, public-facing, internet-routable). Alert on unpatched versions. Establish baseline inventory by 2026-08-10 federal patch deadline.

suggestion.title: Malformed HTTP Requests to FortiOS Management Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'crafted HTTP requests' as attack vector; inspection of HTTP traffic to FortiOS admin/API endpoints for malformed payloads is direct exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound HTTP/HTTPS to FortiOS standard ports (80, 443, 10000, 8443) for anomalous request structure: oversized payloads, URL-encoded escapes, repeated failed auth followed by unexpected status codes, or requests matching known exploit signatures.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Creation in FortiOS Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly cites 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'; filesystem monitoring for unexpected symlink artifacts is post-compromise indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of symbolic links in FortiOS system paths (/etc, /var, /bin, /usr/bin) not correlating with scheduled maintenance or patch windows. Baseline normal link activity. Investigate links pointing to config files, binaries, or log directories.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Access on Compromised FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'; detection of anomalous read access to config, credential, and log files post-compromise indicates data exfiltration setup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor read access to FortiOS config files (system.conf, fortios.conf, admin credentials) and log stores by non-admin processes. Correlate sequential file reads over short time window. Alert if reads are followed by outbound network connections to non-authorized destinations.

suggestion.title: Child Process Execution from FortiOS Daemons
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates filesystem-level compromise requiring prior exploitation; detection of unexpected child processes spawned by FortiOS daemons (httpd, fctd) signals post-exploit command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FortiOS system processes spawning shell interpreters (/bin/sh, /bin/bash), non-standard child processes, or making unexpected outbound network connections. Baseline expected child process relationships during normal operation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Patch Deployment Compliance Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch deadline 2026-08-10; tracking remediation velocity against compliance deadline provides risk timeline and audit trail for regulated environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish patch compliance baseline: percentage of FortiOS fleet patched by each milestone. Report on systems remaining unpatched past 2026-08-10. Cross-reference unpatched systems with network exposure classification (public-IP, DMZ, or internet-facing). Escalate high-risk unpatched + exposed combinations.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article directly references CVE-2025-68686; pipeline produced zero IOC output. Minimum baseline: match CVE against vulnerability scanner results.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Fortinet FortiOS instances flagged by vulnerability scanners as susceptible to CVE-2025-68686. Correlate scanner results with asset management CMDB to prioritize exposed internet-facing instances. Federal patch due-date is 2026-08-10; flag any unpatched instances post-deadline.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence on FortiOS Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' Pipeline did not map to persistence phase. Symlink creation is a strong indicator of adversary foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of symbolic links in sensitive FortiOS directories (/etc, /var, /etc/init.d, /etc/cron.d). Alert on symlinks pointing to critical config or data files. Correlation with prior filesystem compromise attempts increases confidence.

suggestion.title: Patch Bypass Exploitation via Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism, via crafted HTTP requests.' This is weaponized exploitation; no detection logic generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect malformed or anomalous HTTP requests targeting known FortiOS vulnerable endpoints. Look for parameter fuzzing, HTTP method misuse, or requests with unusual User-Agent / Accept headers. Alert on rapid-fire requests from single source IP attempting multiple payloads.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Sensitive Information Access Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact as 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Pipeline did not map to exfiltration detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-compromise, monitor FortiOS logs for unusual access patterns: large bulk data reads, access to config/credential stores from anomalous process contexts, or VPN/CLI sessions with suspicious data export commands. Correlation with persistence indicators (symlinks) increases confidence of live breach.

suggestion.title: Two-Stage Filesystem-Level Exploitation Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Pipeline did not surface this dependency or correlation strategy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner alerts for *other* FortiOS CVEs with subsequent filesystem access anomalies and symlink creation. A 2-stage attack will show: (1) exploit attempt/success against secondary vuln, (2) filesystem-level file/dir operations within minutes, (3) symlink creation or patch-bypass HTTP requests. Time-window: 1–24 hours between stages.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Internet Exposure Audit
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status implies active wild exploitation; no network exposure hunt was generated despite relevance to initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Fortinet FortiOS appliances reachable from untrusted networks (internet-facing). Cross-reference with asset mgmt CMDB and scan for CVE-2025-68686 presence. Flag any internet-exposed, unpatched instances for immediate remediation given CISA KEV active-exploitation status and 2026-08-10 federal due-date.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure — Fortinet FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Internet-Facing Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Remote unauthenticated attacker' requires external access to FortiOS. CVE in CISA KEV means active wild exploitation. Mandatory discovery hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Fortinet FortiOS appliances reachable from untrusted networks. Correlate with vulnerability scanner confirming CVE-2025-68686 presence. Flag unpatched instances (patch due 2026-08-10).

suggestion.title: Exploit Detection — Crafted HTTP Requests Targeting FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article: exploitation occurs 'via crafted HTTP requests' to bypass patch. Requires HTTP-layer detection for attack payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous HTTP to FortiOS admin/API endpoints from external IP: unusual User-Agents, malformed headers, path traversal sequences, or probing known vulnerable FortiOS interfaces.

suggestion.title: Persistence Bypass — Symbolic Link Traversal in FortiOS Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker 'bypass[es] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' Requires filesystem-layer detection for symlink abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Fortinet logs for symlink creation/access, directory traversal attempts (../ sequences), or modifications to bootstrap/startup files post-exploitation. Correlate with HTTP exploit attempts.

suggestion.title: Data Exposure — Unauthorized Access to FortiOS Configuration/Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article: vulnerability enables 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Detect post-exploitation data collection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on access to FortiOS config files, credential stores, VPN profiles, firewall rules, or backup locations following successful exploitation. Detect exports or transfers of sensitive data to external IPs.

suggestion.title: Prerequisite Compromise — Initial Filesystem-Level Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Prerequisite compromise must be hunted separately.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for signs of prior FortiOS compromise: unexpected filesystem modifications, privilege escalation in Fortinet processes, suspicious system file writes, authentication anomalies from privileged accounts. Cross-reference with other FortiOS CVEs published concurrently.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Exposed to Internet — Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes that remote unauthenticated attackers target exposed instances; no existing UC covers asset-exposure baseline. Article explicitly recommends template-based hunts for 'standard asset-exposure' pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify FortiOS appliances (via banner-grabbing on known ports, management interface paths, or cloud metadata) accessible from untrusted networks. Correlate with unpatched status (missing post-2026-08-10 patches for CVE-2025-68686).

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests Against FortiOS Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states exploitation occurs 'via crafted HTTP requests' — this is the execution phase but no UC exists. Primary attack surface for T1190.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS for HTTP requests with anomalous patterns: non-standard methods, payloads in unusual header positions, path traversal syntax, or requests to sensitive paths (e.g., /admin, /api/cmdb) from unexpected source IPs. False positives likely from automated scanners; baseline against legitimate administrative traffic.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Manipulation in FortiOS Startup/Config Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' as post-exploit persistence vector; attacker 'bypass[es] the patch developed for' this. No UC captures this defense-evasion persistence technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect symlink creation or modification in FortiOS startup directories, config paths, or plugin directories. Focus on symlinks pointing to unexpected locations (parent directories, /tmp, world-writable paths). Baseline: FortiOS init should not traverse symlinks outside of official paths.

suggestion.title: Filesystem-Level Compromise Preceding CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' — indicates RCE or file-write primitive that enables the HTTP-based exploit. This two-stage requirement is critical for detection but no UC addresses the initial foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized file modifications in critical FortiOS directories (especially scripts, binaries, config parsers), unexpected process execution (especially interpreters spawning from system paths), or privilege escalation attempts. Temporal correlation: if filesystem compromise precedes HTTP exploitation, timeline clustering strengthens verdict.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Administrative Access to FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated attacker' and 'bypass the patch' suggests circumventing both authentication and patch-level defenses. Authentication bypass or credential reuse is a detection gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful administrative/root access from IPs lacking prior successful authentication, or access from unexpected geographic locations / ASNs. Flag any admin session immediately after failed authentication attempts (suggests auth bypass exploit). Correlate with unpatched status.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: CVE title explicitly states 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor' — requires detection of what FortiOS considers sensitive (VPN configs, user credentials, network topology, logs) leaving the appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual egress of config/credential files, VPN keys, user databases, or audit logs from FortiOS instances to external IPs. Baseline: administrative data should only leave via legitimate backup channels (authenticated, to known destinations). Any exfiltration to residential/VPS IPs is high-confidence.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerable Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt.' No scanner-based detection was generated despite this being the primary hunting vector for a CISA KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Fortinet FortiOS instances and cross-reference against CVE-2025-68686 vulnerability database. Flag instances without patches confirmed as-of federal due date 2026-08-10 as critical risk. Prioritize internet-exposed or DMZ-adjacent instances.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests to FortiOS (CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'via crafted HTTP requests' as the active exploitation vector. No HTTP/proxy-level detection use case exists to catch in-flight exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to FortiOS admin interfaces for anomalous request signatures: path traversal patterns, double-encoded URIs, oversized payloads, or requests to sensitive endpoints from unexpected sources. Correlate with FortiOS error logs for exploitation artifacts.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' This persistence layer was not captured; pipeline omitted the persistence kill-chain phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for symlink creation/manipulation in config, log, or system directories. Detect processes operating on symlinked paths or unusual ln/link syscalls. Compare against baseline; symlinks in FortiOS are indicators of post-exploitation hardening.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Disclosure from FortiOS (CVE-2025-68686 Impact)
suggestion.rationale: Article defines impact as 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor,' but no data-access or exfiltration detection was generated. Impact phase is missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized access to sensitive FortiOS files (config, credentials, logs, state files). Correlate file reads with suspicious HTTP sessions or symlink abuse. Flag bulk reads or archiving of system data as data exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Multi-CVE Exploitation Chain: Prior FortiOS Vulnerability → CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' The two-stage attack (initial compromise + secondary exploitation) should be modeled as a kill-chain correlation rule, but pipeline shows no phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FortiOS instances with evidence of prior successful exploitation (e.g., unexpected filesystem modifications, privilege escalation artifacts, suspicious process history) followed by HTTP requests matching CVE-2025-68686 exploitation signatures. Treat as multi-stage attack.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Symbolic Link Persistence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'—this is a second-stage persistence technique that requires direct detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous symbolic link creation or modification on FortiOS systems, particularly in config directories or startup paths. Correlation with failed HTTP requests in the same timeframe raises confidence—attacker may be re-establishing persistence after patch disruption.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Crafted HTTP Request Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly stated: 'via crafted HTTP requests'—this is the bypass mechanism after symlink patching. Must detect HTTP patterns consistent with path traversal or encoding tricks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to FortiOS instances with unusual path encoding (double-slash, Unicode, percent-encoding), directory traversal patterns (../ sequences), or suspicious parameter inflation. Baseline clean request patterns first.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Sensitive Information Exposure to Unauthorized Principals
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly named 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor'—need to detect when sensitive data leaves protected contexts (config files, credential stores, policy databases).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS for large or unusual reads of configuration files, policy databases, or VPN credential stores. Correlate with HTTP exfiltration patterns or data staging on the filesystem. Alert on any egress of files containing API keys or encrypted credentials.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise FortiOS Filesystem-Level Access Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'—this implies prior compromise chain (likely CVE+RCE). Must detect suspicious filesystem activity that indicates execution context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious file enumeration, permission changes, or access to restricted system directories on FortiOS after other CVE exploitation is suspected. Focus on /etc/config, /etc/ssl, and application binary directories. Correlate with web server or process activity.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP POST to TeamCity Admin Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Run OS Commands Without Logging In'—attackers exploit an unauthenticated endpoint. Must detect HTTP POST/GET requests to TeamCity administration paths (e.g., /teamcity/admin, /guestLogin.html) from external or low-privilege sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to TeamCity admin endpoints that succeed (HTTP 200–299) without prior successful authentication event. Baseline legitimate admin access, alert on spike from external IPs or anomalous user agents.

suggestion.title: OS Command Execution from TeamCity Process
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly: 'Run OS Commands.' TeamCity process (TeamCity.exe, teamcityd) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or shell without prior human action on agent/server indicates exploitation or post-compromise lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child process creation from TeamCity service account spawning interpreters (cmd, PowerShell, bash) with suspicious arguments (encoded strings, base64, network callbacks). Exclude known build configurations.

suggestion.title: Rapid Web Service Restart Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation may trigger service recovery, reboot, or log clearing. Detect abnormal TeamCity service lifecycle events (restart, stop/start within minutes) coupled with preceding HTTP activity to admin paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate TeamCity HTTP 200 responses to admin endpoints within 1–10 minutes of TeamCity service stop/restart events. Alert if no known maintenance ticket or scheduled deployment.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File/Script Creation in TeamCity Build Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated RCE allows attacker to drop payloads into build output directories. Detect .ps1, .bat, .exe, .jar creation in TeamCity artifact/build paths with timestamps correlating to exploitation HTTP requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity artifact directories (typically /buildAgent/work, /artifacts) for new executable or script files created outside normal build window. Correlate creation time with HTTP exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: Reverse Shell or Out-of-Band Command Callback from TeamCity Host
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attacker may establish persistence or interactive access via reverse shell or DNS/HTTP callback to C2. Alert on unexpected outbound connections from TeamCity process to suspicious external IPs/domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections from TeamCity process (or child processes) to non-whitelisted external IPs/domains, especially on ports 443, 8080, 4444, or DNS queries for newly registered/suspicious domains.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Build Configuration Modification
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation may be used to inject malicious build steps into CI/CD pipelines to compromise downstream systems. Detect modifications to build config files without corresponding UI admin session or VCS commit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on changes to .teamcity/settings.kts, build configuration XML, or build step parameters not preceded by authenticated TeamCity admin login or corresponding git push event.

suggestion.title: Suspicious tc Command Execution with Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article core: 'race into root exploit' via traffic-control subsystem; pipeline generated zero use cases despite mention of unprivileged-to-root escalation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for tc (traffic control) commands spawned by unprivileged users, especially with rapid file descriptor manipulation or system calls that trigger race conditions. Flag if process token privilege level increases post-execution or if child processes inherit root context.

suggestion.title: Kernel Race Condition via inotify/fanotify File Descriptor Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'race condition' in traffic control; common pattern exploited through inotify/fanotify watchers combined with file operations. Pipeline omitted kernel-level exploitation technique detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid inotify_add_watch / inotify_rm_watch syscall sequences from non-root processes, paired with concurrent write/unlink operations on /etc/passwd, /etc/sudoers, or network config files. Flag race-window exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Local Privilege Escalation via Network Namespace Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'traffic-control' (tc, qdisc) as attack surface; tc operates on network namespaces and netlink interface. Pipeline failed to model detection for netlink-based kernel exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for netlink socket operations (NETLINK_ROUTE family) from unprivileged processes, especially crafted qdisc/tc filter additions with unusual callback or classid values that may trigger kernel UAF/OOB conditions.

suggestion.title: Process Privilege Token Elevation via Kernel Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'root exploit'; pipeline generated no use case for privilege token changes. Core attack chain is unprivileged→root, not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process token privilege transitions where a process spawned by unprivileged user (UID 1000+) gains UID 0 ownership without sudo/su invocation or credential delegation. Correlate with suspicious syscall volume immediately prior.

suggestion.title: AI-Assisted Exploit Toolchain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline emphasizes 'AI helped develop' exploit; pipeline should flag AI code-generation patterns in discovered payloads or implants (e.g., ChatGPT-like variable naming, template-generated shellcode signatures).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect compressed/encoded payloads with entropy patterns consistent with LLM-generated code (repetitive function preambles, stereotyped error handling). Cross-reference discovered exploit scripts against known AI model output signatures.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of tc Qdisc Command Injection via Malformed Filter Syntax
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'traffic-control' as the vulnerable subsystem; no detection use case for command/filter injection in tc operations (e.g., qdisc add, filter add with malformed class/action specs).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor tc command-line invocations for suspicious syntax: nested backticks, shell metacharacters in class/filter IDs, unusual action targets (e.g., action bpf with inline eBPF payloads). Correlate with kernel error log spikes.

suggestion.title: DLL Search-Order Hijacking via SspiCli.dll Impersonation (NightLedger)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The implant masquerades as SspiCli.dll and appears to be designed for DLL search-order hijacking, targeting a legitimate AppVShNotify.exe binary.' This is explicit persistence/execution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SspiCli.dll load attempts from non-system directories, especially when triggered by RPCRT4.dll delay-loading during RPC authentication calls in AppVShNotify.exe context. Detect unsigned or timestomped SspiCli.dll in unexpected paths.

suggestion.title: WebSocket-Based Tunneling Command and Control (BridgeHead/ArcBridge)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'two custom WebSocket-based tunnelers, ArcBridge and BridgeHead, for covert network access and operator-controlled tunneling' as primary C2 mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WebSocket upgrade handshakes over HTTP/HTTPS to C2 infrastructure. Flag persistent bidirectional WebSocket connections from compromised aerospace/aviation sectors. Correlate WebSocket tunnel establishment with preceding DLL hijacking events.

suggestion.title: Recruitment-Themed Spear-Phishing Lures Targeting Defense/Aerospace Sectors
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'recruitment-themed content impersonating trusted brands and hiring platforms, as well as lookalike videoconferencing pages that redirected victims to malicious archives hosted on third-party file-sharing services.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails with recruitment/hiring-themed subject lines and attachments targeting aerospace, aviation, defense, telecom sectors across Middle East/Africa. Flag links to lookalike videoconferencing domains redirecting to file-sharing services. Alert on high-confidence phishing infrastructure impersonating LinkedIn, Indeed, or Zoom.

suggestion.title: Malware Distribution via Third-Party File-Sharing Services Post-Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article states lures 'redirected victims to malicious archives hosted on third-party file-sharing services,' indicating secondary delivery mechanism following initial phishing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor downloads from Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive, Box for archive files (ZIP, RAR) linked from phishing emails. Flag immediate archive extraction and spawning of unsigned executables or DLL loads. Correlate timing with phishing campaign detection.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Capabilities via NightLedger Backdoor (Process Discovery, Screenshot Capture)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies NightLedger enables 'reconnaissance, command execution, file operations, process discovery, and screenshot capture,' indicating discovery phase commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process enumeration commands (tasklist, Get-Process, ps) originating from AppVShNotify.exe child processes. Detect screenshot API calls (BitBlt, ScreenCaptureAPI) from unusual parent processes. Flag file enumeration (dir, ls, find) chained with network exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Deployment of BridgeHead Tunneler in Victim Environments
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'BridgeHead being deployed during post-exploitation activities in victim environments in Egypt and at a Pakistan-based aerospace and aviation organization.' Indicates lateral movement/persistence phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In post-compromise detection, flag BridgeHead tunneler deployment alongside reconnaissance commands. Monitor for WebSocket listener establishment on internal network segments following initial NightLedger compromise. Correlate with aerospace/aviation IP ranges in Egypt and Pakistan.

suggestion.title: VeloCloud Orchestrator Process Execution from Network
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'command injection flaw'—exploitation would trigger abnormal process spawning from VeloCloud service context (e.g. `velocloud` user executing `cmd.exe`, `/bin/sh`, or `powershell`). No detection UC generated despite clear RCE attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes created by VeloCloud Orchestrator services (w/ parent: velocloud/orchestrator process). Flag execution of shells, interpreters, or encoded payload runners outside expected maintenance windows. High fidelity signal in enterprise networks where VeloCloud is appliance-only.

suggestion.title: VeloCloud HTTP Request Parameter Fuzzing or Injection Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'command injection'—exploitation involves HTTP parameter tampering. Pipeline missed detection for malformed or special-char-heavy request payloads targeting known VeloCloud API endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP POST/GET requests to VeloCloud admin or API endpoints (e.g. `/api/`, `/rest/`) for command metacharacters: `; | & $ ( ) < > \n \r`. Correlate with 400/500 error responses followed by 200 OK—signature of fuzz→exploitation sequence.

suggestion.title: Network Egress from VeloCloud to Rare/Malicious Destinations
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE, attacker typically establishes C2 or exfiltration channel. Article doesn't specify IOCs but pipeline should infer callback detection for compromised orchestrator appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline VeloCloud network egress (DNS, NTP, vendor update servers). Alert on new destinations with high reputation risk, tor exit nodes, or dynamic DNS. High-value indicator if VeloCloud is air-gapped or restricted-egress in topology.

suggestion.title: VeloCloud Service Restart or Crash Following Exploit Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Failed injection attempts or exploit edge cases often crash the orchestrator. Pipeline should have suggested monitoring service health events as a leading indicator of active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track VeloCloud Orchestrator service crashes, unexpected restarts, or hang events within minutes of suspicious HTTP requests. Combine with failed login spikes or auth errors to triangulate exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Arista VeloCloud Configuration or Credential Export
suggestion.rationale: RCE via command injection likely enables attacker to extract running config, credentials, or customer VPN keys stored on orchestrator. Pipeline missed post-exploitation data exfil use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file reads of `/opt/velocloud/config/`, `/etc/velocloud/`, or registry hives containing orchestrator secrets. Track unusual tar/zip/scp operations from velocloud process context targeting external IPs or DNS queries for pastebin/data-exfil domains.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Authentication or Privilege Elevation Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: After command execution foothold, attacker typically moves laterally or escalates. Pipeline omitted user/service account creation or sudo/privilege escalation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new local user creation or `sudo` invocations originating from web service context (velocloud user). Look for `useradd`, `net user`, or service-account password changes coinciding with HTTP exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Blockchain-based C2 Beaconing Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Dysphoria IoT Botnet Adds Blockchain C2' — a novel persistence and evasion mechanism post-disruption. Pipeline failed to generate detection for this core attack innovation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect IoT devices performing unusual blockchain network queries or peer-to-peer protocol handshakes indicative of C2 beaconing. Look for DNS queries to blockchain nodes, unusual outbound connections to known blockchain networks (Ethereum, Bitcoin testnet), or patterns of encoded command exfiltration over ledger-based channels.

suggestion.title: Victim Relay Node Identification
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Victim Relays' as post-disruption infrastructure replacement. No use case captures detection of compromised endpoints acting as intermediate C2 nodes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify IoT or end-user devices exhibiting relay behavior: forwarding unusual traffic patterns to external IPs with low payload variance, establishing persistent bidirectional connections, or spawning child processes that bind to listening ports. Correlate inbound C2 traffic with outbound relay to third parties.

suggestion.title: IoT Exploitation and Dysphoria Botnet Infection
suggestion.rationale: Title references 'Dysphoria IoT Botnet' but no detection use case for initial compromise or infection indicators. Article body mentions infection post-disruption resilience.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IoT devices (routers, cameras, NAS, industrial controllers) for execution of shell scripts or interpreted code with network exfiltration, credential enumeration (passwd/shadow reads), or privilege escalation attempts. Correlate with known Dysphoria-associated domains, file hashes, or behavioral fingerprints.

suggestion.title: Post-Disruption C2 Resurrection and Network Reconstitution
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'After JackSkid Disruption' — a behavioral shift from centralized to blockchain-based relay model. No use case detects rapid infrastructure migration or resurrection patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track clusters of previously silent or sinkholed IoT malware nodes suddenly resuming outbound communication with new C2 endpoints, particularly to blockchain networks or peer-to-peer infrastructure. Correlate timing with known disruption events.

suggestion.title: Peer-to-Peer Botnet Mesh Network Formation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes victim relays and blockchain C2 as decentralized infrastructure. No use case detects mesh network topology or peer-node enrollment patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify compromised nodes establishing high-cardinality connections to geographically dispersed peers with consistent port sequences, low-bandwidth heartbeat traffic, or packet patterns consistent with distributed hash table (DHT) or gossip protocols indicative of botnet mesh membership.

suggestion.title: Certificate Requests with Non-DC CDC Values
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'systems previously did not verify that the server supplied through the attacker-controlled cdc value was a legitimate domain controller' and attackers 'direct the CA to the attacker-controlled system, and return false directory information for a targeted machine account.' CDC manipulation is the exploit root cause.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag AD CS certificate enrollment requests where the Client DC (CDC) attribute resolves to a system not registered as a domain controller in Active Directory, or where CDC IP/hostname maps to non-DC subnets. Cross-reference certificate request timestamps against AD computer object creation time.

suggestion.title: PKINIT Kerberos Auth as Domain Controller from Non-DC
suggestion.rationale: Article states PoC 'authenticate through PKINIT as the targeted domain controller' using certificate and 'the attacker can...perform privileged Active Directory operations.' Direct authentication anomaly indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Kerberos TGT requests (AS-REQ) with PKINIT pre-authentication where the requested principal is a domain controller account (CN=DC$) but source IP is not a known domain controller. Alert on certificate-based auth to DC accounts from user workstations or non-DC servers.

suggestion.title: DCSync Replication Initiated by Non-Domain-Controller
suggestion.rationale: Attack outcome: 'the attacker can request account secrets, including the krbtgt secret' via 'Impacket's secretsdump tool to perform a DCSync attack.' GetNCChanges replication from unexpected principals is the detection window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Directory Replication Service (DRS) GetNCChanges operations for directory replication requests originating from systems not holding the domain controller role. Alert on replication of sensitive container attributes (cn=krbtgt) requested from non-DC sources with any authentication method.

suggestion.title: Machine Account Creation by Low-Privilege Users
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'A low-privileged user first creates a machine account, which is permitted under the default ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota configuration' and 'A machine account created through the default ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota setting is a valid domain principal.' This is the attack entry point and exploit enabler.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline expected machine account creators (service accounts, admin groups). Alert on machine account creation by end users, service accounts not in authorized groups, or accounts outside network administration organizational units. Flag creation of multiple machine accounts by single user within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Kerberos Credential Cache Files (.ccache) on Windows Systems
suggestion.rationale: PoC workflow: 'saving the resulting Kerberos credentials to a .ccache file' for subsequent credential reuse. .ccache files are Unix/Linux-native and not standard on Windows, indicating attacker tools like certighost.py or Impacket.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation or access of .ccache files on Windows systems, which indicates credential caching via non-native tools (likely Impacket or certighost.py). Correlate .ccache file creation with PKINIT authentication attempts or certificate enrollment activity.

suggestion.title: Rogue LDAP/LSA/SMB Services Responding to CA Requests
suggestion.rationale: Attack mechanism: 'run rogue SMB, LSA, and LDAP services, direct the CA to the attacker-controlled system, and return false directory information.' These services are the 'chase' mechanism exploitation enabler.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect LDAP (port 389/636), LSA (port 445 SMB), or NETLOGON services running from user-context processes or on non-standard ports. Monitor outbound connections from AD CS server to non-DC systems on LDAP/SMB ports. Alert on service creation by non-SYSTEM accounts for directory services.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'crafted HTTP requests' as the attack vector and 'remote unauthenticated attacker' as the threat actor capability. No HTTP-based detection UC was generated despite this being the primary delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP requests with abnormal patterns (high payload sizes, suspicious headers, or known exploit signatures) targeting FortiOS default paths or admin interfaces. suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal HTTP traffic to FortiOS admin console (/admin, /api/v2 endpoints). Alert on malformed requests, unusual URI paths, requests with atypical parameter combinations, or payloads attempting to trigger symlink-related code paths. Flag requests that bypass standard authentication flows or target protected resources.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to FortiOS Sensitive Information
suggestion.rationale: CVE title explicitly addresses 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor.' Pipeline produced no detection for exfiltration or unauthorized access to credentials, configs, or routing data post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS for unauthorized read/export operations on sensitive files: system.conf, certificates, VPN credentials, firewall rules, routing tables, admin credentials vault. Alert on bulk reads, copy commands, or access from unexpected processes or external connections. Correlate with filesystem-level compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: Patch Bypass Indicators on FortiOS Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability exploits systems 'via crafted HTTP requests' to 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' Pipeline did not generate detection for patched-but-still-vulnerable indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track FortiOS patch level and version. Alert if system reports patched status for CVE-2025-68686 but still exhibits symbolic link anomalies, old binary hashes, or unexpected code path execution. Flag rollback or downgrade attempts that would re-expose the vulnerability.

suggestion.title: Malicious Release Tag Redirection to Orphaned Commits
suggestion.rationale: "The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit, which was the orphaned commit" — GitHub Action tags moved to commits not on main/protected branches is a key obfuscation technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub repositories for release tag deletions and creations, especially when new tags point to commits not reachable from main/master branches. Correlate tag movements with unusual commit orphaning patterns. Alert when a single commit is retargeted by multiple version tags (e.g., v34, v35, v36 all pointing to same malicious commit).

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit Detection in Public Repositories
suggestion.rationale: "Having the attack commit orphaned from any branches, including the main branch... factors added a bit of obfuscation" — commits existing outside branch history enable hiding of malicious code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan repository commit graphs for commits reachable via tags but not from any branch. Flag orphaned commits especially when they appear in widely-used action repositories. Correlate with recent write access and any associated tag operations.

suggestion.title: Unexpected External Network Calls from GitHub Actions Workflows
suggestion.rationale: "The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity." External calls from Actions are detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions execution logs for unexpected curl, wget, or network-based download commands pulling from external domains. Baseline typical network behavior per repository and action. Flag new external domains contacted by established actions or unusual network patterns in CI/CD workflows.

suggestion.title: Plaintext Secret Exposure in GitHub Actions Logs
suggestion.rationale: "attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit that caused encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs" — GitHub secrets should never surface unencrypted in log output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions logs for patterns matching secret formats (common patterns: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=, token=, password=, oauth_token). Alert on secrets appearing outside expected redaction. Cross-reference with repository secret definitions to identify specific leaked credentials.

suggestion.title: GitHub Action Repository Write Access Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: "An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit..." Direct write access to high-impact repositories is the critical enabler; monitor for privilege escalation or account compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual write operations to GitHub repositories used by >1000 downstream repositories (identify via dependency graph). Alert on new collaborators added with write access, unexpected commits from known accounts, or access pattern changes. Correlate with releases and tag modifications.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Attack via Trusted GitHub Action Compromise
suggestion.rationale: "About 23,000 GitHub repos use this Action... An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo" — compromising a single widely-trusted component cascades to thousands of dependent workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify high-impact GitHub Actions (used by >5000 repositories). Monitor for sudden changes to action code, new external dependencies, or network activity. Track downstream execution of modified actions across dependent repositories. Alert when a single malicious action version affects thousands of workflows simultaneously.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2025-68686 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' This is the primary detection mechanism for identifying at-risk FortiOS instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any FortiOS instance detected as vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686 in active vulnerability scans. High priority given CISA KEV status and 2026-08-10 federal patch deadline.

suggestion.title: FortiOS HTTP Exploitation Bypass Attempts

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual or malformed HTTP requests to FortiOS admin/API endpoints, particularly POST/PUT requests with executable content or symlink references, following filesystem access indicators.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistency Exploitation

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem logs for suspicious symlink creation or modification, particularly in web-accessible directories or config paths. Cross-correlate with preceding filesystem access.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Attack Chain: Dual-Vulnerability Exploitation

Correlate with corporate asset inventory to identify unmanaged or non-patched instances. Alert on any FortiOS asset not behind corporate WAF or access control list.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation via Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector as 'via crafted HTTP requests' to bypass published patch. Need signature-based detection on request payload anomalies.

Alert on any successful response (2xx) to anomalous requests targeting `/api/`, `/system/`, or `/admin/` paths.
