suggestion.title: Detect CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation via Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation occurs 'via crafted HTTP requests' to bypass the patch. Pipeline missed HTTP-level attack surface detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS-facing HTTP/HTTPS traffic for request patterns consistent with symbolic-link traversal or privilege-bypass payloads. Baseline normal admin HTTP activity and alert on deviations targeting sensitive paths.

suggestion.title: Detect Symbolic Link Persistence/Evasion Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' and attacker 'bypass[es] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' This is an explicit evasion/persistence vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation/modification of symbolic links in privileged directories (/etc, /lib, /bin, /usr/lib) on FortiOS systems. Correlate with execution of symlink-creation tools (ln, ln -s) by Fortinet service accounts. Alert on symlinks pointing outside expected scope.

suggestion.title: Hunt for Prior Filesystem-Level Compromise (Two-Stage Attack)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' This prerequisite attack chain is undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On FortiOS hosts, detect writes to privileged paths (/root, /etc, admin config dirs) followed by unexpected process execution or child-process spawning. Look for shells or interpreters invoked from anomalous write locations. Correlate timeline with CVE-2025-68686 exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Detect Patch Bypass or Post-Patch Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability allows 'bypass [of] the patch.' This implies detection of attempts to circumvent patched systems or exploit via alternative techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP request patterns known to bypass the published patch (e.g., double-encoding, alternative path traversal vectors). Cross-check patch version from vulnerability scanner against actual HTTP behavior to identify instances where patch claims are false.

suggestion.title: Exposed IPMI/Redfish Service on UDP 623 (CVE-2013-4786)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Looking for publicly accessible IPMI services on UDP port 623' and identifies 36,872 internet-exposed hosts. CVE-2013-4786 is the root cause enabling offline password cracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound connections to UDP port 623 from untrusted networks. Correlate with IPMI protocol signatures. Flag any public-routable infrastructure responding to IPMI discovery probes or authentication requests. High-risk if Supermicro or HPE BMC identified.

suggestion.title: Weak/Default BMC Credentials Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies '6,240 of the hosts accepted an empty username' and '2,340 instances used weak administrator passwords that matched public dictionaries.' Supermicro factory passwords are 10-character uppercase printed on chassis labels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful BMC authentication with default usernames ('ADMIN', 'root', etc.) or empty usernames. Detect multiple failed IPMI authentication attempts followed by success. Monitor for authentication events using credentials matching known factory password patterns for Supermicro/HPE hardware.

suggestion.title: Offline Password Cracking of IPMI Auth Response (CVE-2013-4786)
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'request an authentication response that can be used to crack the password offline using dedicated GPU rigs.' 24,650 servers leaked password-derived authentication material; estimated 1 day per response on M3 for HPE iLO.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect IPMI authentication handshakes where challenge-response pairs are captured (RAKP protocol). Alert if a single source harvests multiple IPMI auth responses from different BMCs. Correlate exfiltration of auth captures with known password-cracking infrastructure or GPU cloud provisioning.

suggestion.title: Suspicious BMC Lateral Movement and Pivot Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'a single compromised BMC could serve as a pivot point to the broader management plane' and 'recovered credentials may work across multiple management interfaces within the same environment.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for BMC sessions accessing other management infrastructure (other BMCs, Redfish APIs, SNMP, Syslog servers). Flag cross-management-network lateral connections from a single BMC credential. Alert on API calls from BMC IPs to production network infrastructure.

suggestion.title: BMC Firmware Update or System Configuration Change Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes BMCs enable 'applying malicious firmware updates' and 'change low-level configurations' at a layer not monitored by security solutions. This is the primary impact of successful compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any firmware update initiated on a BMC outside of planned change windows. Flag unauthorized server power state changes, virtual media mount operations, or boot-order modifications from remote IPMI sessions. Baseline administrator actions and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Accessible HPE iLO or Supermicro Web Interface with Ransom Demand
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'an internet-exposed HPE iLO 4 login page displaying a ransom note demanding 0.3 BTC'—evidence of active exploitation in the wild and post-compromise asset defacement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS access to BMC web interfaces from external IPs. Alert on unusual file uploads or content modifications to iLO or Supermicro web portals. Correlate with monitoring for defacement indicators (ransom notes, cryptocurrency addresses in text content).

suggestion.title: NightLedger Process Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'NightLedger' malware deployment. No execution detection UC generated despite this being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for NightLedger process spawning with suspicious command-line arguments or parent process anomalies. Correlate against known malware file hashes and execution paths.

suggestion.title: Covert Relay Traffic Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article subtitle states victims are 'turned into covert relays'—implies outbound C2 relay traffic and lateral forwarding. No detection UC for relay behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify victim systems forwarding traffic on behalf of attacker (port forwarding, proxy behavior). Look for outbound connections to known Nimbus Manticore infrastructure and abnormal egress patterns from internal systems.

suggestion.title: NightLedger Persistence Mechanism Detection
suggestion.rationale: Malware named in title must establish persistence on victim systems for relay functionality. No persistence UC surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry/startup folder modifications, scheduled task creation, or service installation consistent with NightLedger persistence patterns. Cross-reference with malware family analysis.

suggestion.title: Relay Infrastructure Enumeration & Setup
suggestion.rationale: Article describes victims as 'covert relays'—implies attackers configuring victim systems for traffic forwarding. No UC for relay provisioning phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution for network configuration (netsh, iptables, ipconfig, route commands) shortly after NightLedger installation. Monitor for suspicious port forwarding or proxy tool execution.

suggestion.title: NightLedger C2 Beacon Detection
suggestion.rationale: Covert relay deployment implies ongoing C2 communication to orchestrate relay behavior. No C2 beacon or checkin UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Profile C2 beacon traffic patterns (frequency, size, TLS certificate anomalies, known NightLedger domains/IPs). Detect abnormal encrypted traffic from newly compromised hosts.

suggestion.title: Trojanized MeshAgent WebSocket C2 Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'trojanized MeshAgent binary as their primary C2 mechanism...installed as a SYSTEM-level auto-start service, communicating over encrypted WebSocket (WSS) to an attacker-controlled server.' This is a specific, novel attacker pattern requiring behavior-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for MeshAgent (meshagent.exe, meshcentral-agent) processes spawned with SYSTEM privileges outside legitimate MeshCentral deployment contexts. Correlate with outbound WebSocket (WSS on port 443 or non-standard) connections to suspicious IP space. Alert if MeshAgent registers as auto-start service (Registry: SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services) without corresponding ServicePrincipalName or legitimate domain enrollment.

suggestion.title: QR Code Phishing via Trusted Cloud Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article details: 'compromised Microsoft 365 accounts to harvest credentials...auto-generated, victim-tailored PDF documents containing QR codes that direct to adversary-controlled M365 credential harvesting pages.' UAT-11764 leverages trusted SharePoint for document hosting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with PDF attachments containing QR codes redirecting to /device_code or similar OAuth flows hosted on compromised Microsoft infrastructure (*.sharepoint.com, *.onedrive.com domains). Cross-reference recipient domain with sender to identify internal account compromise. Flag if QR destination leads to blank credential forms or custom M365 login replicas.

suggestion.title: Zoho Assist Unattended Agent Abuse Without User Session
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Warlock ransomware operators...deploying an installer for the RMM tool Zoho Assist Unattended Agent, which is designed to allow administrative remote control of an endpoint without a user logged in...enables the attackers to maintain persistent, stealthy, and unrestricted control.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Zoho Assist Unattended Agent installation (ZohoAssist.exe, ZohoAssistMsiInstaller) outside standard change management windows. Monitor for Zoho Assist establishing connections when no user is interactively logged in (SessionId 0 in Windows). Flag registry persistence mechanisms (SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services or HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run) created by Zoho Assist post-install.

suggestion.title: ARToken PhaaS Device Code Authentication Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals: 'ARToken panel exposes 80+ API endpoints for device code phishing...phishing lures that impersonate trusted vendors and abuse legitimate Microsoft services, allowing attackers to bypass MFA through the OAuth device authorization flow.' Describes specific PhaaS capability and MFA-bypass mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Azure AD logs for device code flow (grant_type=device_code) from atypical geographies or IPs. Correlate successful device code auth within 5 minutes of user receiving phishing template matching ARToken lures (vendor impersonation patterns). Alert if device code converts to interactive token for subsequent OAuth scopes (Mail.Read, SharePoint.Manage). Check for follow-on inbox rule creation within 10 minutes post-auth.

suggestion.title: GPO Logon Script Ransomware Deployment - Domain-Wide Encryption
suggestion.rationale: Article details: 'actor moved laterally...leveraging a service account...ultimately deployed the ransomware across the entire domain using a malicious Group Policy Object (GPO) logon script...encryption of systems with the .SINOBI file extension.' Specific attack pattern with IOC (file extension).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid file creation across multiple hosts with .SINOBI extension within 1-hour window. Correlate with GPO logon script modifications (track gpt.ini hash changes on SYSVOL). Alert if powershell.exe or cmd.exe spawns as child of explorer.exe (logon script context) with encoding or obfuscation indicators. Monitor for service account execution of ransomware binaries outside normal business hours.

suggestion.title: Service Account Credential Theft via NTDS.dit Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'leveraging a service account with a weak, easily cracked password obtained from the domain credential store, ntds.dit.' Describes credential dump and lateral movement mechanism used in Sinobi attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ntds.dit file access outside authorized BACKUP or replication contexts. Monitor for ntlm.exe, mimikatz.exe, or hashdump utilities spawning processes that read ntds.dit. Detect RDP/WinRM logon immediately following ntds.dit access using service account credentials. Flag service accounts with NTLMv2 hashes crackable in <5 minutes (entropy check) or plaintext storage in LDAP attributes.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated TeamCity API Call
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Without Logging In'—explicit unauthenticated access vector. Pipeline must detect API requests to TeamCity endpoints that lack Authorization headers or auth tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to TeamCity paths (/api/v1/, /buildConfiguration, /buildQueue) with missing or malformed auth tokens. Correlate with successful command execution in subsequent logs to identify exploitation.

suggestion.title: OS Command Execution from TeamCity Process
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Run OS Commands'—the core attack payload. Pipeline should detect spawned shells (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) from TeamCity/build-agent parent processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child process creation from teamcity.exe, java.exe (TeamCity JVM), or buildAgent processes. Flag execution of shell interpreters, wget/curl downloads, or encoded PowerShell scripts originating from CI runtime.

suggestion.title: Exploit Payload Probe Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Critical flaws attract rapid scanning. Pipeline should surface HTTP POST/GET sequences with injection payloads or expression-language markers targeting TeamCity endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous request sequences to TeamCity: multiple 40x responses followed by 200 from same source IP, requests containing Java deserialization markers, ${} template injection strings, or known RCE signatures (e.g., 'Runtime.getRuntime').

suggestion.title: Suspicious Build Configuration Modification
suggestion.rationale: RCE likely requires injecting malicious build steps. Pipeline should flag unauthorized additions to buildTypes.xml or build step definitions outside change-control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to .buildTypes files, build.gradle injection, or pre-commit hooks in repos linked to TeamCity projects. Correlate with anonymous/unauthenticated API calls in audit logs.

suggestion.title: Source Code / Secrets Exfiltration from CI Server
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE on TeamCity grants access to source repositories, API keys, and build artifacts stored on-disk. Pipeline must detect data staging and exfil.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large file transfers (>100MB) from TeamCity server to external IPs, especially compressed archives or Git clones. Flag HTTPS POST requests with credentials/keys to external URLs during exploit window.

suggestion.title: Default / Unauthenticated Account Usage
suggestion.rationale: Flaw described as 'Without Logging In' suggests bypassed auth or default creds. Pipeline should surface auth log gaps or guest-account exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication.log entries where TeamCity commands succeed without a valid principal, or build execution initiated by 'guest'/'anonymous' identities. Cross-reference with outbound network connections.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation via Linux traffic-control race condition
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Linux Traffic-Control Race Into Root Exploit' — core detection for unprivileged processes executing tc commands followed by root-level process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor unprivileged processes invoking traffic control (tc) utilities with repeated or concurrent syscalls (Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use pattern). Alert on child processes spawned with uid=0 or setuid transitions immediately following tc operations without sudo/su intermediation.

suggestion.title: Race condition exploitation via kernel subsystem access patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes 'race condition' in tc subsystem; pipeline missed detection for rapid concurrent access to kernel structures indicative of TOCTOU exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid, time-clustered operations on network configuration subsystems (/proc/net/tc, netlink sockets) from single process. Correlate with subsequent setuid/setgid syscalls or mmap+mprotect sequences suggesting kernel exploit execution.

suggestion.title: Unprivileged to root privilege escalation without elevation primitives
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome is 'Root Exploit' but pipeline generated no elevation detection; missing correlation of uid transition without visible sudo/runas/setuid calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes achieving uid=0 without sudo, su, runas, or setuid-binary invocation. Cross-check for kernel module loading, /dev access, or memory-mapped device file operations preceding elevation as exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: AI-generated exploit code deployment and execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title highlights 'AI Helped Develop' exploit, suggesting LLM-generated or synthesized payload artifacts; no detection UC for automated exploit generation signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify exploit artifacts exhibiting characteristics of code generation (redundant symbols, synthetic naming patterns, unoptimized control flow). Monitor for GitHub/Pastebin downloads, GitHub Copilot/ChatGPT access patterns preceding exploit staging.

suggestion.title: DLL Search-Order Hijacking: SspiCli.dll Targeting AppVShNotify.exe
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'The implant masquerades as SspiCli.dll and appears to be designed for DLL search-order hijacking, targeting a legitimate AppVShNotify.exe binary.' This is the core execution technique and a primary detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SspiCli.dll created or modified in System32 or adjacent directories, or loaded by AppVShNotify.exe. Alert on AppVShNotify.exe execution with anomalous child processes or network connections that follow DLL load sequence. Check for SspiCli.dll in user-writable paths preceding legitimate binary execution.

suggestion.title: Recruitment-Themed Spear Phishing with Lookalike Hiring Portals
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'recruitment-themed content impersonating trusted brands and hiring platforms, as well as lookalike videoconferencing pages that redirected victims to malicious archives.' Captures the initial access vector targeting aerospace and aviation sectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with recruitment-related keywords ('hiring,' 'career,' 'interview,' 'LinkedIn-like domains') sent to aerospace/aviation/defense sector users. Flag URL redirects from lookalike hiring portals to file-sharing services (mega.nz, mediafire, etc.). Alert on users who opened recruitment lures then downloaded archives.

suggestion.title: WebSocket Tunneling via ArcBridge and BridgeHead
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies two custom tools: 'two custom WebSocket-based tunnelers, ArcBridge and BridgeHead, for covert network access and operator-controlled tunneling.' These are post-exploitation C2 mechanisms and direct detection targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WebSocket protocol (RFC 6455) over non-standard ports or HTTP/HTTPS from endpoints not typically initiating WebSocket connections. Flag traffic with WebSocket upgrade headers paired with process execution from SspiCli.dll-hijacked AppVShNotify.exe or NightLedger process. Correlate with suspicious proxy CONNECT requests to external infrastructure.

suggestion.title: NightLedger Backdoor Capabilities: Process Discovery and Screenshot Capture
suggestion.rationale: Article states NightLedger performs 'reconnaissance, command execution, file operations, process discovery, and screenshot capture.' Process discovery and screenshotting are observable collection activities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for tasklist.exe, Get-Process, or wmi query execution from child processes of AppVShNotify or SspiCli.dll context. Detect image capture binaries (mspaint.exe, snippingtool.exe) spawned without user initiation. Alert on rapid enumeration of running processes followed by file access to temp directories containing image data.

suggestion.title: BridgeHead Post-Exploitation Deployment in Egypt and Pakistan Aerospace Targets
suggestion.rationale: Article documents: 'we saw BridgeHead being deployed during post-exploitation activities in victim environments in Egypt and at a Pakistan-based aerospace and aviation organization.' Captures the deployment pattern and high-value target profile.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In Egypt and Pakistan regions, prioritize alerting on any WebSocket tunnel process creation or network initialization by previously unknown executables in aerospace/defense networks. Correlate process creation (BridgeHead) with lateral movement patterns from initial compromised host. Detect persistence mechanisms (Registry run keys, scheduled tasks) used to maintain BridgeHead execution across reboots.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Malware Deployment: Malicious Archives from File-Sharing Services
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'lookalike videoconferencing pages that redirected victims to malicious archives hosted on third-party file-sharing services.' Captures the second-stage delivery mechanism distinct from the phishing email itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file-sharing service downloads (mega.nz, mediafire, dropbox, etc.) triggered by recruitment-themed redirects. Detect extraction and immediate execution of archives in user temp directories. Flag process spawning from newly-extracted archives with network connectivity in the first few seconds.

suggestion.title: VeloCloud Orchestrator Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Command Injection Flaw' but pipeline generated zero detection use cases. Command injection is a runtime execution technique requiring behavioral detection on the orchestrator itself and ingress network monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VeloCloud Orchestrator service processes (velocloud.exe, orchestrator processes) for spawning child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) with encoded or obfuscated arguments. Correlate with HTTP POST requests to known VeloCloud API endpoints containing shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, $, backticks) in request body or query string parameters.

suggestion.title: VeloCloud Orchestrator Web Interface Authentication Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of public-facing web interfaces requires initial access; pipeline did not detect T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) as primary attack vector or generate authentication monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed authentication attempts to VeloCloud Orchestrator web console followed by successful authentication from same source within short timeframe. Monitor for HTTP 4xx/5xx error patterns (400, 403, 500) on VeloCloud endpoints preceding successful exploitation (HTTP 200 with command execution).

suggestion.title: VeloCloud Orchestrator Unpatched Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes vulnerability in 'Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator'; pipeline extracted zero product version indicators or patch-state telemetry despite this being critical for asset inventory and risk posture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate software inventory (Windows/Linux registry, installed packages, /usr/bin symlinks) for Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator presence and extract version strings. Cross-reference against CVE vulnerability database for confirmed command-injection flaws and alert on unpatched versions in production environment.

suggestion.title: VeloCloud Orchestrator Service Lateral Movement Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Command injection on a centralized orchestrator (network controller) is high-value for lateral movement to managed edge devices. Pipeline generated no use case for detecting command propagation from orchestrator to SD-WAN endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections from compromised VeloCloud Orchestrator service to managed edge appliances (typical: ports 443, 2706). Detect anomalous SSH/HTTPS sessions from orchestrator to edge devices with command execution indicators (processes spawned on remote devices, file write operations to config paths).

suggestion.title: VeloCloud Orchestrator Configuration Extraction or Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Command injection on orchestrator allows attacker to access WAN policy, encryption keys, and device configurations. Pipeline did not generate collection/exfiltration detection patterns despite impact on data-sensitive network control plane.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious file access or bulk read operations against VeloCloud configuration directories (typically /opt/VeloCloud/config, /var/lib/VeloCloud, registry paths on Windows). Detect data exfiltration patterns (large HTTPS POST to external IP, compressed archive creation followed by SMB/FTP egress) originating from VeloCloud service context.

suggestion.title: VeloCloud Orchestrator API Request Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Command injection via web API requires malformed or injection-crafted API payloads. Pipeline generated no hypothesis for monitoring VeloCloud REST/SOAP API call patterns for injection indicators despite being the direct exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP POST/PUT requests to VeloCloud Orchestrator API endpoints (e.g., /api/*, /configuration/*) for shell metacharacters, common injection payloads (backticks, $(), IFS bypass, Unicode encoding), and parameter tampering. Flag requests with abnormally high entropy in parameters or Content-Length mismatches indicative of obfuscation.

suggestion.title: Internet-Facing Fortinet FortiOS Device Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status requires asset exposure baseline; article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated attacker' access pattern, implying internet-facing deployment risk. No use case generated despite template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify and enumerate Fortinet FortiOS appliances accessible from untrusted networks via vulnerability scanner, shodan queries, and passive DNS. Correlate discovered assets against patching workflows and last-update timestamps; priority for any still running pre-patch versions.

suggestion.title: Anomalous HTTP Requests to FortiOS Admin Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly calls out 'crafted HTTP requests' as attack vector; pipeline missed entire exploitation detection layer targeting request pattern anomalies on known-vulnerable IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal HTTP/HTTPS traffic to FortiOS admin consoles (port 443, 10000, etc). Alert on requests with unusual URI paths, header combinations, or payloads; correlate spikes from external IPs with high entropy request bodies or repeated 40x/50x response codes.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Creation & Persistence Bypass Evidence
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically describes 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism'; filesystem monitoring for suspicious symlink creation on compromised FortiOS systems entirely absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for unexpected symbolic link creation in web-accessible directories, boot paths, or library locations. Flag links pointing to system files, configuration storage, or authentication bypass mechanisms. Correlate with process execution or failed patch-validation attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Sensitive Data Access via FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly exposes 'sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'; pipeline produced no data-exfiltration detection despite clear impact statement. No hunt for bulk config exports, certificate theft, or log access by unauthenticated sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal sensitive-data access patterns on FortiOS (config exports by admins during maintenance windows, certificate queries, log reads). Alert on deviations: bulk file reads of /etc, system key stores, configuration backups initiated from non-admin sessions or during off-hours/weekends.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass & Unauthenticated Admin Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'remote unauthenticated attacker' capability as core attack surface; no detection use case for auth bypass evidence or privilege-escalation anomalies unique to this CVE's exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS authentication logs for successful admin-level access without corresponding login records, session tokens appearing without auth negotiation, or HTTP requests bearing valid session cookies not present in auth logs. Flag rapid auth-bypass patterns (failed logins followed by privileged actions).

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scan: CVE-2025-68686 Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status + article explicitly recommends 'match against your vulnerability scanner.' Active exploitation in the wild requires rapid asset identification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2025-68686 flags. Cross-reference FortiOS inventory with patch status. Prioritize externally accessible instances; flag all vulnerable systems as critical given federal remediation deadline 2026-08-10.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Internet-Facing FortiOS Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated attacker' via 'crafted HTTP requests'—presupposes management web interface accessible from internet. Matches template guidance referenced in article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify FortiOS management interfaces exposed to untrusted networks (ports 80, 443, 8080, 10000+). Alert on externally accessible FortiOS running versions vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686.

suggestion.title: Suspicious HTTP Patterns to FortiOS Admin Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation pathway is explicitly 'via crafted HTTP requests'—detection must target anomalous HTTP patterns attempting the bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS to FortiOS admin interfaces for abnormal patterns: non-standard request methods, oversized/encoded payloads, malformed headers, or rapid request bursts. Flag deviations from baseline legitimate admin traffic.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Access Post-Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Post-bypass, attacker exfiltrates system data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual access to sensitive FortiOS artifacts: system configuration, API keys, VPN settings, customer records. Flag access patterns inconsistent with normal admin workflows or from unexpected source IPs/users.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Symlink Creation in FortiOS Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' as the original payload before vendor patch. Symlink creation signals prior compromise and persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for symlink creation in system directories (/bin, /lib, /etc, /opt/fortinet). Alert on symlinks pointing outside parent directory or to sensitive locations; compare against whitelist of legitimate symlinks.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance: CVE-2025-68686 Remediation Deadline Tracking
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV mandates federal agency remediation by 2026-08-10. Compliance hunts track which assets remain unpatched and enforce deadline enforcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Continuous query of all FortiOS inventory. Compare version/patch status to Fortinet advisory. Alert on any unpatched device; track remediation progress against federal deadline.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Crafted HTTP Request to Bypass Symbolic Link Patch
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the attack: 'crafted HTTP requests' that bypass the symbolic link patch mechanism. This is a specific, detectable exploitation vector that should have generated a use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS admin interface logs for HTTP requests with anomalous structure, encoding, or parameter combinations targeting endpoints known to interact with symbolic link handling. Unauthenticated requests followed by successful state changes (config modification, user creation, data export) should trigger alerts.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' as the core post-compromise technique. Filesystem-level changes are observable even if the HTTP bypass succeeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on symlink creation or modification in FortiOS system directories (/etc, /var/log, /usr/local) especially when preceded by failed authentication attempts or HTTP anomalies. Correlate symlink changes with process execution from FortiOS daemons accessing non-standard paths.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated FortiOS Administrative Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker is 'remote unauthenticated' and can 'bypass' authentication via crafted requests. Successful admin operations without credentials are definitionally anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any configuration change, credential creation, or backup operation in FortiOS admin logs where the source authentication session is null, blank, or does not appear in authentication logs. Any admin-level action from untrusted source should trigger SOC escalation.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Sensitive Information Exfiltration from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' — then leverages this CVE to expose sensitive info. Detection must cover post-compromise data access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual FortiOS daemon process access to credential stores, encryption keys, or configuration files (typically /etc/fortimgmt.conf, /etc/passwd, /var/run/certs). Baseline normal access and alert on deviations, especially during or shortly after indicators of system compromise.

suggestion.title: Unpatched FortiOS Version Inventory Audit
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal remediation deadline (2026-08-10). Standard asset exposure hunt referenced in article template. Pipeline should recommend immediate inventory scan against known-vulnerable versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results and asset inventory for all FortiOS instances running versions vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686. Fortinet will publish patched versions; any unpatched instance should be flagged for emergency patching given CISA KEV status and active exploitation.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article states this CVE is in CISA KEV (actively exploited in the wild). Substitute into standard asset-exposure hunt template per article guidance. Primary detection is vulnerability scanner match for CVE-2025-68686.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Fortinet FortiOS instances by version string, cross-check against vulnerable versions for CVE-2025-68686. Federal remediation deadline is 2026-08-10; flag any unpatched instances. Use WMI, SNMP, or vendor-specific APIs to enumerate FortiOS deployments.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistency Bypass via HTTP Requests

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for symlink creation/modification in FortiOS system paths (e.g., /etc/rc.d, /etc/init.d, cron.d). Baseline legitimate symlinks and alert on post-compromise anomalies. Cross-correlate with filesystem access logs and HTTP request timing.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism...via crafted HTTP requests.' No detection for malformed/anomalous HTTP payloads targeting patched endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal HTTP patterns to FortiOS endpoints pre-patch deployment. Post-patch, alert on requests with unusual encoding, oversized parameters, malformed headers, or double-encoding targeting symlink-related functions. Correlate with 403/bypass error responses.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Sensitive Information Access
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability classified as 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor' but no collection/exfiltration detection generated. Article implies data access after filesystem compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After filesystem-level compromise detected, alert on anomalous access to FortiOS config files, certificate stores, credential vaults. Monitor egress for bulk data transfer or connections to external IPs from compromised FortiOS instances.

suggestion.title: Patch Deployment Timeline Violation Post Due-Date
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due date 2026-08-10. No temporal hunt for systems remaining unpatched beyond deadline, when exploitation risk escalates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any FortiOS system still vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686 after 2026-08-10. Correlate patch-deployment logs with asset inventory. Alert on unpatched systems with internet exposure or access from untrusted networks post-deadline.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Reversion to Malicious Commit
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker deleting original tags and re-pointing release tags to orphaned malicious commit: 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit.' Pipeline missed this defense-evasion pattern entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub repository tag modifications on critical/popular Actions. Alert when tags are moved to commits not on main/release branches, especially if commit shas differ from prior tag points. Cross-correlate with repo write-access logs to identify suspicious privilege use.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit Creation in Public GitHub Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker created orphaned commits to obfuscate the attack: 'Having the attack commit orphaned from any branches, including the main branch These factors added a bit of obfuscation to hide the attack.' Pipeline captured no defense-evasion detection for this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits reachable via commit SHA but not reachable from any branch HEAD in repositories with ≥1k stars or ≥100 watchers. Flag if commit authored by account with write permissions but commit never merged to main or released via tag.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Secrets Exposed in Plaintext Logs
suggestion.rationale: Core attack outcome: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit that caused encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs.' Pipeline generated zero detection for this high-impact credential exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions run logs (especially public repos) for patterns matching GitHub secret format (starts with gh[opsu]_ prefix). Cross-correlate with commits that modify Actions workflow YAML or step output handling. Alert if plaintext secrets detected within 24 hours of unexpected repository code changes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious External Network Calls from GitHub Actions Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attack relied on external network calls that enabled discovery: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' Zero network-based detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from GitHub Actions runners to non-canonical CI/CD infrastructure domains. Baseline expected artifact repositories per org, alert on calls to unfamiliar or single-use domains, especially with large payload downloads or POST exfiltration patterns.

suggestion.title: Write-Access Abuse on High-Profile GitHub Actions Repository
suggestion.rationale: Root cause: attacker exploited write privileges on repo with 23k downstream dependents. Article notes: 'the bottom line is that a malicious actor had write access to a repo that 23,000 other repos relied on.' Pipeline never surfaced the account-compromise or privilege-abuse angle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For repositories tagged as GitHub Actions / widely-used packages, alert on new or unusual user push events, especially commits that introduce external network calls, modify action.yml entry-points, or access repository secrets environment variables. Require secondary approval for deployments to tags on high-impact repos.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit Reachability via Tag or Release Asset
suggestion.rationale: Attacker exploited GitHub's permissiveness: orphaned commits remain accessible via SHA and can be re-tagged. Article demonstrates: 'You can still navigate to that commit, even though it is no longer associated with any existing branch.' Detection gap on persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For public repositories, monitor API calls resolving commits to tag/branch associations. Flag cases where a release tag points to a commit SHA with no branch ancestry or where branch deletion is followed within 24h by tag creation pointing to previously-branched commit SHA.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt (Windmill)
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes 'arbitrary server files' access without auth. Pipeline missed mapping this to path traversal patterns. Phrase: 'Read Arbitrary Server Files Without Authentication' implies directory traversal or path-based exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request logs for Windmill endpoints receiving path traversal payloads ('../', '..\', '%2e%2e', Unicode equivalents) in URI or query parameters. Alert on sequences combining directory-traversal syntax with file-read operations (e.g., /api/read?path=../../../etc/passwd).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated File Access to Windmill APIs
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Without Authentication.' Pipeline failed to surface detection for unauthenticated calls to protected endpoints. Core attack prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to known Windmill file-read or resource-access endpoints (e.g., /api/scripts/*, /api/resources/*) that lack valid authentication tokens, API keys, or session cookies. Correlate with HTTP 200 or 206 responses indicating successful unauthorized access.

suggestion.title: Bulk or Sequential File Read Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Arbitrary file-read vulnerabilities are typically weaponized through enumeration: attacker probes /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, config files, secrets. Pipeline missed collection-phase detection. Phrase: 'arbitrary server files' implies attacker can request unknown/multiple files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of HTTP requests from a single source to Windmill file endpoints requesting progressively sensitive paths (e.g., requests for /api/files?path=config.yaml, then secrets.json, then .env, all within minutes). Flag if response sizes or HTTP 200 counts exceed baseline for anonymous/untrusted users.

suggestion.title: Windmill Version Disclosure or CVE Probing
suggestion.rationale: No IOCs extracted; pipeline should have identified version-specific indicators or CVE reference if present. Attackers typically confirm vulnerability via version header or endpoint response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP responses from Windmill services for version disclosure in Server headers (e.g., 'Windmill/1.x.x'). Alert if versions match known-vulnerable ranges. Also detect probing for CVE-specific endpoints (e.g., requests to deprecated or previously-vulnerable API paths).

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of System Configuration or Credentials via File Read
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows reading arbitrary files without auth; implies access to /etc/passwd, config files with embedded credentials, .env, or secrets. Pipeline had zero impact/exfiltration mapping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Windmill file-read requests targeting known secret locations (e.g., paths containing 'secret', 'config', 'password', 'api_key', '.env', '/etc/') with outbound DNS or HTTP exfiltration. Alert if file contents are echoed in HTTP response bodies or sent to external hosts.

suggestion.title: Windmill Service Compromise via Unauthenticated API Abuse
suggestion.rationale: If arbitrary file read allows access to workflow definitions, scripts, or API keys, attacker can pivot to service manipulation or lateral movement. Pipeline missed this secondary impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After unauthenticated file reads, detect modifications to Windmill workflows, job definitions, or stored scripts without corresponding authenticated API calls. Alert on creation of new workflows or jobs immediately following high-volume unauthorized file access from the same source IP.
