suggestion.title: Obfuscated JavaScript Execution from Node Modules Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'Obfuscated Remote Access Trojan' — detection should target obfuscated code patterns within node_modules to catch similar payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Node.js executing JavaScript files from node_modules containing characteristics of obfuscated code (high entropy strings, excessive bracket nesting, variable names as hex/unicode escapes, or known deobfuscation tool usage). Correlate with module load events from suspicious packages.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing from npm Package Runtime Process
suggestion.rationale: RAT capability implies remote command and control; article lacks specifics but detection should cover C2 patterns from Node.js child processes spawned by npm module initialization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect persistent outbound connections (TCP/HTTPS) initiated by Node.js processes loading from compromised packages, with regularity suggesting heartbeat or command polling. Look for DNS queries to newly-registered domains (< 7 days old) or IPs with no legitimate npm CDN association.

suggestion.title: Process Hollowing or Code Injection from npm Module
suggestion.rationale: RAT functionality often includes process injection to maintain persistence and evade detection; no injection techniques were mapped despite RAT classification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for parent-child process relationships where Node.js spawns unexpected child processes (especially system utilities like powershell.exe, cmd.exe, or svchost.exe) with code injection indicators (VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory API calls or equivalent). Flag mismatches between module declared dependencies and spawned processes.

suggestion.title: npm Package Metadata Anomalies and Rapid Version Publishing
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often rely on typosquatting or hijacking existing packages; no behavioral detection on package repository patterns was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag packages with abrupt ownership changes, unusual version bumps without changelog, or publish patterns deviating from historical cadence. Correlate compromised package publish timestamp against known breach disclosure dates to identify compromise window.

suggestion.title: New authenticated session from IP mismatch post-redirect injection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'IdP to redirect the victim's authorization code to an attacker' — attacker now possesses valid auth code and can initiate authenticated sessions. Pipeline missed detection of new successful login for victim user from previously-unseen IP within 1h of failed redirect attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication for user U from IP not in 90-day baseline, within 1 hour of ErrorCode=50011 (redirect mismatch) logged for same user. Increase severity if IP is anonymized, foreign geography, or accesses high-privilege resources within 30min.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated OIDC/SAML endpoint fuzzing with multiple Host header values
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker' — initial reconnaissance/injection attempts target Poweradmin auth endpoints. Pipeline missed detection combining: repeated unauthenticated requests to */oidc/*, */saml/*, */logout* from single IP + multiple distinct Host header values in logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag 3+ unauthenticated requests to Poweradmin auth endpoints (*/oidc/*, */saml/*, */logout*) from single source IP within 10min window, with 2+ distinct Host header values present. Correlate with 301/302 redirect responses to confirm injection attempt.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation / sensitive app access immediately post-token theft
suggestion.rationale: Article implies attacker gains victim's credential via stolen token. Compromise detection post-theft requires detecting victim's account used for high-risk operations (Graph API, SharePoint, Teams, Azure AD Graph) from anomalous IP within narrow token-lifetime window (~1h).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect user resource access to high-value targets (msgraph.microsoft.com, SharePoint, Exchange, AAD Graph) from IP cluster not in user's 90-day baseline within 30min of correlated signals (failed redirect + new anomalous session). Flag especially: consent grants, service principal creation, forwarding rules, app registration.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated IPMI Hash Extraction Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'Disclose IPMI Password Hashes Before Login.' Hash material is retrievable without authentication via RAKP phase 2 capture or similar IPMI protocol mechanics, enabling offline cracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IPMI service port 623 for unauthenticated RAKP or authentication requests that return hash material. Detect IPMI protocol handshakes that leak credential hashes (bcrypt, MD5, or salted formats) in response frames. Correlate with external source IPs to identify reconnaissance of exposed BMCs.

suggestion.title: Port 623 IPMI Exposure and Scanning Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes '24,650 Internet-Exposed BMCs'—massive surface of IPMI port 623 open to public internet. Detection should identify both unintended exposure and active reconnaissance of IPMI services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound connections to port 623 from public/untrusted IP ranges. Monitor for scanning patterns (e.g., rapid sequential IPMI probes to multiple targets). Detect IPMI service banners or responses to external queries. Correlate exposure with CMDBs to flag unexpected internet-facing BMCs.

suggestion.title: IPMI Default/Weak Credential Login Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Exposed BMCs commonly retain default credentials (ADMIN, IPMI, 12345, etc.). Article's volume (24K+) implies many are unpatched or misconfigured with predictable passwords.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IPMI services for successful login attempts using known default account names or weak passwords. Alert on any successful IPMI auth without prior failed attempts, suggesting pre-known credentials. Track login anomalies from unexpected geolocations or times.

suggestion.title: IPMI Lateral Movement via Serial-Over-LAN (SOL)
suggestion.rationale: Once credentials obtained via hash cracking, attackers pivot through IPMI to access host consoles, reboot systems, or modify firmware. IPMI provides direct BMC command and SOL access to target servers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect IPMI web console or SOL session initiations from external IPs. Monitor for IPMI commands (power cycle, reset, firmware update) issued in unusual sequences or outside change windows. Correlate IPMI login with host-level anomalies (unexpected reboot, privilege escalation, persistent backdoor installation).

suggestion.title: Bulk IPMI Service Enumeration and Credential Testing
suggestion.rationale: Availability of hash material and volume of targets enables large-scale attack orchestration. Attackers will enumerate capabilities and test credentials across the 24K+ exposed BMCs systematically.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid-fire IPMI enumeration queries (Get Channel Info, Get Session Challenge) from single or few sources targeting multiple BMCs. Alert on distributed credential testing patterns (N failed IPMI logins across M targets, followed by successes). Identify tooling signatures (e.g., metasploit IPMI modules, custom scanners).

suggestion.title: IPMI Firmware/Configuration Tampering Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Once BMC compromised via IPMI credentials, attacker can modify firmware, disable security features, install rootkits, or enable persistence mechanisms at the hardware management level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IPMI for firmware upload or update commands issued outside maintenance windows. Detect BMC configuration changes (e.g., disabling ACPI power button, modifying alert settings, enabling debug modes). Alert on modifications to IPMI user accounts or access control lists. Track firmware hash changes on production BMCs.

suggestion.title: snap-confine privilege escalation via flaw exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states flaw 'could give local users root' and is marked critical severity. Pipeline did not generate any privilege-escalation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for snap-confine binary execution with privilege-level transitions (UID 0 spawned from non-root parent, or execve syscalls changing effective UID/GID during snap operation). Flag if snap-confine or snap-spawned child processes obtain root credentials without sudo/auth entry. Correlate with snap policy violations in audit logs.

suggestion.title: Unexpected root shell spawning from snap context
suggestion.rationale: Local user exploiting snap-confine flaw to gain root access would manifest as shell spawning under root after snap process invocation. Article describes impact as 'root on default desktop installs.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when /bin/bash, /bin/sh, or other shell spawns with PPID chain originating from snap-confine or snap.*, and the process UID is 0 but parent UID is non-zero. Baseline normal snap execution and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: snap-confine binary modification or integrity breach
suggestion.rationale: LPE via snap-confine likely involves either exploiting a code path or tampering with binary/config. Article implies default installs are vulnerable—suggests the flaw is in snap-confine codebase itself, not misconfig.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for changes to snap-confine binary (/usr/lib/snapd/snap-confine), snap policy files, or snap.conf. Detect file-write events from non-privileged users targeting these paths. Compare file hashes against known-good versions for affected Ubuntu releases.

suggestion.title: Snap operation audit-log tampering or suppression
suggestion.rationale: If snap-confine flaw allows privilege escalation, attacker may disable/clear audit logs post-exploitation to cover tracks. Article does not mention this, but common post-exploitation pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on auditctl rule deletions or audit log writes from processes spawned by snap operations. Monitor for gaps in auditd event stream coinciding with snap-confine invocation. Flag if audit daemon is restarted after snap execution.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Anomalous HTTP Request Pattern to Bypass Patched Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism, via crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this clear attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS-targeted HTTP requests originating from unauthenticated sources (no successful auth events in preceding 5 minutes). Correlate request patterns against CVE-2025-68686 PoC signatures. Flag requests containing suspicious query parameters, path traversal attempts, or binary payloads sent to known vulnerable endpoints (likely /api/v2/ paths on FortiOS).

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Creation for Persistence on Compromised FortiOS Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'—establishes filesystem-level persistence technique requiring detection but pipeline ignored entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect symbolic link creation attempts targeting FortiOS configuration directories (/etc/fortiosconfig/, system paths). Alert on `ln -s` or filesystem syscalls creating symlinks to sensitive config files, particularly from non-standard process parents. Correlate timing with prior exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Access to FortiOS Sensitive Configuration Files via Exposed Filesystem Permissions
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' requires detection of unauthorized config/credential file access—pipeline produced zero data-access detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor access to FortiOS sensitive paths: /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /root/.ssh, /etc/fortiosconfig/*, VPN configuration stores. Establish baseline of legitimate admin access and alert on after-hours, weekend, or anomalous user/service account reads. Cross-reference with failed authentication events or suspicious HTTP requests from same source.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scanner and Asset Inventory Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CISA KEV status ('currently being exploited') and urges 'one quick check across your fleet—patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline should prioritize asset discovery for this specific CVE but generated no inventory/scan-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results and CMDB for all Fortinet FortiOS instances. Filter by version/patch status against CVE-2025-68686 vulnerability timeline. Compare reported patched status against observed network behavior (unpatched systems may exhibit exploitation indicators). Generate priority list flagged for manual verification given federal remediation deadline 2026-08-10.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Attack Pattern: Initial Compromise → Symlink Persistence → HTTP Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes kill-chain: 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' followed by bypass via crafted HTTP requests. Pipeline's empty kill-chain reconstruction missed this staged attack—should detect pattern across three distinct behaviors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Construct multi-event correlation across 24-hour window: (1) Exploitation indicators targeting FortiOS public-facing service; (2) Filesystem activity creating symlinks or modifying persistence mechanisms post-exploitation; (3) Subsequent anomalous HTTP requests from same source or internal pivot attempting to bypass patched vulnerability. Alert if all three phases observed in sequence.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Unauthenticated Access Attempts and Authentication Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated attacker' can exploit—implies detection should flag repeated unauthenticated access or successful auth bypass patterns. Pipeline generated no authentication-related use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS access logs for repeated failed authentication attempts followed by successful connection without credentials (HTTP 200/302 after 401/403 responses). Detect requests that bypass expected login flow via malformed session tokens, path traversal, or HTTP header manipulation targeting CVE-2025-68686 endpoints.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Internet-Facing Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status confirms active exploitation in the wild. Article establishes threat requires internet-facing FortiOS exposure: 'remote unauthenticated attacker' implies public-facing systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for Fortinet FortiOS instances with public IPs or exposed HTTPS management interfaces. Cross-reference asset inventory with external scanning data (Shodan, Censys). Prioritize audit of unpatched instances pending 2026-08-10 federal remediation deadline.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistency Bypass via Crafted HTTP
suggestion.rationale: Core exploitation: 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism...via crafted HTTP requests.' Article explicitly names the bypass technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS HTTP access logs for path traversal patterns, symbolic link constructs (/proc/*, ../*, absolute paths), or requests targeting filesystem-level resources after authentication. Correlate with prior compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability core: 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' After patch bypass, attackers access credentials, certificates, licenses, or configs stored on FortiOS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal file access patterns on FortiOS. Alert on access to sensitive resource paths (certificate stores, license files, configuration backups, admin logs) by unexpected processes or outside business hours.

suggestion.title: Configuration or Credential Exfiltration from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: After exposure, attackers exfiltrate collected data. Article's 'sensitive information' likely includes certificates, API keys, network configs valuable for lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound FortiOS traffic for large data transfers, config backups sent over HTTP/FTP to non-Fortinet IPs, or unusually structured POST requests encoding sensitive data to external domains.

suggestion.title: Pre-Stage Compromise: Earlier Fortinet CVE Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article requirement: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Detect the initial foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate FortiOS systems patched late for 2024–2025 CVEs with later CVE-2025-68686 activity. Cross-reference failed SSH logins, HTTP errors, or auth anomalies preceding suspected exploitation of this CVE on the same asset.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Symbolic Link Persistence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'; this is a forensic and behavioral detection gap for any FortiOS monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS systems for creation or modification of symbolic links in init.d, systemd, cron, or service-startup directories. Correlate with prior compromise indicators or unexpected process spawning from those directories.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Crafted HTTP Request Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attackers 'bypass the patch...via crafted HTTP requests'; no detection rule addresses anomalous HTTP patterns targeting post-compromise persistence on FortiOS systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on malformed, oversized, or out-of-spec HTTP requests to FortiOS management interfaces or service endpoints in systems where symlink persistence indicators have been detected. Look for header injection, encoding obfuscation, or non-standard methods.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerable Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal patch due-date 2026-08-10; pipeline failed to generate any asset-discovery or patch-compliance use case despite this being a live, exploited CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Conduct systematic discovery of FortiOS instances and version baseline. Flag any systems running versions vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686 and track remediation progress against federal due-date (2026-08-10).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Access to Sensitive FortiOS Directories
suggestion.rationale: CVE title is 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor'; post-compromise, attackers would exfiltrate or access sensitive configs, credentials, or audit logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual file read/access patterns on sensitive paths: /etc/passwd equivalents, FortiOS credential stores, admin config files, and audit logs. Alert when accessed by processes not normally requiring those permissions, especially post-symlink-persistence setup.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Asset Exposure via Vulnerability Scanner
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies this as a CISA KEV entry and requires 'one quick check across your fleet.' No scanner IOC or asset-hunt UC was generated despite template mentioning 'Standard asset-exposure hunt.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset inventories for FortiOS systems flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686. Correlate patch dates against federal due date 2026-08-10 to identify unpatched assets. Baseline: zero unpatched instances of FortiOS in critical/DMZ segments.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Creation in FortiOS Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'bypass[es] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' This is an explicit persistence technique that requires filesystem monitoring but went undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem activity (via audit logs or EDR if installed) for symlink creation or modification in standard FortiOS config/binary directories. Flag unexpected symlinks pointing to sensitive files or external mounts. Alert on any symlink changes within 24 hours of FortiOS log restart/patch events.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests to FortiOS Patch-Bypass Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation uses 'crafted HTTP requests' to bypass the symlink patch. This is an active exploitation signature that needs HTTP-layer detection but was omitted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS HTTP access logs and web application firewall alerts for unusual request patterns targeting known FortiOS admin endpoints or API paths post-patch dates. Look for requests with malformed headers, path traversal sequences, or uncommon User-Agents targeting patch-vulnerable code paths. Flag if originating from internal or post-compromise IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Filesystem Access by Unprivileged FortiOS Processes Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attacker 'need[s] to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Detection of abnormal filesystem access patterns is a critical post-compromise indicator that was not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of which FortiOS processes access which filesystem paths under normal operation. Alert on deviations: unexpected process spawning with elevated file access, new processes accessing /etc, /var/log, or backup directories, or processes writing to directories normally read-only. Correlate with failed patch deployment or FortiOS service crashes.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Access Post-FortiOS Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Exposure of Sensitive Information' and notes this is the impact of successful exploitation. No data-access logging or exfiltration detection use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS configuration exports, backup downloads, or bulk file reads targeting config storage (/etc/config, /data) or credential stores. Flag unexpected data egress from FortiOS (DNS queries to uncommon domains, unusual egress volume, encrypted tunnels). Cross-reference with successful exploitation indicators (symlink creation + crafted HTTP activity).

suggestion.title: FortiOS Unpatched Inventory Report with Federal Compliance Check
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due date 2026-08-10 and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' No compliance tracking or due-date-aware inventory use case was generated despite explicit federal mandate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate weekly report of all FortiOS instances, patch version, and patch date. Flag any unpatched systems red if current_date > 2026-08-10. Include in monthly SOC dashboard and CyberOps/Risk burn-down. Alert immediately if any unpatched FortiOS appears in DMZ, public-facing, or federal-connected network segments.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly prescribes 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and mandates federal patch due 2026-08-10. CISA KEV only lists actively exploited CVEs; scan misses indicate patch lag risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search endpoint inventory for Fortinet FortiOS instances reporting CVE-2025-68686 presence. Treat unpatched systems as critical assets under active exploitation risk, even if local scanners report false-negatives due to patch timing lag.

suggestion.title: Anomalous HTTP Requests Post-Filesystem Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker sends 'crafted HTTP requests' after achieving 'filesystem level' compromise to bypass symbolic link persistency patch. This HTTP phase is distinct post-exploitation behavior warranting direct detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After confirming FortiOS filesystem compromise, hunt HTTP request logs for patterns deviating from baseline traffic—particularly requests with unusual path traversal, file handle manipulation, or serialized payloads that might trigger symlink resolution or patch bypass logic.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Creation for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' — this implies attackers create symlinks to maintain access. Detection of symlink abuse is prerequisite to understanding the persistence vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS for unauthorized symbolic link creation in system directories, particularly those related to auto-start, web handlers, or configuration paths. Baseline normal symlinks; flag additions outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Filesystem Access via Unauthenticated Vector (Pre-HTTP Exploit)
suggestion.rationale: Article requires attacker to 'have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' before HTTP bypass is possible. Detecting this prerequisite compromise phase is critical for early kill-chain interruption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline FortiOS process behavior and authorized file modifications. Alert on unexpected process spawning, file-write activity in restricted directories, or command-line execution outside normal admin workflows—these precede the HTTP bypass attempt.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'remote unauthenticated attacker' exploitation via 'crafted HTTP requests,' but no vulnerability detection use case was generated despite template system references asset-exposure hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner hits for CVE-2025-68686 on FortiOS systems. Prioritize public-facing instances. Cross-reference patch dates against federal deadline 2026-08-10.

suggestion.title: Anomalous HTTP Requests to Exposed FortiOS Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'crafted HTTP requests' against 'public-facing application' as the exploitation mechanism, establishing a behavioral detection gap not addressed by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic to FortiOS management interfaces for malformed payloads, unusual parameter encoding, or suspicious header patterns indicative of crafted exploitation requests.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Post-Exploit Symlink Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases,' indicating a distinct persistence phase after initial application compromise. Pipeline missed the multi-stage attack decomposition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: FortiOS attackers establish persistence via symlinks post-compromise. Monitor system directories (/etc, /var/etc) for suspicious symlink creation/modification, especially correlated with prior exploit attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to FortiOS Credentials/Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome is 'exposure of sensitive information,' implying attackers access credential stores or administrative configuration post-compromise. Pipeline missed collection/disclosure phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor compromised FortiOS instances for non-standard access to credential storage, VPN configurations, or session data. Alert on bulk file reads from administrative stores by suspicious processes.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Compliance Enforcement (Federal Deadline)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly cites federal patch due-date 2026-08-10 and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer,' yet pipeline generated no deadline-driven compliance detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Daily report: identify FortiOS instances lacking CVE-2025-68686 patches. Flag non-compliant systems 7 days before federal deadline. Reconcile with asset inventory to ensure complete coverage.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Patch Status Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status mandates immediate patch detection. Article names CVE-2025-68686 explicitly; pipeline extracted zero IOCs despite this being the primary detection pivot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and vulnerability scans for Fortinet FortiOS instances below patched build version for CVE-2025-68686. Cross-correlate with firewall/WAF telemetry to identify publicly exposed instances lacking mitigation.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Creation in FortiOS System Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack involves 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' and 'filesystem level' access—directly indicates symlink abuse as the persistence/bypass vector the patch was designed to block.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on symlink creation or modification in FortiOS system configuration or autostart-equivalent directories via ln command or filesystem APIs. Baseline by privilege context and correlate with preceding unauthorized filesystem access.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Sensitive File Access Post-Filesystem Breach
suggestion.rationale: Article states impact is 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' following 'filesystem level' compromise—indicates data exfiltration hunt is required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor access to FortiOS credential stores, configuration files (system.conf, admin profiles), and authentication logs from unexpected processes. Flag reads followed by outbound network connections to non-RFC1918 addresses.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Patterns Against FortiOS Admin Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states exploitation occurs 'via crafted HTTP requests' in the context of patch bypass—indicates HTTP-layer attack detection gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP requests to FortiOS admin paths for malformed parameters, path traversal sequences (../, etc.), or header anomalies. Alert on patterns consistent with symlink-traversal bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation to Filesystem Access Post-Initial Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'—establishes a two-stage kill chain requiring detection of privilege escalation between compromise and symlink exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate initial exploitation indicators (CVE scans, HTTP anomalies) with subsequent process execution or file access from elevated contexts. Flag instances where non-admin process transitions to system-level filesystem access.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [...template...].' Pipeline failed to instantiate the template-substituted asset discovery use case for this CISA KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all FortiOS instances exposed to untrusted networks and cross-reference CVE-2025-68686 vulnerability scanner results. CISA KEV implies active exploitation; patch lag requires validation even on systems reporting patched status.

suggestion.title: Symlink Persistence Mechanism Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' — establishes persistence phase requiring filesystem monitoring for abnormal symlink creation in sensitive paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on symlink creation in /etc, /var, /proc, or startup directories on FortiOS hosts. Correlate symlink events with preceding exploitation attempts (failed auth followed by access anomalies) to detect post-compromise persistence setup.

suggestion.title: Patch Bypass via Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases, via crafted HTTP requests' — indicates structured exploitation payloads targeting patch mitigation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests with path traversal sequences (../, ..%2f, %2e%2e), unusual header encodings, or symlink-manipulation payloads targeting FortiOS admin paths. Alert on successful (HTTP 200) responses after multiple failed attempts.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exfiltration Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' — core impact requires data access and exfiltration detection following exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor compromised FortiOS hosts for unusual outbound connections post-exploit indicators. Track data volume to non-whitelisted IPs, especially targeting cloud storage or C2 indicators. Audit which sensitive resources (config, VPN logs, user credentials) were accessed before exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Remote Access to FortiOS Admin Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated attacker' capability — requires detection of unauthorized admin access attempts and successful bypasses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated failed authentication (HTTP 401/403) from external sources followed by successful access, or single-request exploitation indicating auth bypass. Alert on suspicious admin interface access patterns (unusual payload, encoding, or request structure).

suggestion.title: Symlink-Based Privilege Escalation Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Symlink persistence mechanism implies attackers leverage symbolic links for lateral movement or privilege escalation after establishing foothold 'at filesystem level'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate symlink creation on FortiOS with subsequent process execution under elevated privilege or service account context. Monitor for symlinks targeting setuid binaries, startup directories, or restricted resource paths that enable privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerable FortiOS Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs to asset-exposure hunt; CVE-2025-68686 is the detection anchor ('match against your vulnerability scanner'). Pipeline must flag FortiOS systems and substitute CVE into template queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for FortiOS systems flagged with CVE-2025-68686. Prioritize exposed / internet-facing instances. Cross-reference patch inventory against due date 2026-08-10.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests to Patched FortiOS (Post-Exploit Bypass)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch...via crafted HTTP requests.' Requires prior compromise but detection is POST-initial-access, implying forensic HTTP log review on already-breached FortiOS systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On compromised FortiOS systems, search HTTP access logs for request patterns that deviate from normal admin traffic post-patching. Look for encoding bypasses, path traversal, or unusual parameter values typical of CVE exploitation.

suggestion.title: Symlink Persistence Mechanism on FortiOS Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' Attacker leverages symlink to maintain foothold after initial compromise and before HTTP bypass. Filesystem artifacts must be hunted on suspected breach targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search endpoint logs for symlink creation events on FortiOS systems, particularly in system directories (/etc, /root, /var). Correlate creation timestamp with known exploitation windows or lateral movement alerts.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Exploit Chain: Prior CVE + CVE-2025-68686 Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.'
